I LOVE this shampoo and was very excited to have the opportunity to review this product for my unbiased opinion.

review_title: A great way to trim your beard!
review_text:
This is a great way to trim your beard. A definite step up from traditional trimmers. The magic in it is the vacuum that captures and stores trimmed beard and mustache hair instead of letting it fall into your sink to make a mess. You don't make your lady mad, and everyone is happy.

The trimmer itself fits comfortably in your hand. It has an detachable cord that allows the unit to be charged. It can operate on the cord or off it's batteries for cordless use. The trimmer is NOT submersible.

The attached guard can be adjusted to 9 length settings with a rotating selector. It can also be taken off for trimming necklines or other areas. There is also a separate smaller attachment that can be used for precision cuts.

The vacuum is power and made more powerful over earlier models through the use of the "Turbo" button that amps up the cutting power and vacuum power substantially. When you are done cutting your hairs are captured in a removable tray for disposal. There are still a few hairs that don't get sucked up but it a huge improvement over using trimmers without suction.

The only negatives are that the hair capture cup is a tad small. There is also a plastic piece that guides hair into the cup that makes neck and cheek-line trimming a little tricky until you get the hang of it.

Overall a great trimmer for those of us real men with beards. A must have!!

review_text:
I've been trying to get better about regularly going to a salon for a hair cut. For years I just went to Great Clips once a year. Basically, I'd go whenever I hated my hair so I'd have to chop inches off of split ends. But now I have a salon and a hair stylist I love so I'm trying to go every 3 or so months. My stylist recommended that I start using a hair diffuser whenever I dry my hair because I have naturally curly hair.

I don't use heat on my hair often but when I do, I've been attaching this to my hair dryer. I have the Infiniti Pro by Conair 1875 Watt Full Size Salon Performance AC Motor Styler/Hair Dryer (that I also bought from Amazon) and this fits on it perfectly. I read reviews that sometimes this hair diffuser doesn't work on all hair dryers because the diameter is smaller or larger than what this is compatible. But I measured the diameter of my hair dryer so I knew it would work. And I love how my hair reacts to being diffused. My curls just look marvelous. I almost wish I had time to blow dry my hair every day - almost.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
The good the bad and the ugly. Here goes. I've always sworn by Norelco trimmers. I've owned several. They normally last reasonably well. I normally get 5 years of use out of them. I say reasonably well because in this day and age, 5 years is good but I prefer things to last 20 years like they used too. Sadly; that's not going to happen. The adjustable guide is the best design that I have found. Far better than similar units that use multiple guides that can get lost, damaged and require additional storage space. The turbo function does work, it has enough high power that calling it "turbo" is not only cool but accurate. The charge/low battery lights function well. The vacuum functions well. I've tried other manufactures so called vacuum units and found that not only did they not work they were a total disappointment. This vacuum system works! Removing and installing the guide was a bit tricky at first but you get used to it. The single thing that I miss is the slide up mini trimmer. Frankly; I would rather have that than the vacuum. Still, I like this product and recommend it! I have had it about a year now and it still works perfect!

Update: 3 years old and like new!

Update: 5 years old, still like new! If it ever fails I'll be buying another Philips/Norelco.

product_title: GranNaturals Boar Bristle Smoothing Hair Brush for Women and Men - Medium/Soft Bristles - Natural Wooden Large Flat Square Paddle Hairbrush for Fine, Thin, Straight, Long, or Short
review_text:
You get what you pay for when buying a boar bristle brush. This brush has a great feel to it, the handle and weight of the brush in my hand work well to guide the brush through my long hair. The purpose of a BBB is not to detangle; it is to stimulate the scalp, spread sebum throughout your length, and use as a finishing brush. One should use a detangle brush or comb before brushing with a BBB. I use the GranNatuarals Boar Bristle Brush in the morning and at night, and I never use it on wash days. It is not a brush to use on wet hair. So, if you know this about a BBB, this is an excellent choice in BBB.

Also, the weight and shape of this brush make an excellent hair brush paddle choice.

I highly recommend this brush on both counts.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
A great alternative to the expensive plug in version. It has just as much power - maybe more. Reliability is about the same. You end up spending more for batteries, but the unit is much cheaper to begin with. I'm not sure how much electricity costs are for the plug in model. I subtract a star from both this one and the plug in model because of reliability. Over the years I have had almost everything go wrong from dead batteries to bad switches to corroded wires to just plain dead. The first one I had lasted 4 years. None have since. These units are not repairable. Expect them to last a year, maybe two.

This unit has the exact same mechanism as the expensive plug in model and uses the same replacement heads and is about the same size. The batteries come out the bottom and there is an O ring seal there. If moisture is allowed to enter it will mess up the battery compartment. If you stand it vertically after use rather than laying it down it will last much much longer because the water drains off it. I get a month, sometimes two, out of a set of batteries.

Do not buy the suggested newer model of this for $15. It's not the same as the others. It a motor driven thing with a huge head that is hard to use and doesn't do near as good of a job. It's small and cheap. Junk.

product_title: Easy Feet Foot Cleaner
review_text:
I was highly skeptical about this gadget, but when I ruptured a disk in my back, I decided to take a chance. I should have listened to my instincts.

Let me put it bluntly. This contraption does not work in ANY way as advertised. Anyone saying otherwise HAS to be a lying SHILL!

The suction cups don't stick to the floor of tub or stone shower. At all. This makes every other feature kinda worthless. The point of this toy is to not have to bend over to scrub the dirt or smooth out the calluses on your feet. But since it won't stay put, there is nothing easy about cleaning your feet with this thing.

Since the suction cups didn't stick to the floor, I tried jamming the thing in a corner and holding it there with my other foot. But even if you can get it to stay still enough to rub your foot on the brush, the bristles are weak and cheap. They flattened out with the third attempted use. The stone is small and even more useless than the brush.

This is the perfect example of a sucker product! Wouldn't it be great if this worked? But it doesn't. SAVE YOUR MONEY!

A long handled bath brush/pumice stone combo actually does work. If you use it while seated, there is very little bending involved, saving your back.

review_title: Great for those with athletes foot!
review_text:
Using this product and Defense Shower Gel (link here: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B01BICMJ16/ref=twister_B01E0GSW8Q?_encoding=UTF8&psc=1 ) I have been able to completely get rid of Athletes Foot (after having Athletes foot for 6 years). The defense soap is the cure, this thing just makes it easy to use it every day. I mix one bottle of defense gel up with water in a spray bottle which I spray onto my feet and then scrub with this thing.
The main complaint I have with this item is that the top part hits me on the top of my foot even when trying to be careful not to, and it hurts pretty bad when it does. If the top part (the arch holding the bristles above the foot) was at an angle, the edge wouldn't hit your foot and it would make the whole thing allot easier/comfortable to use. The only other (minor) change that I would like is for it to have more bristles in the back instead of the stone and the bristles in general could be a bit firmer as they are very soft.

Overall it's a nice inexpensive product that works great for me.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
This is definitely the most inexpensive entry into the Sonicare line. Well worth the price.

Likes:
-Uses AA batteries, either disposable or rechargeable. Works great with Sanyo Eneloop or similar "pre-charged" rechargeable batteries.
-Very inexpensive
-Uses same technology and brush heads as the far more expensive models.

Dislikes:
-Lacks some of the features of the higher-end models, such as the little beep that prompts you to move on to a different quadrant of your mouth.
-No indication of low battery. When the batteries are done, they're DONE. Leaves me running around with a mouthfull of toothpaste while fumbling to replace the batteries.

I've had mine for about 17 months with no issues other than periodic brush and battery replacement. Recently added two more to the household for the kids.

review_text:

Cr^p was growing inside and seemed to be........ well......it was not an attractive habitat inside the toothbrush.....not for me anyway....

With my most recent battery operated toothbrush, I have decided to remove the brush head (right word?)and shake all the water out every time I use it. This one has been going strong, with every day use for over 6 months!

It would be nice if the manufacturer gave instructions as to how to prolong the life of your purchase... but then again, they probably wouldn't make as many sales.

They have sold me three in the course of a year.

review_title: Great product! But leave the battery cap off between uses...
review_text:
Sonicare are great products, as my dentist has noticed.

The only problem with this great replaceable battery version is that the batteries didn't last for more than a week or two. Until I discovered that removing the battery cap between uses made the batteries last 2-3x as long.

I can only guess that there is a small constant current drain on the batteries. Removing the cap disconnects them and stops that constant 24-hour-a-day drain. Then they last fine. I use NiMH rechargeables.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
Ok, here's my summary review of this trimmer.

I've had a T900 trimmer for a few years now and wanted to upgrade to a new and hopefully better trimmer. I've had it now for two weeks and here's what I think...

* The vacuum is great, period. When shaving with my Norelco T900, the shavings would fly all over the place --- in the sink, behind the faucet, in between the handles of the faucet, and on the floor. With the vacuum set on low, I barely see any clippings now! Now, my wife doesn't get mad any more!

* The height adjustment can be easily set, and unlike other reviews mention, I haven't accidentally changed the setting without knowing.

* The clipper works great and easily cuts/trims without any effort. This is an upgrade from my T900.

* Battery holds its charge pretty well. You can use it with a power cord also when the battery is low.

* The smaller trimmer is a now a separate attachment. My T900 has it attached to the trimmer, and it can be popped up or down when needed. To me, this is a downgrade as it is not as convenient.

* The parts seem somewhat delicate. I try to be careful as to not cause damage.

Overall, the price is good, it works well, and I'm glad I purchased it, and would recommend it to all.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I was going to buy a Wahl trimmer as that is what I have been useing for years...it was a great trimmer...adjustable length long battery life..When it died on me I thought "well" I'll just get a new Wahl..the problem was they didnt make the one I have any more...thats when I thought I would make a change to see what else is out there..I looked on the web for 2 days trying to figure out what would be my next purchase...my beard got longer and didnt want to make the wrong choice...I read all the articles, reviews and then this trimmer was in front of me...never thought of getting one with a vaccuum on it...seemed simple enough just to wash the mess down the sink..and off the sink..and shake out my shirt and ...well you get the point..just didnt think that the vaccuum would be that good since it was cordless...it was really a surprise when I got it ..it got all but two little hairs the first time out..and the rest is history..it has all the options I want plus the vaccuum..If I ever have a complaint on this trimmer I will repost or add if possible to this review...but I like my choice and have no regrets..

PROS: works great, vaccuum is a plus, have not recharged it since I got it.

CONS: none, yet.

UPDATE:
well its sept 26 and all is well..I have not had to recharge this trimmer since I bought it. I still have no problems with it. it took a trim or two to get used to the new settings from my old trimmer but what dont you have to get used to when you change brands. I read a few articles from other users saying they had hair all over the place when they used it. they either look like grizzly adams and try to mow the whole thing at once or? I cut from the bottom of my face going up and never had more than a few hairs that didnt get in the vaccuum. It might depend on your style of cutting,havnt tried from the top down to see if the vaccuum gets it all. thats not my style of trimming. In my book its perfect..do you know why things are not always perfect because everybody has their own opinion. I hope this helps you in any way..Lyndon

review_title: Might be helpful, but not spectacular
review_text:
I am cautiously optimistic that this product will be helpful, but it's hard to say since I can't scientifically compare the "after" to the "before" . I've been using it for about a month. It certainly does no harm and might do some good, but to say that it's miraculous is a bit of an over statement.

My hair is damaged from old age and too many medications. The newer the hair, the less dry and damaged it appears. The tips are terribly dry, but it seems to me that, since using this product they are a little bit more flexible and maybe softer in texture but no different in appearance.

The shampoo lathers well and I leave it on for a few minutes while I bathe to let it soak in. However, since I can't find an Argan Oil Conditioner that doesn't have to be washed as in shampooed) out I'm not using a conditioner. It seems to me that having to shampoo, then add a conditioner, and have to shampoo it out is more time consuming than necessary. I haven't used any of my non-argan oil conditioners because I'm afraid they might undo whatever the shampoo is supposed to have done. To me, the idea combination is a shampoo and rinse-out conditioner that are meant to compliment each other.

More Than Clean is a combination scrub and masque recommended for morning use. You work it into your skin for a couple of minutes, then leave it on for a few minutes before rinsing it off. There are no unpronounceable ingredients in it, and it smells like peppermint. It's a very thick bilious colored liquid dispensed through the bottle cap. I've used it four times with great results on my skin and one unexpected but welcome side effect.

The MTC initially feels like mud, but there's a really refreshing tingle that's just great first thing in the morning. If you're of the generation that used a product called Seabreeze, that's exactly the sensation, only stronger. The tingle doesn't go away until the stuff is rinsed off, either, and skin feels really clean. I have some large pores around my nose, and they're thoroughly flattened by
this stuff.

If you have dry skin, go easy with this, and use a good moisturizer afterwards. I have an oily T Zone with dry cheeks, and have learned to concentrate on my oily areas with the MTC, with just a quick once over on the dryer areas of my face. I've been using this just before showering in the morning, and then using the shower to rinse it off--and here's the unexpected side effect: my miserable early spring sinuses have improved! I think it's the herbs in the product coupled with the steam from the shower, but my whole sinus area feels SO much more open. Hooray!

I'm thrilled with this product. My skin feels awake and energized, and the products I use daily--serums, moisturizer, and BB cream--just sink right in after use. I was provided a bottle of More Than Clean for review, and am delighted to do so. I really like the effect on my skin, and love breathing easier. Win all around!

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I have been using a Norelco T370 trimmer for several months. I bought it for the mini-shaver initially, decided to grow a beard, then trimmed the beard with the beard trimmer attachment. It did a great job of shaping and trimming, but left a mess of clippings in the sink. After reading a million reviews, I decided to try the T980 for it's vacuum feature.

The T980 is great! It does a perfect job of trimming my beard evenly (setting at 7, ultimate beard length to be a 9). The best part is that about 90% of the clippings go into the vacuum receptical with only about 10% being lost. I have not come across any of the negatives (adjustment slips, tugs hairs and on and on) mentioned in other reviews. Unlike my T370, this trimmer lets you know when it's fully charged or about to go dead, and even if it does die in the middle of a session from a dead battery, plugging it in finishes the job. Most other trimmers only work when charged, not on house current.

I can't think of anything this trimmer could do better. In my estimation it's looks, design and operation are flawless. The clipper works well on my beard's 'neckline' and the mini-trimmer keeps the bottom of my mustache trimmed perfectly. I really think the T370 does as good a job trimming as this one does, but will not run with a dead battery when plugged in, and does make a mess with beard clippings all over the place. For those two reasons alone, this trimmer is a BEST BUY!

I am not putting the T370's abilities down in any way. For the price it can't be beat. It trims well and the mini-shaver is still the best way to shave the short hairs on my cheeks above my beard on a daily basis. I use it daily along with the T980 and will continue to. They both have their place. If you don't mind the beard trimmings everywhere, you will be happy with the T370, however if you are serious about perfect beard grooming (and I DO mean PERFECT), with none of the mess, both tools are a must.

review_text:
I had a pretty ugly blackhead on my nose. For weeks I tried everything to get rid of it. I even asked my girlfriend for some beauty tips. Nothing worked. After awhile I noticed it getting bigger so I became desperate. I did something most guys would ever do... I visited a beauty salon that specializes in skin care. Fortunately for me, the lady I spoke to didn't want to take my money and told me to just pick up a bottle of Vi-Tae Blackhead remover. She told me all this mombo jumbo about why and how it works and I pretended like I understood but it all flew over my head. I went home later that night and found it on Amazon. Honestly, I didn't want to spend $30+ dollars on a health and beauty product because, well, I'm a guy. But I took the lady's advice and went with it. Like Prime normally does, I got it in two days. I followed the directions - apply every morning to damp skin, let it sit for a few minutes and rinse. I have to be honest... I didn't see any difference after the first day. The blackhead was still there. I did it again the second day. Nothing. Third day. Zilch. Fourth day. Nada. I was becoming impatient and felt ripped off. However, after I applied it on the fifth day, the blackhead was gone after I rinsed it! I was like WHOA! This girly stuff really works. Before I start to rave about this stuff, I have to say that it didn't get it all out. If I look close enough, I can still see a tiny spec left in my pore. But I'll just continue using this stuff and see what happens. In all honesty, no one else can see it anymore. But my girlfriend said to continue keeping it clean so it doesn't come back.

FYI, I'm a 31 year old Asian male with pretty oily skin.

PROS:
- Actually works but it can take up to a week to remove a large blackhead
- Smells good and refreshing
- Directions are easy to follow

CONS:
- This stuff will sting the first few times you use it. It's not unbearable but it's pretty annoying
- It's a tad difficult to rinse off after you let it sit for a few minutes

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I've had this product for something like 3 years now and finally thought I'd write a review.

I love it. Others have stated quite clearly it's benefits, which I fully agree with.

So, I'm going to focus on the long-term (minor) issues I've had just so you know.

a) After about 2 years, the trimmings basket (the plastic container your hair gets sucked into) came apart. I used some crazy glue to fix it and it's been fine since.

b) It's sometimes hard to get the guard back on on the head, takes some finesse.

And that, my friends, is really it.

The vacuum really works but you gotta have turbo on. My girlfriend no longer has to deal with hair in the sink. It does a great job on my beard (I like it short, I'm a #2), and it's even fine for my neck (YMMV).

Best beard trimmer I've ever owned in 15 years.

review_text:
let me start by saying, I was reluctant about this shampoo because when I think of Argan oil, or any oil for that matter, I think of something that will weight down my hair and make it oily. Therefore, I did not go into this with high expectations.
I can say that I was pleasantly surprised!!
smell: It smells amazing! seriously, the smell reminds me of laundry. It is clean, light, and pleasant.
lather: It was a great lather especially for it to be sulfate free. It lathered well and made my hair feel clean
results: I did not use conditioner so that I could really gauge the results. I blow dried my hair per usual and I was really happy with the results. My hair had body and volume, felt very healthy, had some shine, was not oily or dry, and smelled amazing.
Day two and my hair still looks and feels great. I would definitely recommend this product. It also makes me feel good using something that has all natural oils and ingredients that I can read and understand.
The ONLY bad thing I could say is that my pump is ineffective and doesn't work like it should. however this is not enough to effect the ratings as I just unscrewed it and poured it into my hands. simple fix.

I was given this product for free in exchage for an UNBIASED review. This did NOT reflect my review in any way.

review_title: I counted the days I was without it...
review_text:
My original Sonicare died after about 2 years. My wife spent [...] bucks on it and needless to say I was not happy to see it go. You would think a $[...] toothbrush would last pretty much forever... Anyway, I replaced it with this much cheaper model and am very pleased so far. In addition to being a lot less expensive it has a much simplified design which should last longer, and has a user replaceable battery.

On the negative side, it seems to chew through batteries. In fact I actually reported the first one Amazon shipped as defective as it stopped working after 5 days. Turns out the batteries I swapped were dead too and there was nothing wrong with the toothbrush after all. My bad. The fresh batteries I installed only lasted maybe 3 weeks or so. I'm going to use rechargeables from now on, but just be forewarned that this thing gobbles batteries.

But in terms of the operation of the toothbrush I love it. In the short time I had to use a regular toothbrush waiting for this to arrive I felt like I had trench mouth. No matter how long or how vigorously I would brush my teeth just never felt clean, and by 10AM if felt like I hadn't brushed in days. The commercial is a cliche but it's true - Sonicare makes you feel like you just walked out of the dentist office.

product_title: Gauge Gear Ear Stretching Balm | 10 ml Jar | Piercing Aftercare | Stretched or Damaged Skin Care | All Natural Moisturizing Salve w/Jojoba
review_title: DONT WAIT AS LONG AS I DID!
review_text:
I had this on wishlist for months now, debating back and forth if I needed it. If you're doing debating as well, seriously just buy it. Its less than 10 bucks and definitely worth using on your ears or other pierced areas. I have very sensitive skin so when I went up a size before I got the balm, my ears would be irritated for weeks to a little over a month. They would constantly be hot, itchy, dry and clear discharge would be oozing down my neck. GROSS! I even waited 10 months to go up a size and that was only at the 12G-10G stage.

2 days after I got the balm, I prepped my ears after a shower. Rubbed the balm generously over my left ear and on the taper. There was very minimal tugging and it did not make me cringe. Took less than a minute to get the taper in compared to before, taking over 5 minutes of twisting, pushing, & massaging to get the taper in w/out the balm. Took no more than 5 days to "fully heal." No dry, flaky, irritated, oozing ear. Waited 6 months this time around to size up to 2G.

At the same time, my right ear was already infected because I had to replace my plug but I was out in public and only had a spare in my purse. I cleaned it as best as I can but it didnt work. My ear felt like it was back to its newly stretched phase- cracked skin, bump under the ear and clear discharge constantly flowing down. Cleaned my plugs and my ear with salt water then rubbed the balm all over. It started to heal up faster than it did when all I had was salt water & vitamin E oil.

Highly recommended for anyone who's trying to stretch their ears.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
At first I thought this was going to be the solution to the problem of the original rechargeable Sonicare toothbrush with batteries that can't be replaced (my original Sonicare stopped holding a charge).

However, after only four months (just long enough to waste money replacing the brush head!), the button began to only work erratically, and now it does not work at all (can't power the toothbrush on).

The reviews that state that the battery compartment does not keep water out are completely true. The battery compartment is always moist, and the batteries will begin to rust.

I was pleased that my Eneloop batteries worked well to power the toothbrush, so I could be using rechargeable batteries, however it doesn't matter if the toothbrush itself doesn't last past 6 months.

The batteries that came with the toothbrush lasted around a month. The Eneloops needed charged only once in the next three months.

Looks like the Sonicare brand just fails on too many levels, regardless of whether you are using the ultra-expensive rechargeable unit, or this unit with two AA batteries.

[Update] Flashlights have had "screw on" caps for nearly one hundred hears. The Sonicare toothbrush is the same form factor. I have no idea why someone at Philips thought a "clip on" cap (vs. a screw on) would be better, ESPECIALLY for something you use with water. I am still COMPLETELY BAFFLED by why they would use this design. The battery compartment will ALWAYS be moist. Being able to use rechargeable batteries is clearly superior to being stuck with the Philips Soincare charging station. However, the fact that your batteries get wet means you will eventually ruin your batteries. That said, I am about to purchase another one. Being able to use your own batteries makes it a when, both for the fact that you can replace the batteries and also so that the (much more expensive) toothbrush isn't useless when the internal batteries fail after a year or so. Unfortunately there is no better alternative at this pricep oint.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Still a classic quality Norelco trimmer.
review_text:
I used to have an old Norelco trimmer that used for years until it just wouldn't charge anymore and bought this as the "new and improved" replacement and for the most part . . . it is.
Here is the short:

Pros: Classic Design, Same quality and function, powerful vacum
Cons: Not good for trimming to skin w/o Guard.

The Long:

Its form, design and cut remind me of my old Norelco (which is great) with only one major difference, the vacuum. In order for the vacum to work there is a plastic vacum "sleeve" or "guard" that goes up to the teeth. The other reviewers complained about close trimming without the full guard and I do agree that it is awkward to pull down the vacuum sleeve for a close trim but I found that on both this model and my old one, the teeth on the trimmer were too big for a comfortable close trim anyway, so I do not use that feature. I instead use a fine tooth slid-up trimmer on another shaver for that. I disagree with the noise complaints, I thought the vacuum was only slightly louder than the actual trimmer and there was plenty of suction at the lower setting, which you can't hear over the trimmer. Overall, a great classic Norelco trimmer.

All of them are still working and I have replacement heads delivered regularly via Amazon's "Subscribe & Save" program. Great! We use them with rechargeable batteries; they last almost a month between charges.

But let me repeat what others have said: you simply have to LAY THEM DOWN TO DRY. Don't stand them up on the base. I had read that advice in the reviews when I bought them. My kids and I quickly got used to laying them down after use. However, my wife really had trouble learning this and she kept leaving it upright. Her toothbrush would occasionally stop working so I would open it up and let it dry thoroughly and it would start working again (although there is some corrosion inside.) She finally learned to lay it down, though.

Highly recommended (unless you are unwilling to slightly modify your behavior for a bargain!)

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
This purchase was to replace a Wahl trimmer that died suddenly after a couple of years. It had done a good job but the feature I liked best about it was the built in vacuum. Stopped my wife from complaining about a trail of hair on the sink.

After a quick look thru the internet I soon discovered this vacuum feature was a rarity. Then I found the NorelcoT980 Turbo here on Amazon. It has the vacuum and a extra Turbo function that your first time you'll think it's going to pull off all the hair. Well it doesn't but the motor does get louder in turbo and I'm sure it also eats up more battery power. It's a well made piece of machinery that feels good in your hand. The heigh adjustment click in nicely. The cover over the blades ride nicely over your face but this is something you'll have to use the included cleaning brush to wipe out hair that will stick in it's nicks and crannies.

There is a second blade that is used for finer detailing like around your mouth. It works well and enables you to keep the hair out of your mouth. Funny thing about the attachments. The first few times you change them or remove the hair catcher they seem to be difficult to remove. But soon they pop off easily. Suppose it's just a matter of learning were to pull.

I do wish it came with a stand for the razor. It comes with a pouch that you can store a everything including the charger, but somehow I get the feeling Norelco though us guys with beards travel a lot. I don't and would have like a place to sit the T980 where I can grab it for a quick trim.

review_title: Why did I wait so long?!

I hate the mess that using the traditional mouthwash cap creates. No matter how careful you are, how well you rinse the lid or wipe off the bottle- it always gets that mouthwash crust. Plus I tend to over pour and waste it and yeesh...

First, it does make the bottle even taller- keep in mind- those are big bottles already and the pump needs to be tall to accommodate that. It ain't pretty.
Secondly- it will disperse as you push down but will also give a tiny squirt as the pump comes back up. Just be mindful to keep the cup under it until it's back in position.

That's it! I love it. I wish I had bought one sooner.

review_title: Protects my RED hair. Stopped the color stripping from my old shampoo.
review_text:
This stuff is wonderful. I am in a place in my life that I am removing ALL chemicals from our household. There are so many bad things for you in Makeup and Hair products - endocrine disrupters and such. I had done everything from Baking soda and ACV - and I was trying my hardest to get to a water wash only place in my hair care. However, I have been having to combat the fact that a year and a half ago I decided to perm my hair. It was AWEFUL. 2 months later, I bought a home perm and combed it through my hair to reverse the fried frizziness. Needless to say, my hair hasn't been the same since. It grows slowly, so I have major issues with split ends (sometimes a strand is split in 5 places and when I brush my dry hair, I have tiny pieces breaking off everywhere.) I also have VERY fine hair so using anything reparative makes it flat and heavy - and who wants that?! Anyway, I was doing ok with a Dr. Bronners soap (which I really loved) but I recently colored my hair red and the Bronners was stripping the color. After reading a ton of reviews on this product, I bought it and LOVE it.

I was hoping that I wouldnt have to use a conditioner, but if you dont, then you HAVE to wait till your hair is dry to brush it as to not damage it while wet. But I can tell you that THIS Argan Oil shampoo keeps my color fresh AND smooths the shaft to make it soft without weighing it down. I have yet to find something to repair my split ends - but I have only used this 3x now - so we'll see.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
There have been a lot of complaints about the vacuum option of this trimmer. Let's be realistic....its not a Hoover, it's a trimmer. It catches MOST of the hairs, which is a lot better than NONE of the hairs. I've used it a few times so far and haven't had the problem others complained about where the setting is changed mid-trim. Just hold the thing below the dial, and not right on the dial. It gave a nice even trim all around. I've had it for a couple of months, used it 3-4 times, and still haven't had to recharge it.

Suggested improvement - A stand would have been great so I could put it in my medicine cabinet and not have it roll around my counter.

Tips for using - I found you're better off with dry hair. When the hair's wet, it's harder for the vacuum to pull it in. I also found that the vacuum works much better on longer hair then on shorter hair. Maybe the shorter hairs are too light and get blown around? Last but not least, watch out for the settings. The dial goes 1-9 so I started with 4, which was way too short. I could have grown that beard from scratch in a couple of weeks. 5 also proved a little short for me. Be sure to start a lot higher than you think you need, and work your way down if needed.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
Now that I bought and used the T980, my cool slacker goatee is attracting too many women. I'm not getting any rest.

Naturally, a product that causes grief should be down-rated, but I won't here because this shaver is just doing its job.

And, we all like things with "turbo" in the description, however loosely that term is applied. It makes it go faster with a cool noise, so even in a shaver that is attractive to many.

Electric shavers for beards sure beat the heck out of scissors! The Norelco has a wide range of cutting depths and my beard comes out a uniform length. I did not feel any pulling or other discomfort. The charge seems to last for days and the charger itself, like the shaver, is a decent and modern design.

The little detail cutter is easy to attach and does a great job of defining the beard area and also clipping any stray hairs under the nose where the big cutter head cannot reach.

Some people think the closest cutting position is still not close enough for that short-stubble look and that does seem to be the case. I don't want mine that close, but I understand those who do and I take off a star for brotherly solidarity. Actually, I'm sure that if it was to cut more closely, that would take it into the realm of regular shavers, an expensive world of high-tech blades and lubricants. Actually, if you press down a little, you can get closer.

The turbo thing works well. It vacuums almost every hair into the storage chamber. I didn't expect the vacuum action to work so well. I think the turbo button should be the only button, but there it is. The non-turbo setting is less noisy...

The parts detach easily and the little supplied brush works well to clean it out. The little travel pouch is nice.

The T980 works just as it should, for me, and the price is reasonable. I think it will last a long time and I am glad I bought it.

As for the women, I did exaggerate. One did make a favorable comment which is one more than before. That is an improvement, eh?

product_title: Braun 8000 360 Complete Foil/Cutter Block for Models 8995, 8985, 8975
review_text:
If you've been reading any of the reviews here lately you will know the 8000 series foil/cutterblock combo has been replaced with a new combo now called the series 5 Combi 51S. You will receive this replacement even if the picture on the product page shows "8000 series" as it has been discontinued for over a year. Braun merged the replacement for the 8000 series (Activator) with the 360 Complete. This new foil/cutterblock is garbage! The cutterblock has wide blades, as opposed to the thinner blades of the original 8000 series, which pull your stubble and take MANY passes over your face to shave. They are prone to premature failure and I have gone through 3(THREE) of these in 6 months! (I bought one and two were free through Braun after complaining). All the free replacements in the world weren't making the shaving experience any better. I longed for the days when my Activator 8595 cut smooth, close, and comfortably. After all, this shaver had been my favorite for 6 years so far! I was very close to dumping the whole shaver and moving on when I happened across a reviewer on Amazon who suggested using the 7000 series replacement foil/cutterblock in his review. It worked PERFECTLY! The 7000 series replacement looks just like the much coveted original on my 8595 Activator - down to the thinner cutting blades! It didn't pull my stubble, it cut smooth as butter, and was comfortable: JUST LIKE NEW! I'd like to thank the original reviewer (James L. Walls "sixtoe") for the very good advice.

***Update: August 10th, 2011***
I hope people are happy with the replacement I recommended. I sure am! I just wanted to update the product link for the better replacement: [[ASIN:B001VH6F9G Braun Series 3 Combi 30B Foil and Cutter Replacement Pack (Formerly 4700,7000)]]

***Update: January 13, 2013***
Unfortunately, the Braun 30B Foil and Cutter Replacement Pack is now the same terrible cutter block design as the series 5 (8000 replacement). I ordered another 30B to replace the one I bought 2.5 years ago and was highly disappointed when the package came. I will have to do some research to see if any of Braun's other replacements are the good, narrow blade versions. I have read some reports that the narrow cutting block is available, but without the foil. If I cannot find a narrow blade replacement I am going to throw in the towel after 8 years of service from this shaver. Shame on Braun for putting out those ill performing wide blade cutting blocks. Terrible...

***Update: January 18, 2013***

It appears the highly elusive narrow blade cutter block can be found on the 31S replacement pack. The unfortunate news is the included foil is not compatible. Therefore, a replacement foil for the 8000 series/Activator/7000 series/360 Complete would be needed in conjunction with the quality cutter block effectively doubling your cost because it is difficult to find the foil sold by itself. This would be a combined expense of roughly $55-$60 in order to bring your shaver back to the "like new" shave we all want. Remember - the "direct" replacement combo for this shaver series will leave you highly disappointed due to the WIDE cutter block which pulls hair and easily nicks skin. Another facet to influence your decision in spending $60 to refresh your Braun is many of these shavers - due to their age - are in need of new motors and potentially batteries. The motors gradually slow down with time and I noticed a HUGE difference when I replaced mine 2 years ago. Now, these motors are almost impossible to find at this point and for me, personally, it is getting to the point of diminished returns. I hope this post helps you in both informing you of the available narrow cutter block, but also in weighing your decision in either keeping your Braun chugging along or researching a new alternative.

Ours both have very long, firm bristles top and bottom that are difficult to move back and forth through, and there are bristles completely surrounding the pumice stone so that you can't really get to it.  The pic on the box and the advertisements show no bristles at the back of the "shoe" behind the pumice stone, only in front of it, so that it's actually accessible.  The way these are made, the stone might as well not be there, because you can't use it. I'm not even sure it's an actual pumice stone after running my fingers over it--it feels artificial and has a different texture than pumice.  It's a good concept, and will at least take off surface dirt--if you can hang on to it.  I actually worry about it causing seniors to fall, instead of preventing it. I have to think there are different models; I looked online at the commercial and the plastic looks different and there are several colors, plus no bristles at the back.  It says EZ Feet on the box, but it looks like this may be a cheaper model than the one they push on their site and their commercials.

review_text: I have extremely thick, somewhat wavy hair. Not curly, not straight. This product didn't do much for me. I am a tender head also so it was nice to brush through with no pain. If you are going to use this here are some tips: brush your hair before. I keep reading reviews that say "it won't brush through my extremely curly hair." Well of course it won't! It isn't a magical brush that will glide through hair. When using the heated brush, I used my regular brush with it because the ends wouldn't get straightened. I had to make sure to keep my hair held tight all the way through so I used my regular brush in the other hand. My hair didn't turn out to be "bone straight" but it's better than when I started. My ends didn't get straightened but I also just really need a hair cut so I am not blaming the product for that. But it is true what people are saying, it doesn't get hot enough. I have straighteners that (claim to) get 300 degrees Fahrenheit. This product is in Celsius, so I'm not sure of the conversion but it gets up to 230 Celsius. If it was hotter, I'm sure it would work much better. Basically, I will use this a few more times and try to get the hang of it and hopefully like it more.

This is how I have to use it to get a fabulous result, otherwise it just feels like my hair is weighed down by a bunch of product after more than one use.

First, I wash my hair with a gentle clarifying shampoo like Paul Mitchell. Then I use just a dime size of this product as directed. (I have thick coarse hair that falls past my shoulders.) I work the product well into my scalp and roots, pulling the suds through to my ends. After rinsing, I apply a good conditioner to just the midsection-ends of my hair, avoiding my roots.

My hair comes out wonderful, and manages to stay that way over the course of several days where before I would start to get that greasy look/feel after the second day. Very happy with this product!

product_title: Moroccan Argan Oil Shampoo, 8 Fl Oz - Smooths and Repairs - Sulfate Free - Natural - Imported from Morocco by Pure Body Naturals
review_text:
When I first saw this product on Amazon, I was wary of all of it's good reviews. I have long hair that is prone to dryness and breakage, and have tried just about every shampoo and conditioner on the market to improve hair health. I am pleasantly surprised that this shampoo lives up to it's claims.

I want everyone to understand that this is, in fact, a shampoo; it is NOT a cleansing conditioner. In my opinion, that is a plus, as it's important to cleanse your scalp and hair follicles without adding buildup that a "cleansing conditioner" often imparts. This shampoo is sulfate-free and gives a mild lather. I feel like it cleans my scalp and hair sufficiently, without stripping. I color-treat my hair, and this shampoo has never stripped or lightened my color.

As far as moisture is concerned, this adds hydration without weighing my hair down. Yet, it is NOT drying to my hair as so many shampoos are. I have long, fine hair, so that's a significant point. If you read the ingredient list, you will see that this product contains many natural oils and humectants. Given that, I am continually surprised that it doesn't weight my hair down.

After use, my wet hair feels smooth and sleek, but I still need to follow with a conditioner for detangling. Again, this is a shampoo; it is not a cleansing conditioner. Since there is no matching Pure Body Naturals daily conditioner for this shampoo, I have been experimenting with some other argan oil conditioners sold here on Amazon.

No matter your hair type, I think this shampoo can add to your hair health. I highly recommend trying it.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
I absolutely love this toothbrush! I have been using it for months and still really appreciate it for several reasons. I have previously owned a rechargeable Philips Sonicare toothbrush and I was nervous that with it only using two AA batteries it would not have the same power as my previous rechargeable version-I was pleasantly surprised to find that it had just as much power as I remember the rechargeable to have had (granted the last time I used that one was several years ago).

I really love the auto-off timer on this toothbrush, as it allows me to brush my teeth early in the morning or late at night, while semi-awake, knowing that I have brushed long enough. I really like the toothbrush head as well, as I feel that the contoured tips on the bristles get in between my teeth instead of just on top of them.

Before I ordered this toothbrush, I found that most of the negative reviews it was associated with concerned the not-so-water tight seal on the battery compartment; which ended up causing premature failure of the toothbrush. I also read about some really simple ways to increase the effectiveness of the watertight seal by oiling the O-ring with a dab of Petroleum Jelly. I probably overdid this, as when I snapped the base back onto the toothbrush it oozed quite a bit of Petroleum Jelly, but I will say it certainly seems to have helped as my toothbrush is happily still alive and getting my teeth squeaky clean! :-)

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I researched all of the Norelco beard trimmers before deciding to buy on Amazon. I read all of the reviews and noted some of the negatives like noise and the fact that the shaver doesn't "vaccum" all of the whiskers. I must say I haven't seen much of these negatives. The trimmer works great and beats my old Braun which did not collect whiskers. I would say that 90% of the whiskers are collected in the compartment rather than on my bathroom counter. The noise in my opinion is to be expected given the cutting and vacuum action being performed. I especially like the carrying case and accessory trimmer that are included with this model. The only negative I have noted is that the trimmer settings are not real precise. If I want a real clean look I have to go all the way down to the lowest setting and my goatee needs trimming about every 3 days. For the guys who are able to keep their beards a little longer this is probably not much of an issue.

I highly recommend this shaver if you are wanting a clean, neat trim.

Pure Body Naturals Argan Oil Shampoo

What is in it?
Aragan Oil- Beneficial in its numerous properties making it known as Liquid gold for your hair. It hydrated hair, enhances the elasticity of hair, creates shine and tames uncontrollable,unmanageable frizzy hair. Aragan Oil strengthens and repairs damaged hair as well as healing split ends.

Additionally, fatty acids omega 9, 6 and 3 help to reflect damaging UV rays and protect hair from the sun, deterring the dullness that comes from dryness. Jojoba Oil- Moisturizes your scalp deep down to its pores and doesn’t evaporate. Helps control the sebum production of the scalp. Prevents and stops hair loss and thinning of hair, stimulate and promote new hair growth.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: Fix the leak issue, and the toothbrush is superb
review_text:
Since I originally wrote this review, I bought 5 of them, over time. All are still working.

I've used Sonicare since before they were bought out by Philips. One thing I hated in over 15 years of owning them is the battery dying out, it lasts about 5 years, and I've gone through 3 versions already. While a new brush will hold a charge for over a week, after 3 years, it will give about 3 days sometimes not, so if you travel with the brush you'll also have to lug the charger, otherwise you'll have a useless brush with no power sometime in your trip. The brushes still use NiCD, so you get a memory effect and to revive it you have to recharge best when the brush is dead; to do so you have to endure the increasingly weak brush stroking and it dying sometime while you brush. You can't just leave it on, all Sonicare's have a 2 minute timer, Quad Pacer or not.

This AA powered Sonicare I've had for 1.5 years, and it works as good as the rechargeable versions except it doesn't have Quad Pacer, not a problem. As a brush, it has the vigor and thus, the benefits of what made Sonicare famous.

I was concerned about Amazon reviews of water leaking into the battery compartment. I've tested the brush since then, and found what the weakness is; not cleaning the battery compartment O ring seal after each battery replacement.

Like many items used for water, you should clean the battery compartment O ring and its sealing surfaces thoroughly before resealing it. The head usually has toothpaste on it that is abrasive and gritty and will break the O ring seal if not washed clean out. All a user need do is during a battery change, use an old manual toothbrush to brush clean the open end cap until its clean of all debris. Wash the O ring with soap and water. Let both air dry to avoid getting lint on the cap or ring. Use a clean finger to wipe clean the interior battery compartment to insure its clean or clear of residual toothpaste, as this is the other half of the sealing surface that contacts the O ring.

When ready to seal, take a tiny dab of vasoline or silicone O ring lubricant between your thumb and forefinger, and pass the O ring through these fingers so it has a light coat of lubricant. This prevents the o ring from twisting as you insert the cap, and breaking the seal. Place the o ring on the cap, and push on the Sonicare. That's it!

I use NiMH batteries, and a new set lasts over 2 months, brushing once a day. I can even use my old used NiMH cells on this brush, and I get about 1 month.

The O ring should last over 5 years but if you know O rings, it AS568A size is -023, change them every 2-3 years. These rings typically cost 1c each, but the problem is finding them, usually they are sold in industrial supply houses.

The toothbrush has held up, so it won't die because of leaking or bad battery. For $25, this unit is an ideal Sonicare. Now if only the brush heads were cheaper.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: To date the fastest, most convenient, least messy shave I've had
review_text:
This shaver really is a treat to use. I have had no difficulty with the "grade" of shave slipping mid shave and I find it a very comfortable shaver to use.
The shave is quick and the receptacle really does seem to catch upwards of 95% of what I'm using.
So far I've had four shaves off the one charge and I shave once a week, so the battery seems to hold its charge really well.
Cleaning is a cinch.
It's noisy with turbo on, but certainly not in the same vicinity as a hair dryer. It's certainly not anything that's a detraction from the shave.
The only reason I haven't given this 5 stars is because of the area just under the nose, the other reviewers that have mentioned this are correct - it's very hard to get to this area without contorting your nose and/or lip.
I simply remove the protector and do the last few hairs freehand with the open shaver or a pair of cuticle scissors.
The overall performance of this shaver more than makes up for this one shortcoming.
Very nice carrying bag too included.

review_title: Not as good as its predeccesor.
review_text:
My old T965's battery gave up after 4 faithful years of service. Philips has now replaced the old standard coiled power cords with specialized adapters. This means when you're on vacation you've got to bring the AC adapter for your face trimmer and then bring a different AC adapter for your beard trimmer.

Pros: It looks real pretty. It cuts well.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Might be the best out there for the $, but not terribly impressed
review_text:
I purchased this unit to replace a 7-year old Norelco trimmer (that had an integral main blade and an integral mini pop-up blade, but no vacuum).

Good Points: Comfortable, not too noisy, even on "Turbo" setting. Strong blades clip everything in sight. Mini trimmer blade is sharp and precise. Guide pops off easily. Comfortable to hold. Vacuum does pick up lots of beard/stache clippings and it's easy to empty clippings,too. Easy to change lengths. Nice travel bag. Battery life excellent (but do NOT overcharge and obey the drain-to-zero recommendations).

Bad Points: Vacuum not strong enough to suck up all clippings...you'll still need to trim over a sink or trash container, which really takes away from the advantage of having the vacuum (even on the Turbo setting). Length indicator needs a stronger click-and-hold ratchet mechanism -- too easy to accidentally change length settings. I miss the pop-up mini trimmer: Having to manually swap out blades is a pain. The trimmer can't stand up, even temporarily...it can only be stored in the bag or lying down.

Summary:
This trimmer might be the best compromise of cost / features / functionality out there, but was disappointed with the vacuum capabilities even on Turbo. I was very impressed by the cutting quality.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: Half the cost, but more convenient than a regular Sonicare
review_text:
Pros: half the cost of a Sonicare w/charger, less bulky
Cons: None so far

First of all, I should state that I have owned this product for over a year, and I am still giving it five stars.

Here's why: I had a Sonicare Advance for about three years and it worked well during that time, but at the end of those three years I had to keep it in the charger at all times or it would die in the middle of brushing. I was sick of lugging around the bulky charger any time I traveled, so when I saw the AA-battery model at Target for $40 I scooped it up.

Now instead of having to rely on an internal battery and a charger, I just keep four rechargeable AAs that I swap out when one pair dies. This isn't something I have to do very often--a pair of AAs lasts about a month (that's with two two-minute brushings a day). I have also not had any water damage, so the brush still works as great as my old Sonicare ever did. I do try not to get water on the brush and dry the entire unit whenever I finish using it. In addition, I take it apart once every two or three months and swab the O-ring with alcohol to keep it clean. This seems to be all of the maintenance needed to keep it in top condition.

So, if you want a good Sonicare brush that takes up less space and is easier to travel with, I highly recommend this model. I recommend cleaning it once in a while and trying to keep water out of the insides. I acknowledge this might not help if you get a bad unit (as many reviewers seem to have gotten), but mine has been great and I figure it can't hurt!

UPDATE: I have now owned it for a year-and-a-half and it still goes a month on two AA rechargeables. Even though I stopped doing the maintenance described above it's still working like new.

review_title: Works great, I'd rather have this than the expensive ones
review_text:
My pet peeve in electronics is non-replaceable or proprietary batteries, so I always choose the standard AA model if it's available. After a little research, I found this performs exactly the same as the high-priced units and at a fraction of the cost! I already have tons of rechargeable batteries that I use in remotes, mice, cameras, etc, so I didn't even have to buy extras.

I can see how the battery compartment may not be entirely water-tight, but it's on the bottom of the device, so I think the problem may be that people are standing the brush upright when not in use. It actually has a little stand on the back of it indicating it's clearly meant to be laid down horizontally. If you stood it upright and did not dry it off, I can see how water could seep down into the battery compartment, but it's clearly not meant to be stored that way. Or as is indicated in another review, put some vaseline on the gasket to seal it if you're really worried.

review_title: Works great, but needs extra care to prevent failure
review_text: OK, same complaint as everyone else.  My first unit died in less than 2 months from water seepage into the battery and switch compartments.  That being said, it does an excellent job of brushing your teeth.  It is cheaper than the sealed battery Sonicaire, and when the battery dies you don't have to wait for it to recharge, just pop in new batteries (I use NiMH rechargeables).  So the downside is that you have to dry the unit carefully after each use.  I still cannot find out how the water is getting inside the unit, but it is irrelevant if you dry it well enough.  Don't bother with trying to seal the unit, it is more trouble than it's worth.  My current unit is a year old and working fine.  BTW, save the battery cap from any old "dead" units.  I dropped my new one and the battery cap broke.  I used the cap from the dead unit (cleaned off the corrosion) and it worked fine...so at least I got some utility out of the dead one...sigh.  Minus one star for stupid design flaw.

review_title: Clear, healthy-looking skin after just 5 days!
review_text:
The first time I tried this product I noticed how different this face wash is from my normal face wash; it left my skin feeling clean and fresh, without drying it out! After a week of using the product, I really do notice smaller pores, and clearer skin.

I both love and hate the scent of this product. I love the fact that it has a eucalyptus-like effect that clears my sinuses. I don't like the 'organic' scent of the product that continues to linger long after I wash my face. It reminds me of mushrooms, and I hate mushrooms.

The two cons are simple:

Price- $34 for a 4.5oz bottle is extremely pricey! I'm not sure I can afford to keep buying this product.

Time- The length of time recommended to scrub your face, and leave it on your face is a total of five minutes. There's not much else you can do while washing your face, so this either extends your shower time, or getting-ready time in the morning.

The biggest pro is that I have clear, healthy-looking skin after only 5 days of using this product!

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
If we're completely honest, we've been conditioned by manufacturers these days to accept rubbish without complaint. Quite true, you can dial into their computer and navigate circles around their voicemail system for a few hours until your anger dissipates. Or is transferred to computer answering systems. Whichever comes first.

Happily, however, such is not the case with the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer.

Not only does this eager little trimmer solve several problems at once but it does so with a composure and aplomb that will sweep away the corporate fog and, suddenly, everything else you own will seem completely and utterly inadequate.

Trimming whiskers used to be such a chore that the ZZ Top look began to show some sense, if not appeal. The constant recharging, sweeping up afterward, seemingly endless search for single-tasking components that had wandered off and an assembly/disassembly process for cleaning the tool that would make Bill Gates weep. Philips, however, decided to go in a slightly different direction.

For a start, the battery holds on to a charge with a grip that would make Chuck Liddell cry. It doesn't last mere hours, days or weeks. Under standard use, mine lasts well over a month. Even when the battery light does begin to blink, what it really means to say is, "Pardon me but, at some point in the next several days, when it isn't too much of a bother, could you please plug me in for a bit?" Nothing urgent about it whatsoever. And once the lead is connected from socket to trimmer, a scant hour will have it fully refreshed and ready for another month on the road.

Then there is the all-in-one design. Unlike most trimmers, which require that you dig around to find the correct attachment in order to trim your left eyebrow now that you're done with the right, nearly everything is built directly into this sleek little unit. The only exception is a neat little detail trimmer that stands eternally at the ready in its own clear and obvious pocket inside the travel pouch. That's it. Nothing else to search out when you're dashing to work. It's all right there.

Not everyone who sells a "vacuum trimmer" truly means it. Most generate just a bit of wind, sufficient to scatter your whiskers over the widest possible surface. I firmly believe my last vacuum trimmer was designed by a consortium of housekeepers seeking job security. The T980, however, actually captures every single whisker, every single time. And then there's a Turbo button that doubles the already adequate force of the vacuum's suction so that you can give yourself that wind-blown look if you so choose.

But, by far, my favorite thing about this trimmer is the way it feels. It sits in your hand as if it were custom designed specifically for you. It's lightweight and nimble around the bends, falls effortlessly into its case when deeds are done and assembles as if there is an invisible force guiding your hand at every step of the way. I am genuinely amazed at the simplicity of removing and replacing the grille guard. For a time, I thought it must be drawn together by magnets. But it isn't. It's just a set of exceptionally well designed tabs and slots that quickly correct a hurried approach and seat the grille home with a satisfying, subtle click.

Most products on the market today are slapdash clumps of flimsy plastics and mechanics that are carefully designed to fail at the worst possible time. And, for some reason, we have accepted this corporate abuse in the hopes that prices would compensate us somehow. But they don't really, do they? When you've re-purchased the same device five times because it keeps breaking, whose interests are truly being served?

So, then, the T980 is a warning shot fired over the bow of companies everywhere who treat their clients like stupid, slobbering monkeys, devoid of choice or rights. With it, Philips is saying, "See, everyone? You needn't accept rubbish in exchange for your hard-earned money. We've done it properly and at a price point that is competitive." And why wouldn't we honor that?

I wish my hair grew faster.

review_title: Great Shampoo w/ Natural Ingredients and No Parabens
review_text:
I really like this Argan Oil shampoo. It leaves my hair feeling soft and shiny. I love the fact that it contains some very nourishing ingredients like Argan oil, jojoba oil, camellia seed oil, vanilla and honey. I also can feel great about using this product knowing there are no parabens and no harsh chemicals to damage my hair.

This shampoo comes in a 16 oz. brown plastic bottle with a pump dispenser. I absolutely loved the shampoo however the dispenser was a total fail. When I try to pump the product out it comes out of the dispenser as well as the top of the bottle where the pump goes in. It made a big mess when trying to use the dispenser so I just opted to transfer it to another bottle and use it without the pump.

Overall I love the shampoo but the product packaging (the pump in particular) needs some work. So, for me this product gets 3.75 stars and I'll round up to 4. If the company works on the dispenser and ensures they work I would give it a solid 5 stars.

product_title: Sally Hansen Miracle Gel Set 6-Piece Random Collection
review_text:
I originally purchased this because I thought it would be fun to get 6 colors at random, but I should have known better. I strongly dislike all 6 colors I received and the Tan-acious has nail polish around handle area which makes me question if I should even try it out.

Granted, unlike some purchasers I got all miracle gel polishes and none were broken. The packaging was a bit iffy and I’m shocked none were damaged in shipment.

It’s a given that it’ll be a gamble with what colors you get, but if you’re going to give an atypical color at least balance it out with something more normal like a red or pink, even black or white would have helped!

Again, it’s all subjective and someone out there might love every single color I got, but I’d rather pay more per bottle knowing it’s a color I’d actually use. If you really don’t care what colors you get, then by all means this is a great deal and you should totally go for it!

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text: A beard trimmer with a built-in vacuum to keep the trimmings from collecting all over your sink is a good thing.  So when I decided it was time to replace my Wahl Vacu-Trim, which needed new blades and battery, I was sorry to see that Wahl apparently no longer makes that model.  It seems that the only vacuum beard trimmers available at this writing are the two models from Philips Norelco.  Seeing a good price here at amazon, I sprang for the Turbo model, which promised a little extra oomph.  Well, the trimmer works very well.  Better than the Wahl, I think.  To my surprise, I like the look it gives me at the closest setting -- if I didn't know better, I would say it makes an old geezer like me look younger.  I haven't had the problems others describe with the length comb changing settings on me.  The nicad battery life is acceptable -- I get a week of trims on my full beard and moustache at the Turbo setting.  When you see the red light come on after turning the unit off -- figure you have one more trim at Turbo speed.  Then it's time to recharge.  The unit is a little large, but not unwieldy.  I will be interested to see how well the blades hold up to the "ever-sharp" claim.  No lubrication needed either!  I am deducting one star because of failings in the instructions and packaging.  The instructions never tell you which side of the trimmer to hold against your face, and the T980 works the opposite of most other trimmers and shavers.  Most others have you hold the side with the buttons and logo against your face; when you use the length comb on the T980, however,you hold it with the buttons and logo on the side facing AWAY from your face.  I wonder how many of my fellow reviewers have been using this trimmer correctly, given this unconventional orientation.  Nowhere in the instructions do they show a clear photo of a guy using the trimmer.  There are two tiny, hard-to-follow line illustrations.  Adding insult to injury, the first time I called Norelco for help, the woman rep on the phone -- adding helpfully that she had never used a beard trimmer herself -- gave me the wrong answer.  Further experimentation -- and another call to a male rep -- confirmed that I was using the trimmer correctly.  The other problem with the packaging is the dreadful plastic blister pack holding the trimmer and accessories inside the box.  Any package requiring scissors to open needs to be redesigned with more eco- and user-friendly materials!!!  At any rate, the T980 is the current state-of-the-art in vacuum beard trimmers, and I recommend it, the packaging notwithstanding.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
Another design disaster from Philips. When the old Sonicare died I didn't feel like buying another since they still use Ni-Cad batteries which were state of the art in the Eisenhower era but no longer. This portable brush has the potential to be perfect. It requires no base, no cord, no electrical outlet. The batteries are always as fresh as you want. Use any AA batteries - rechargeable, disposable, lithium. Heck, even Ni-Cads if you can find any. It's perfect for traveling. It can be stored horizontally. It takes the regular Sonicare heads.

But its from Philips. I read all the reviews about it leaking so I was very, very careful. And when that didn't work, I tried running electrical tape around the bottom. To make a long story short, there are tiny channels that the water still gets in and after a week or so, the bottom cap wouldn't even stay on. A huge disappointment because I really liked it more than old Sonicare. Now I'm hooked on true cordless so I'll have to check the other brands.

product_title: Moroccan Argan Oil Shampoo, 8 Fl Oz - Smooths and Repairs - Sulfate Free - Natural - Imported from Morocco by Pure Body Naturals
review_text:
My hair type: naturally curly. Medium thickness/density. Medium/long length. Very fluffy i use no hair products. I usually blow dry it straight after a wash and it lasts for several days before I need to wash it again.

PROS:
- Smells nice. Smells like the essential oils. It's very subtle, not perfumey at all, and really I can't even smell it after my hair is dry.
- Gentle. It does not irritate my scalp
- Cleared up my dandruff/scalp rash from my previous shampoo that irritated my scalp and I was always itchy.
- Cleans well. Some natural shampoos don't seem to remove all natural oils or hair products, but this one does.
- Even without conditioner, I can get a comb through my hair. Not something I can say about most shampoos.

CONS:
- Still need conditioner. I thought with all the oils are nourishing that I wouldn't need a conditioner, but I do.
- My hair gets oily faster. When using this, I need to wash my hair more often. I used to get 4 days out of wash and now I barely get two since switching to this.
- My hair is extremely static-y! It doesn't matter how much conditioner, leave-ins or serums I apply, I cannot get the static to go away. I didn't have this problem before this shampoo.
- Price. It doesn't do anything for me that I can't get from a cheaper shampoo.

OVERALL: The fact that may hair gets greasy fast and and that it's so static-y tells me my hair is too dry. I need a moisturizing shampoo. When my hair/scalp is properly moisturized, it doesn't get greasy and I don't get flyaways. I thought this was a moisturizing shampoo with all the oils in it, but I guess they all just get rinsed away, and then some. I will not buy this again because I cannot stand static-y hair.

product_title: Moroccan Argan Oil Shampoo, 8 Fl Oz - Smooths and Repairs - Sulfate Free - Natural - Imported from Morocco by Pure Body Naturals
review_title: Such an amazing and gentle shampoo
review_text:
I think at last this is my Holy Grail! Having finally understood 8 years ago that regular shampoos were poison to my head, and first trying Wen, which was ok but expensive, then various non SLS shampoos, also just OK, and finally this which is truly in a class by itself- if you read the ingredients.
Very nice stuff, and so super gentle. The smell is pleasant and mild, does not smell like cheap perfume. My only complaint is that the product is very thick and the pump does not work.
I have used this now several times, every other day for the last 2 weeks and my hair is definitely improved. You could certainly use it every day if you so desired. I don't think conditioner adds anything to this, so I probably will use up the conditioner around my house and not re-purchase. This product makes a good 2 in one, for those who like to simplify their routine and de-clutter the bathroom. It is a little expensive, but much less expensive than many other products .You can save money by not washing your hair every day as you probably don't need to, unless you work a very dirty job. I used a quarter size dollop for my very thick, shoulder length hair, but you could probably use less. A bottle should last a couple of months or more.
It was the list of ingredients that truly sold me. This has a very gentle cleaner in it and Wen does not. I have suffered with bushy and coarse hair my entire life and this has actually helped. That being said, I have also been gradually shortening and layering my hair to accommodate its' natural flow.

review_title: A Really good Argan Oil Shampoo
review_text:
Man oh Man, this shampoo is AWESOME. I've been on the Argan Oil train for a while but never used a shampoo, only styling products courtesy of my hair stylist. I have LONGGGG hair and as such towards the end takes a beating from brushing, styling and just everyday aging. I wasn't due yet for my next appointment but new my hair needed some TLC so when I saw this product, I just had to give it a go. I stopped using shampoo with sulfates and other harsh chemicals over a year ago and have not regretted it, so seeing that this shampoo was so natural was a HUGE plus for me.

On to the shampoo, it's creamy and luxurious feeling and it smells a little like cologne...which is what my argan oil conditioner smelled like too..and then I realized that that's what argan oil smells like. I don't mind it, it was just a surprise from the usual floral or fruity undertones of shampoo. I'm not complaining. It's a good lather, and I love the ingredients. At the end of the wash before the conditioning my hair feels cleaner, I LOVE IT!

PROS: good lather, great ingredients, sulfate free, good quantity for price
OVERALL: AWESOME and my hair looks GREAT!
Also, while I did receive this product free or discounted, what I wrote is an UNBIASED review. If I didn't like aspects of a product, I'd let you know. I try to review products that I use/need for my lifestyle and also know what to expect. Further, I make sure I have a sound opinion before posting my review.

product_title: Braun 8000 360 Complete Foil/Cutter Block for Models 8995, 8985, 8975
review_title: I wish I owned the factory that makes these things...
review_text:
This is a factory replacement part for several models of Braun shavers, so it fits perfectly, and it works just like the original part.

The bad news is the price. You'll hold it in your hand and say, "How could this thing cost $30!?" Well, it just does; if you want the factory part, you have to pay the factory price. There is no after-market replacement.

Do you even need to replace the cutter assembly? Probably so. Obviously, if you dent the original by fumbling your shaver, you'll need a replacement. However, even with perfect care, the original cutter wears out in about 18 months. If you pop the foil cover off of your shaver, you can see why: The blades run back and forth against the foil cover, shearing off the whiskers that have protruded into the tiny holes and slots. Eighteen months of friction does the damage.

So, if you want the Braun shaver-- which, by the way is excellent-- then you just have to buy the parts needed to do the periodic maintenance. Life is like that sometimes...

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: No annoying charging, travel friendly, and more enviro-friendly if using Eneloop batteries than the other sonicare
review_text:
This works MUCH better than my old sonicare, which was a love-hate relationship that started out so well until the battery life diminished which really makes one resent the ugly charging dock even more, not to mention traveling with the beast. Worst of all, I felt environmental guilt knowing products with built in batteries often get moved overseas for peasants in Asia to mine at a tech waste salvage dump.

This battery operated sonicare is better because:
* It doesn't have the, "where do we hide the ugly charging dock in our bathroom?" problem.
* It lasts much longer between charges because batteries last WAY LONGER than the rechargeable sonicare built-in batteries and Eneloop rechargeable batteries last much longer than disposable batteries.
* It is way more travel friendly to not have to remember to bring a bulky annoying charging dock (and who needs one more thing to remember).
* It's more green to use this product with reusable Eneloop batteries, as you're not stuck having to buy another rechargeable toothbrush once the built in battery stops being super.

I really hope more environmentally responsible companies follow this route and opt to make products with an alternative to built in batteries, so products will last longer and there will be less waste; it's great to be able to use my own rechargeable Eneloop batteries that are always charged and ready for use.
