product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: It sucks. And that's a good thing!
review_text:
I owned another Norelco beard trimmer with a vacuum in it ... until my wife broke it by knocking it off the shelf. But now I'm glad she did. On the old one, the vacuum was fairly useless because just as much hair ended up in the sink and all over the blade as in the catcher bin. Maybe more.

But the T980 Turbo (and don't all guys love stuff with "Turbo" in the description?) does the job. Yes, I know it has two settings: Turbo on and Turbo off. But I see no reason to use it with Turbo off because then it's just like the old underpowered version. But with Turbo on it collects nearly all those little hairs. (Some get away, but many fewer.)

Some people say that the Turbo is too loud, which is why they offer an option I suppose, but in our house the bathroom is far enough away and well-insulated enough that no one can hear it running full blast.

One caveat: It's better to trim the beard dry not wet. Remember to trim it before you get in the shower because when the hair is wet the vacuum still has trouble collecting the hairs, even on Turbo. Plus showering washes any remaining trimmings away. Yes, this may be self-evident to some of you, but I hadn't thought of it before. Keep in mind I'm doing this before morning coffee.

So no more little hairs all over my daughter after daddy kisses and snuggles her. I like the T980 trimmer.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
Like many of the reviewers here, I was actually seeking an overall body hair trimmer when I came across the Norelco T980. After several months of continuous use (as a body hair trimmer), I have not been disappointed. Here are some of the highlights:

* The blades remain sharp, never requiring further sharpening, nor rinsing or oiling. The blades have also never pulled any hairs, making for a pain-free trim
* The vacuum component works really well to collect and house the trimmings, keeping the bathroom sink free of stray hairs
* Ease of use to change through nine different blade lengths, without needing to swap for extra components
* Turbo button to boost the speed of the blades is a nice feature
* Sideburn accessory is very handy for keeping the 'burns neatly trimmed
* The internal battery holds a charge for a remarkably long time
* Travel pouch and charger make for an easy-to-travel-with item

Keep in mind that if your intended use is for a body hair trimmer, the Norelco T980 does not shave the skin completely smooth -- as that is not in its intended design. But if you are seeking a trimmer to crop and maintain body hair, especially facial hair, this is an ideal tool to have.

Tapers slid in easily, the pain subsided within minutes, and my ears felt ready to stretch up in size within days (though I still waited two weeks per size). I haven't noticed ANY unpleasant smell, despite expecting and being on the lookout for it.

My ears are even stretching into nearly perfectly rounded openings. This stuff made a HUGE difference and I wholeheartedly recommend it.

review_text:
I am a fan.

I am one that likes to avoid shampooing my very long, thick and curly hair, usually just sticking to conditioning. I decided to give this a try as a discounted sample. It arrived on a very cold day and it was very thick to the point I thought the pump might be broken. As it turns out, it really does have a high oil content that solidifies in the cold, as olive and coconut will do.
I was happy to see it was not creating tons of lather but was freshening up my hair and rinsing it clean. I followed with an argan oil deep conditioner and then brushed out. Without even a leave in and no product, my hair is fairly smooth with great shine and looks healthy. I have a bit of frizz but very little considering no products I usually have to use to tame, presentable even without them.
It has a clean scent that isn't coming across as a chemical creation at the Glade air freshener lab but soft and natural. My 8 year old son was laying next to me and told me my hair smelled good, he's a fan.

review_title: Not for all hair types but...

Im sure this product works great with other hair types but My hair is sort of on the African American side because Im mixed.

are my own.

I'll stick to my current regular for now

product_title: Meeteasy Dental Cleaner Tool Kit - Dental Care for Adult - 100% Proven Safe
review_text:
So I saw a family member of mines teeth were so bad it literally scared me for them. They had so much dental calculus you almost couldn’t see the tooth/teeth anymore. It was just enveloping the teeth so much.
So I quickly went online in search of solutions for at home for dental calculus and found this and ordered it for same day delivery. I went to work as soon as it came.

At first I wasn’t getting anything & didn’t think it was going to work. But then I was SHOCKED with seeing it work. It’s kind of scary at first seeing chunks and pieces just chip and come off and hearing them break off. So if you have dental calculus this bad too be prepared for that mentally but if yours is that bad too it’s best to have someone help you cause you can’t really see it yourself.

I worked on their teeth for over and hour and was able to get probably 80-85% off which I wasn’t expecting at all. I mean I was hoping but it was something I’d never done before and never used this product either so I didn’t know what to expect but I was seriously able to get most of it off in a little over an hour.

One thing I will say about the device is for some reason it will randomly turn off (and no I’m not talking about the auto shut off after 5mins) it really does just turn off it seems when it thinks it’s stuck or something. It’s annoying but not too bad but I thought I’d mention it.

I also used the manual tools it came with too to try and get more control for picking the calculus off in sensitive spots and they worked too :) I found them useful for going in between teeth.

So far I’m REALLY glad I bought this. Worth the try if you’re struggling with SEVERE dental calculus because it does work.

Their thoughts on it’s performance is now their teeth feel rough but that’s because it’s not been perfectly scraped and not finished being cleaned so there’s now rough calculus instead of a “smooth surface” of HUGE dental calculus deposits.

I also bought a special toothpaste to pair with it that softens plaque so hopefully that will help too.

Good luck and I hope this was helpful :)

They didn’t want to share pictures but hopefully my description was helpful.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: This is the Sonicare model to buy.  Seriously.
review_text:
This is fantastic. Free yourself from Philips' non-replaceable-battery tyranny! In their high end toothbrushes, Philips doesn't use Li-Ion or even NiMh rechargeable batteries. They use cheap Ni-Cd batteries that no one else has used for 20 years. You can't even buy Ni-Cd rechargeables if at your local retailer if you wanted to, because they are so lousy nobody wants them. And to top it off, they make the cheap Ni-Cd batteries non-user-replaceable.

This means when the NiCd batteries die (won't hold a charge), and they will, SOON, your Sonicare toothbrush is useless.

Unless you have this one.

It's just like the other Sonicare toothbrushes, except you can put your own rechargeables in it. I use Sanyo Eneloop. They run the toothbrush for about 6-8 weeks (compared to 2-3 weeks for a new Sonicare). Then you just pop them out, recharge them, and pop them back in. And the Eneloops, because they are a modern battery, will survive over 1500 recharges. And if the batteries DO die, replace them, and this toothbrush will go on forever.

I'd fallen victim to Philips' trap twice before, when I had to trash two Sonicare's due to failed NiCd batteries.

Now I am free from their battery tyranny. All their toothbrushes should be made with replaceable batteries this way, and the fact that they're not is just to force you to buy new ones (otherwise they would use modern battery technology.)

Don't worry about other reviews saying this toothbrush shorts out. It's perfectly sturdy and reliable. Just don't drop it in the water. It doesn't matter if the brush end gets wet, it's only the battery end that can't be submerged. Unless you plan to use this toothbrush while swimming, this is the one for you.

Best Sonicare toothbrush I've ever had, an the last one I will need to buy.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text: My first impression at taking my $44 trimmer out the box, was "Gee, this feels cheap." But I was impressed by the vacuum (which does collect a good 80% of the hair) and thought I'd try it out for the 60 day money-back time period. That time has come to an end and I've decided the nifty vac is just not enough. The huge trimmer head makes it impossible to cut evenly under the nose. Also, the "Flexing Contour Guide" requires one to push the shaver fairly hard against the face for an even shave. review_text: Compact, powerful and convenient. Light enough to let you control the tedious drilling around the cuticles. Shanks fit snug and easy to insert. It did a good job and this was hard gel to drill out but I'm not discouraged. These bits aren't designed to last forever but I'm new to doing my own nails so oozing happens. If you're a pro, you probably won't abuse the bit like I did!! Still recommend this product!!! AND, the free travel manicure set is beautiful and packaged in a nice, hard snap-click case. There were items that I've never received in a set like this.

review_text: I have curly hair I need a diffuser to dry it. I’m traveling extensively in Europe and wasn’t sure what I was going to do. Normal diffusers take up so much space in your luggage but this takes up almost no space and it works fantastic! I highly recommend it.

product_title: Collapsible Hair Diffuser by The Curly Co. with The Curly Co. Satisfaction Guarantee
review_text: This is a good product.  it actually fits my Sedu 4000i, which is a big plus.  Also love that it collapses to store.  I have thick curly hair (3A and 3B), and so i was excited to try this.  So far i am having two issues.  One, it tends to collapse to smaller size during use, esp when i get it closer to my head. Not sure that's a good thing.  Two, and this may be an issue of me not using it properly, it seems to make my hair too curly!  I like having the longer thicker big curls, rather than the tighter smaller and collier curls - and when i air dry, i usually have big thick curls.  But with this diffuser, i end up with smaller tighter curls, which is not exactly what i want.  As a result, my hair overall ends up looking another 2-3 inches shorter because the curls are tighter and smaller.  So if your hair is wavy and you want more curl definition, this might be great - but for me, going from curly to almost coils/kinky is not a plus.  But on the plus side, it does give me good volume at the top of my head and the crown.

review_text:

All bottles are fresh and in tact. I was also nervous about the colors being chosen at random, but there were no repeats and only 1 color I will probably never use (tan and due to very pale skin). Of the other 5, I really like 4 and the 5th I will probably use in seasonally in fall (orange).
I'm currently wearing this product from a purchase at a local store. It goes on really well, dries fairly quickly, has nice pigmentation (currently wearing a dark purple), and lasts a long time. Every 4 or 5 days, I'll buff down the shine and throw on a new coat of color and top coat to refreshed, but it's not really necessary as it still looks fine. More preventative in my case. review_title: YOU NEED THESE IN YOUR LIFE
review_text: Great clips, although the ones I received were in a much different color scheme than the ones pictured. Mine are translucent pastel colors (some light gray and white). Didn't really care either way, however. These are so much better than traditional jawclips in terms of getting a grab on your hair. These clips are intended for hair-styling purposes more so than using IN a hairstyle if you get what I mean. review_text:
We've had this shampoo for a while so I can testify to the longer term effects: it's really great!

I let my teenage son use this once before he decided it was his and is now obsessed with how soft it makes his hair. 500 times hearing "feel how soft my hair is" is all the proof I need on that aspect... yes, this makes your hair super soft.
I assume that is due to the argan oil, of course, but this also has avocado, jojoba, and coconut oils which also contribute to soft healthy hair. In addition to the oils, there are some other chemicals like Cocamidopropyl betaine which is a surfactant and foaming agent. That doesn't matter to the average person (only matters to someone with serious allergies and dermatitis) and there are less surfactants and similar ingredients than the average shampoo found at Walmart which is good.

I'm very happy with what it's done to my son's bleached and dyed hair, and to my own dry brittle hair as well.

I received this free in return for my review.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
I have been using the other battery powered brand for over a decade, and decided to try the Sonicare Xtreme. This model cleans better, and is easier to use. As far as the leakage - the bottom is sealed by an "O-ring" (black plastic ring on the bottom). To keep this seal intact and working, smear a SMALL amount of petroleum jelly on the O-ring all around. This, plus some common sense care has kept our two Sonicare toothbrushes dry and corrosion free.

Update - We have been using the Sonicare Xtreme for almost two years, and here are some tips: Clean the toothbrush head with the head pointing down under the hottest water out of the faucet. Then dry the head shaft and back of the head with the head pointing down. List will eliminate any water seeping into the head base. The head normally last two months, and with standard use, the batteries should last the same.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: Great brush for short money. Perfect for travel.
review_text:
This sonicare operates like all the others, it just doesn't include the expensive rechargable battery and charger like the more expensive models do. Because it operates on AA batteries, the unit is susceptible to some water entry if one is careless.

It shouldn't be necessary to tell people not to get electric appliances wet, but apparantly it is. The handle should never be exposed to water. It is not submersible. The only portion of the entire device that should get wet is the brush-head. Remove the brush-head after every use, wash it thoroughly, and dry it. Wipe the handle dry. That is it. Take care of it like an electric hand mixer. You remove and clean the mixing pieces, you don't dunk the motor assembly in the sink. You wipe it clean. No water means no corrosion.

The directions clearly state that the motor assembly/handle is not water-proof. Others have found that a #33 o-ring seals the battery compartment very well. It is an excellent, inexpensive preventative solution to water entering the battery compartment.

Phillips does not include the following warning and disclaimer, but perhaps they should:

Item is not idiot proof.

review_text:
I purchased this after reading reviews, however, I don't agree with some things, so I have returned it after one use.
First, the buttons are on the handle, so I kept accidentally pressing them as I was using it. (Also, it is in Celsius, so I had to convert temp to Fahrenheit.)
Second, it gets EXTREMELY hot and the coated bristles DO NOT protect your skin from burning. I felt like I should wear hot pads on my hands! Even the back side of the "brush" was very hot to the touch!
Third, the heat element does not get close enough to the hair near your scalp, so there is obvious difference where the "straightened hair" starts and stops. This makes for a lot of work.
Next, the rubbery coating just stuck to my hair, causing it to pull and pinch. Ouch!
And lastly, only one hour after use, my hair started to curl at the ends. (My hair can always keep form, as I straighten it everyday.)
This product has failed in so many ways. This is not what I expected and I would not recommend it.

review_title: great for not having a dentist
review_text: I am currently living away from my regular dentist and my last dental appointment was cancelled. Because I missed an appointment, I decided to buy this product to keep my teeth extra clean aside from my regular brushing/flossing/rinsing. The only reason I am giving 4/5 stars is because I did not receive a scraper tool. The tartar remover has multiple vibrating settings to use. When you turn the tool on, you can use it against your teeth to remove tartar. I don't have that much tartar build up, but it does remove plaque that is sitting on your teeth. I am only using this because I don't have a dentist available to me currently. If you do have a dentist, just go to them!!! They go to school and are trained to use better tools than this in order to keep your teeth healthy. Yes you can try to do it on your own with this tool, but this is not comparable to a dentist. If you use this the wrong way, you will cause damage to your gums and enamel. OTHERWISE this product is okay to use periodically when you want to get the extra extra crud off your teeth that a spin toothbrush may not get off

review_text:
Save money in the long run by buying a model with a charger.My husband and I have had these brushes for about a year and a half and are down to replacing the batteries about once a week.
Mine died within a couple months of use. It would just keep shutting off during use even though the batteries were new. I called Sonicare, they had me take it apart and clean the contacts with rubbing alcohol, that didn't help, so they sent a replacement. The new one started doing the same thing within a few weeks, called again, again they sent a replacement. Their customer service is actually pretty good and they stand behind their products, but it gets old replacing batteries and replacing brushes.
Overall, I like the performance of the brush, it does a great job, and my teeth really do feel much cleaner.
I just ordered a set of two with chargers from Amazon, they are more initially but I know we will save money in the long run by not having to use 4 AA batteries every week.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
I have had a Sonicare for many years, and it was the rechargeable type. It lasted a total of 8 years, but I hear the newer ones only last about 3 years, so I chose THIS battery operated brush, and have had it for 3 months now. I read ALL the reviews herein, and was wondering why so many reviewers complained about the base not being water resistant. I have been brushing MY teeth for over 60 years now, and do NOT brush them underwater. I have no clue why someone would want to brush either underwater, OR in the shower.

When this brush is used as a toothbrush, then there is no reason why it should get water in the handle. The battery compartment is located at the opposite end of the brushes, and if used normally, rinsed off, then dried with your towel, there is no way water can get into the compartment.

I LOVE my brush..it stops automatically AFTER 2 minutes of brushing, and IF you use it for two minutes each time, your teeth will really be clean. My dentist tells me that my gums and teeth appear more healthy than many others they have seen, and I owe it all to my sonicare brush. BTW, I only brush ONCE per day in the morning AFTER breakfast, so if YOU use it more often than that, your mouth and gums will be healthier than MINE!!

Light

review_text:
I've used a Sonicare toothbrush since 1998 because I have problems with my gums. The Sonicare has kept my gums healthy.

I travel a lot and it is - more often than not - a hassle to take my Sonicare with me. But no more! This travels so much easier and takes up substantially less room. Because it charges and operates via batteries versus an electrical outlet, it also saves counter space.

I've only had it for a week, but it seems to be a bit more powerful than my other Sonicares. Even though it doesn't have all the bells and whistles of the more expensive versions it cleans my teeth very well. So far, I'm very, very pleased.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Shifts beard length setting without warning
review_text:
My T980 does almost everything perfectly: it holds a charge for weeks; its vacuum reduces the number of trimmed hairs around the sink by about 70%; it feels wonderful and it works quickly.

However, my T980 does NOT stay at the level I set it at. If I don't firmly grip the length setting wheel it will jump from, say, a 5 to a 3 -- as it did this morning -- embarrassing me either by giving me a patchy trim or by forcing me to shorten my beard length.

This problem doesn't seem to be a result of the way I'm, say, holding the trimmer -- I used the [[ASIN:B0001HYL0M T765]] for four years without having this problem -- but rather a flaw in the trimmer itself. From these reviews, it seems like only a few of the T980s have this problem; still, you might want to try the [[ASIN:B000FED5D0 T780]], which doesn't seem to have this problem -- I wish I had.

Update 3/12/08: Make me look like a fool once, shame on me; make me look like a fool twice, shame on you.

I've used this trimmer about 12 times since writing this review, and by a combination of duct tape, a pinch grip, and a good deal of vigilance I had been able to avoid too many embarrassing shifts in beard length.

...until this morning, when it shifted silently from a 5 (Late Winter Academic Beard) to 3 (Peach Fuzz) in mid-shave. Two options: shave my entire beard to a 3, which is inappropriate for my face type, or look deranged because half of my face is at 5 and half is at 3.

I threw my T980 in the garbage ten minutes ago.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Three years of use and still EXCELLENT
review_text:
I've used the T980 for a year and a half and it still works great.

I've tried several trimmers and a couple that claimed a vacuum ablility, most failed miserably. Most others also felt like junk compared to the T980's construction.

The T980's vacuum actually DOES work very well...with a couple of caveats. You must switch it to turbo mode to be effective, and if you're trimming more than a light amount of hair you need to dump out the cut hair once or twice (which is easy to do with the way it is made) for the vacuum to still work effectively.
Great quality product and the storage pouch is such a nice simple touch but so very handy.

UPDATE 2/2012: 3 years of use and still works well. Battery quit holding a charge a month ago, but that was not unexpected. One reason I bought this model was that it will work corded even after the battery quits holding a charge.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text: I had a Norelco trimmer that lasted several years and loved it. The main reason I chose the T980 over the T765 is that it can be operated from the plug. However, the comb is difficult to re-attach after cleaning and ultimately busted completely after less than 2 months of use. The vacuum is a nice feature but the receptacle is not secure, sometimes sending hair flying everywhere. The worst part is the vacuum feature makes it impossible to use the bare blade to trim edges; you have to use a separate attachment for this. The button to operate the "turbo" feature (totally unnecessary) is extremely cheap and came off the first time I pressed it. Norelco / Philips trimmers are definitely the way to go, but don't shell out the extra money for the shoddily designed extra features. Get the T765, I just did as a replacement for this piece of dung.

product_title: Moroccan Argan Oil Shampoo, 8 Fl Oz - Smooths and Repairs - Sulfate Free - Natural - Imported from Morocco by Pure Body Naturals
review_title: An Honestly Cruelty Free Hair Treat!
review_text: This shampoo is brilliant! (Bought & used it with the Art Naturals Argan Hair Mask afterwards.) I have fine, thin, color treated hair & wanted a cruelty free, NO animal testing, phosphate free product. I am thrilled at the experience. No drying brittle effect, nice moisturizing feeling with an actual total cleanse of my hair. And any product that gives me that "swing" in my hair is a miracle cure, as my hair is baby fine & always full of static & very fly-away.  I am totally hooked! You can't go wrong trying this Pure Body Naturals product. (Unexpected side effect: the aroma is AMAZING! I have had multiple folks wiggle their nose & ask about my shampoo because of the aroma.  I can't do it justice, it's a nutty, natural smell that has an unexpected aromatherapeutic benefit. This wouldn't make me buy a product, but as an added surprise it's lovely!) I have already ordered a second bottle for our second bathroom.  You need so little it will last a while, but my whole household wants to use it now so we are all stocking up! product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I scoured the net looking for the perfect beard trimmer to trim my beard that I brough back from Iraq. I didn't want to look like a terrorist, so I needed a trimmer to keep my beard looking civilized. I read the reviews here and was prepared for a somewhat weak vacuum- even on turbo. No big deal- I wanted results, and the vacuum was just a perk anyway. It caught maybe half the hair on turbo, so whoopie.

Well, I should have paid more attention to the negative reviews! I was careful not to hold the trimmer by the click wheel to avoid accidentally going down a setting... I did that once and clicked from a 5 to a 4. I liked the 4 better anyway, so stuck with that. I happily trimmed to a 4 once a week (sometimes twice to clean it up) for the last couple months and it worked well, until just a couple of days ago when the setting slipped all the way down to 1 when I was in the middle of shaving! I went from a nice beard to the 5 o-clock shadow look! I AM FURIOUS!

There needs to be some sort of setting lock that prevents it from just slipping and ruining your beard! How hard would that be? Just build the dial with a notch you can slide a bar into in order to lock it!

Until they build this with a locking device, avoid it, or you could lose your hard-earned beard- just like I did!

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
When my old beard trimmer conked out after a half dozen years, I wanted a nice new one. Not the clunker my wife had purchased for me six years ago that pulled hairs, kept my sink a mess, and looked cheap. So I typed in Google, "What is the best beard trimmer?" On two of three sites I checked, the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer was tops.

What sold me, was the video of one reviewer actually using the trimmer and explaining all of its functions and how to use it. As an aside, the Amazon reviews were helpful as well - so when I was shaving and turned the trimmer on its side, I was not surprised when hairs fell out of the vaccum trap.

That being said, the beard trimmer worked just as I had hoped. I look forward to taking time out once a week to trim my beard. The guard feels good against my skin and the hairs are all evenly cut. I haven't had a pulled hair yet. The shaper works well, giving nice clean lines. And the vaccum works great with the beard trimmer and guard - 99% of hair winds up in the vaccum chamber. The pieces are easy to clean and adjust.

Negatives and these are minor andonly have to do with the vaccum. Mind you, if there was no vaccum my sink would be filled with black hairs, so having any type of vaccum is great. The negatives are: 1. if you turn your hand too far over, the hairs will start to spill out - that's happened twice in the eight times I've used it so far. And it was only a little. 2. One other thing, where the beard meets my hairline just above the ear, I've found the guard obstructs the view a bit so it's hard to see where to stop. review_title: The customer service was also, I might add, very friendly, helpful, and quick to respond!
review_text:
I am actually pretty happy with this brush for the almost week I've been using it! The bristles are good and stiff, so they were able to get through most of the layers of my hair, and it does a seriously terrifying good job of volumizing. Or floofing, in my case. Easily remedied with a little spritzing with water. Or not, if you're into floof.

There are a few cons to the brush, but nothing that should stop you from buying it, should you be looking for a nice brush to give yourself a nice scalp massage/shine to your hair/add volume... and other such things. There IS a smell that comes from the rubber bedding that the bristles rest in from using recycled rubber. However, if you let the brush air out after unboxing, the wafting odor goes away. You'd literally have to stick your nose in the bristles to be able to smell the rubber scent again, and it doesn't brush the smell into your hair. Believe me, I've done just that, much to the angst and irritation of my poor snoot.

The bristles are juuuuust slightly shorter than I like, but it still grazes the scalp enough to give some nice stimulation (a pretty darn good itchin' relief) to your scalp. I know most people are used to a brush giving the full on scritchin' experience to your scalp, but I find that usually a lot of that, no matter how delicious it feels, usually makes my hair uber oily.

Other than those very little things, it's a good boars bristle brush to invest in, I think!

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: Best bargain in the Sonicare line
review_text:
UPDATE: 18 months later, still working perfectly.
-------------------
While there appear to be people who have had trouble with these, I have had mine for over 6 months now with no problems. I should note, however, that I took the following precautions:

1. Sealed the seams in inside of the brush-head socket end of the handle with a thin smear of silicone caulk.
2. Applied extra plumber's silicone grease (available at hardware/home center stores) to the O-ring on the battery cap.
3. After use, I remove the brush-head, so the unit can dry better between uses.

I do not know if these precautions were necessary -- but they were easy, and the unit has run faultlessly. The battery compartment remains dry, there is no sign of corrosion anywhere.

Also note that Philips offers a 2 year warranty on the device, although I am sure that the specifics of the warranty are probably annoying.

NOTE that the free batteries supplied with the unit are fairly priced -- you are better off just discarding them immediately and using fresh alkaline AAs.

product_title: Segbeauty empty bottle 160083
review_title: I love it--and so does my parrot!
review_text:
This is probably the best household item I have found in years. It produces an ultra-fine, fog-like mist reminiscent of a steamy summer day-- but intentional. First, it is extremely well made of hard, high-impact plastic. It was a bit hard to open and close initially, but now it's easier. As I note below, the tight fit is essential to how it works, and also probably causes a problem if the wrong kind of water is used.l

I have naturally curly hair, and it's perfect for a tune-up in the evening or on a day when I don't wash my hair. More importantly, my little rescue parrot loves it. This bird refused to bathe for more than a year after I adopted him, and I tried everything, from showers in the sink to bowls of water and a regular sprayer (which he hated and flew away from). He loves this, and as soon as he sees it, he flies to his cage, fluffs up, and waits for me to mist him.

I have read reviews saying that the water gets stinky, so it should be emptied and refilled frequently. Even the manufacturer suggests that. I think the problem is that the sprayer seals so tightly, it creates an anaerobic environment in which "swampy" bacteria that don't need oxygen will thrive. So if you're using tap water or well water that contain bacteria (all water does, and normally they are not a problem), this is what causes the stink. My solution is to use previously boiled water in it. I always keep a kettle of boiled water on the stove, for use in cooking and such, and it works great in the Segbeauty mister. I filled it with the water over a week ago, and refilled it today after birdie bath time. It was still fresh. So the problem is not the fault of the sprayer; it is the result of how well it's made, and how tightly it seals.

I have not yet used it on my plants, but I'm sure it will be perfect for them also. Overall, a great product, which I give my highest recommendation.

review_title: Good trimmer; battery holding up well
review_text:
Purchased the T980 trimmer in January (is now mid-Oct), and it has worked well. This replaced an earlier Norelco whose battery finally gave up (+ it got dropped a couple of times...), and - for once - the replacement actually seems better than the original.
Unit shipped with a decent (not great) flip-cover travel case, large enough for the trimmer & charger, and with a small net pouch for the narrow trimming head (which has not been used). Have also never needed the "Turbo" mode.
The "vacuum" feature on the T980 works somewhat better than the earlier unit: it does not catch everything, but certainly captures most of the clippings. The flip open door to empty the contents is convenient.
Don't care for the hard body, but there is a nice rubber ring (used to change the cutting depth) that makes a good grip point. Find it difficult to read the "zoom" - that is, cutting depth - setting from certain angles / lighting conditions, but this is not a major problem.
After some 9 months of use, this unit still looks great, cuts great, and has a pleasingly long battery life. It lacks a multi-LED charge indicator, but does have a "Low" battery warning light (+ a Charge light) & the unit will still run for several beard trimmings once the warning light comes on. All-in-all, a good purchase.

review_text:
I used to have a Sonicare a long time ago. You know, the VERY expensive plug-in one. Yes, it worked like a dream (just like they say). My DDS could tell the difference. But having another thing to plug-in in our tiny bathroom was a hassle and after about a year the charger was mucked up beyond control. Most embarrassing! Years went by and new dental problems arose. After going through the joys of a root plaining, I was looking for a new Sonicare. I saw this one and loved that it was battery operated and had a smaller head. I didn't need all the bells and whistles on the other models. Just the auto-timer.

The first one that came died in 2 days. WAHHH! Amazon kicked butt and sent us a replacement right away. We've had the new one for a month now and it's still going strong. I think the first one was just defective.

It does go through batteries pretty quick, so I highly suggest you get re-chargeable batteries. My DDS noticed a difference within the month. It's totally worth it, and a great price! It ends up being cheaper than the disposable electric brushes we were using.

A good family brush for all ages. Easy to use, even for kids.

All in all a decent trimmer but could be quieter and it would be nice if the vacume was more effetive and worked with the neck trimmer.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
Look - Life ain't perfect - neither are we. We increasingly live in a time where YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR.

First Premise: Anyone who still manually brushes is asking for trouble - the environment ain't what it used to be and groundwater poisoning is a big part of the story of deregulation. I've spent thousands and hundreds of hours in dentists' chairs - currently much of the lower left quandrant of my smile is cerac - and I brushed faithfully daily for decades - up and down brushing with daily flossing (no matter how intense)does not cut it. Thus, the incredible evolution in electronic toothbrushes over the past decade.

Second Premise: AC Outlet Rechargable is better and the motor will last twice as long (assuming proper care). However, Battery Run is FAR MORE CONVENIENT. I have found that with proper maintenance - these units last approximately two years. Proper care means unscrewing the brush head and cleaning and drying the connection at least monthly if not weekly. After a month of brush use (or thereabouts you'll find alot of gunk - mostly from you and your tube of toothpaste - inside there - I use q-tips and paper towels to clean it) Proper care means checking the batteries for corrosion as well as charge when the unit slows down. If you find signs of corrosion in the - clean it out thoroughly. For checking batteries - use a simple aa/AAA/C battery tester - an invaluable tool to these days.

Conclusion: You spend about $10 bucks a year on the unit and $10 to use two brush heads per year as well. After two years, if it's broke or the motor has slowed down significantly - even when new batteries are installed - chuck it. If you've got the money, $20 a year for a new unit annually is not really a whole lot compared to what dental work costs these days. Actually, mine unit is going on three years old and is working fine - although battery life does seem shorter.

review_text: My wife bought this initially, but couldn't get use to the vibration, so she asked me if I wanted to try it. Having had stains on my teeth for a long time, I thought why not. product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
I've used this toothbrush, the essence 5600, and the flexcare r910. The flexcare is more powerful and has better brush heads (it also avoids the problem of having water trapped inside the brush and growing mold), but it's also far more expensive. The essence 5600 is a waste of money in my opinion as it has the same performance as this toothbrush, but suffers from a shoddy li-on battery that dies after about a year or so of use. This avoids the battery problem by using replaceable AA batteries and lasts quite a while on each replacement.

The only major con is with the brush head design. There is a a gap between the brush body and head, and this gap tends to fill with water after use. This unfortunately leads to black mold growing in the cavity. It's easy to avoid this by simply unscrewing the head after brushing and rinsing out the cavity, but it's an annoyance nonetheless.

All in all, this is a great cheap way to get the benefits of sonicare.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Pretty good, but too many bells and whistles.
review_text:
This trimmer is pretty good. Trims well. Mostly used for personal body grooming. It is easily cleanable with most important parts just pulling off. The price is fair.
The battery capacity is excellent. Have used a half dozen times without need for recharging. Cordless feature is great to trim in shower and not make a mess in bathroom.
The bells and whistles such as turbo power and vacuum chamber are more annoying than useful. The vacuum chamber fills really fast and if you have black hair you can not distinguish it against the groomer's black body color despite what the advertisements claim. When the chamber is full cutting ability drops dramatically. The work around is just pull off or keep open the chamber door while grooming.
I have not figured out what turbo is for, sure the blades move faster and the device is louder but since we're triming hair and not a full lawn of grass it seems pretty pointless.
The power button is very sensitive and an inadvertant flick of a finger easily shuts off (or turns on trimmer). Not a disaster but slightly annoying.
As far as reliability it has lasted longer than my previous Panasonic so that's a plus.

product_title: Listerine Pump for 1.5 or 1 Liter Bottles (1 Pump)
review_title: Works as described.  Use taller 3 oz cups with pump.
review_text:
Bought the pump for my elderly mother-in-law who has difficulty lifting the larger size mouthwash bottles and opening the caps. Works fine for our needs.

Pros:
Fits Listerine Zero 1.5L bottles. Can't comment on whether it fits other brands or sizes but based on previous reviews, sounds like it doesn't fit other brands.
Makes it easier to dispense product vs. lifting and pouring out product.
Inexpensive solution - I paid $6.50 with free Prime shipping.

Cons:
Pump dispenses additional product as it releases/comes back up so be prepared for this and keep your cup beneath the spout the entire time until it has reset to the starting position.
Spout tip is angled outwards so place your cup directly underneath the tip to keep product in cup.
Pump flow is strong so definitely use a taller larger cup or you'll get splash back. I'd recommend the standard 3 oz Dixie type cups. I bought the tiny 3/4 oz paper medicine type cups thinking that would work but they're a tad too difficult to use with the pump.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
Been using this brush now for a few months now - love using it! Cleans like crazy, but isn't too harsh on my gums or anything.

One thing I've discovered though is that it needs *good* batteries. When I put new, but cheap, batteries in, it acted like they were already dead. I actually changed the brush head assembly out too early because I thought something was wrong with it, when in fact putting *good* batteries in solved it.

Note that when there isn't enough juice, it doesn't slow down, it just randomly turns off.

Love the brush overall though :)

EDIT
After reading some of the other reviews, thought I'd mention a few things.

I minimize/prevent water damage to this by:

1. Use the minimum amount of water that I need
2. Shake the bristles after use and wipe off the whole thing with a paper towel
3. Store it immediately, don't leave it laying on a wet counter or anything. I don't do anything particularly special for storage - just put it in a drinking glass on the counter with our other toothbrushes. Obviously I make sure there isn't a pool of water in the glass.

Just what I do - seems to work for me.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: The best value in the Sonicare line
review_text:
With Amazon now selling this directly for < $20 this is the absolute best value in the entire Sonicare line. You get the same drive, the same brush head compatibility, 2 min timer and the ability to use your own rechargeable batteries. 5 years ago I purchased a Sonicare Elite 7300; the internal NiCad battery eventually died and the unit is not designed to swap out the battery. I tried, but ended up damaging the rubber molding and had a lot of difficulty finding a comparable battery that didn't require paying a high shipping cost. I eventually purchased the E3000 on a whim at a retail store for nearly twice what it sells for on Amazon nowadays and started using the newer low self discharge NiMH batteries. I get about a month of usage before I have to charge the batteries. And when the batteries finally start losing their capacity -- they haven't yet in 2 years -- I don't have to worry about performing major surgery on my toothbrush.

I'm not sure I understand the water seepage/contacts/failure issues. I own 2 E3000s now, one for travel and one for home, and have used them both for 2+ years now. Neither have failed. I take care not to rinse the base of the unit under running water and I don't leave it sitting in a pool of water or anything. I definitely see the potential for failure as nothing but a plastic cap and a rubber gasket protect the AA batteries from potential moisture, but I think standard, common sense can prevail here. Let me stress -- I do not baby this thing. I use it daily in a bathroom that gets very humid during showers and summer weather (no exhaust fan and no central air conditioning). I clean it every usage under running water and I don't dry it off afterwards. I also have done the same types of things with 2 different E3000 units and have used them for over 2 years now and they have worked perfectly from day one.

Highly recommended. I would actually feel comfortable recommending this over a higher-end Sonicare that was discounted to be within a similar price range as this unit. Being able to use your own rechargeable batteries is simply way too powerful of a feature since that seems to be the limiting factor in keeping this brushes for the long haul.

review_title: Scares the cat, but Over all, pretty impressed
review_text:
I am a firm believer in facial hair, but often try to avoid that shaggy look. The cat mistakes my face and starts nuzzling a little too enthusiastically.

I have trimmed with scissors, rasors, the old cip on guard trimmers and the grandfather of this trimmer which just recently died after 7 years of service (not bad Norelco!). Like its grandfather, the click adjustable guard is the single best reason to buy one of these trimmers.

It does struggle a little bit with longer bushy hairs (as most do), but works like a champ when keeping previously trimmed ones in check. Clean up is fairly easy, plus this one looks really cool.

The only thing I am not inlove with is, and that it has a super rechargeable battery which will have to be removed one day and recycled appropriately. Replacement batteries and recycling can be a challenge, and I'd almost rather just have a corded mode. Otherwise I totally love it.

The vacuum and turbo vacuum featured on this model are an interesting new rendition, and they do a fair job capturing most (not all) of the shavings. Admittedly though I have only used the turbo vacuum on my person as I cant imagine a situation when you'd want less suckage... except to make this more stealthy when you have a few beers and decide its time to shave the cat... having done so, the cat is now afeard of both the trimmer and any other vacuum noises. Even a long drag though a straw now makes Mitsy Boots nervous. My sink drain and my wife are quite grateful with the vacuum, the cat not so much.

product_title: Collapsible Hair Diffuser by The Curly Co. with The Curly Co. Satisfaction Guarantee
review_title: and feels like it might slip off
review_text:
It came right on time, with Prime 2-day shipping. But it came in a plastic baggie with the Curly Co logo on it. No product box, no instructions. Granted, I could be the only nerd out there who needs instructions on how to attach and use a diffuser. It was mostly the attaching that I needed help with. It was very difficult to attach to my blowdryer (a travel size Revlon, I think? I'm not sure, I originally bought it for helping my watercolor dry faster), and feels like it might slip off.

To attach, I ended up putting the diffuser on the floor, pressing the barrel of my blowdryer into the attachment tube, and sort of peeling the attachment onto the dryer. My fingers got pinched and scraped in the process, and I pretty much had to put my full bodyweight into it. If my partner had been home, I would have asked him to do it since he used to throw people for fun (cheerleader) and would have had the required strength in one arm. Even so, it took me a solid 5 minutes of bodyweight and a few minutes of Googling to figure out if maybe the diffuser just wouldn't work with my dryer, or if I was doing it wrong.

I haven't used the diffuser yet. It just got here 10 minutes ago. I'll update when I've used it a few times.

**EDIT** I've now used this diffuser twice. It stays on well enough while I'm using it, but as someone else mentioned: collapsible means holding the diffuser the whole time anyway, because it keeps collapsing during use. Also, be prepared to go through the painful process of reattaching it EVERY time you want to use it. When I lay my dryer down when I'm done, at least 1/3 of the edge of the diffuser slips off the barrel every time. And although I no longer need to use my bodyweight and I've tried other ways of attaching the diffuser, the only one that works is getting my fingers in the silicone attachment ring of the diffuser and stretching it over my dryer. Doesn't sound like a big deal, but this material doesn't stretch well-- as a result, my index fingers and thumbs are visibly scraped, and one index nail got smashed between diffuser and dryer hard enough that one side of the nail is detached and bleeding. A+ job making this "universal" diffuser attachable by the women it's meant for, dev team!

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: The trimmer that looks like a light sabre
review_text: I'd been wanting a trimmer with a vacuum option on it, so when I was buying some other new trimmers and shavers, I decided to get this one too.  I have to say in some ways I don't like it as much as the plain Norelco trimmer it replaced, but I'll give it 4 stars because the main reason I bought this, for the vacuum, works very well.  Didn't even use the turbo option, the counter-top looks a lot cleaner after a shave now.  The back of the trimmer guide looks odd, but it works fine.  My biggest knock is when you take the guide off. There's a sliding plastic panel that I guess is there to help direct hair into the vacuum, but it makes trimming without the guide a bit of a pain.  I used to use my old trimmer to trim my mustache, but I'll probably use the trimmer on my shaver for that now, it's less work even though I have to reach for a second gadget.  Using the trimmer without the guide though to try to shape the sides of my beard was a little bit of a hassle, though I've only used the trimmer once, so maybe with some experimentation it will get easier.  Anyway, the vacuum part of it certainly works well.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
I have been a user of Sonicare for about 10 years--since I had a roommate who had to have gum surgery for gingivitis, and her oral surgeon recommended switching. They do a fantastic job. The price is excellent on this model, but I was concerned from previous reviews that it might not do as good a job as the regular Sonicares and that it might get destroyed from water leaking into the battery compartment.

While I was trying to decide, I used one of those disposable-type battery-operated brushes you can buy for a few bucks. My teeth felt disgusting compared to when I was using a Sonicare. Since I could tell such a huge difference, but money is really tight, I decided to get this model, and just try not to get the battery area wet, and live with the lower power, and hope that it doesn't die too early.

And I'm really glad I did, because I couldn't be happier with this brush. The design must have been updated because there are no holes near the battery housing as previous reviewers described (there are no holes anywhere). I'm pretty uncoordinated but without really trying I haven't gotten water anywhere near the battery area. I do blot the brush head dry on a towel between brushings, and that might be key since no water drips down the handle after I put it away.

It feels just as powerful to me as my previous Sonicares, and my teeth feel just as clean.

I like not having a charger taking up one of only two outlets in my bathroom and collecting dust on the counter. And I love that for travel I'll just be able to throw this in my bag without lugging a charger along. And for long travel you could just pop in two more AA batteries when needed--available almost anywhere. The batteries that came with the brush were strong, but they did die after two weeks. I would definitely recommend rechargables.

Although this brush is marketed for teens or kids, the brush head size is perfect for me; I still have my wisdom teeth and with other brushes it's been very difficult to really get to them.

For the price, even if this brush doesn't last a really long time, I think it will still be a very good deal. But if you buy it and it doesn't last, remember that there is a 2-year "limited" warranty.

Update Nov 1 2010: Still going strong on the second set of batteries. No problems whatsoever. GREAT deal.
Update May 22 2011: Still no problems, and I have only had to change the batteries 3 times since I first started using rechargables last October. When this dies I will definitely buy the same model again. It's so much cheaper than other Sonicares, and I think using regular batteries instead of a charger is a big benefit over the other models, too.
Update Jan 10 2012: BUY THIS! Still working perfectly, still easy on batteries, still much more convenient for travel than other Sonicares...and considering how much other Sonicares cost, this value is pretty unbelievable.
Update Nov 23 2012: OK, so I let my guard down and have now used this toothbrush in the shower many times. NO PROBLEMS! Since many reviews still complain of leakage or short lifespan, I can only assume there is a quality control issue and I lucked out. Still, for less than $30 with a 2-year warranty, I totally would have put up with one or two lemons.
Update: April 2013--SERIOUSLY, BUY THIS!

product_title: Moroccan Argan Oil Shampoo, 8 Fl Oz - Smooths and Repairs - Sulfate Free - Natural - Imported from Morocco by Pure Body Naturals
review_text:
I really love this shampoo. First off it comes in a pump. I have no time to fight with a bottle in the shower, waiting for it to drip down to the bottom. And if you stand them up by their caps (so that shampoo is already at top), they fall over! I also love the smell of this! I think it's mostly the almond oil and argan oil combining together, but I'm not sure. It smells almost like tanning lotion, but not quite! This shampoo does lather some. I have frizzy hair and can skip conditioner if I use this shampoo! I tend to only shampoo my hair every other day. So on the second day my hair did start to look oily. But nothing that I wouldn't go out in public. I find this so much more convenient than the masks. With an Argan oil mask, you have to shampoo, then put the mask on your hair, then wait 5-10 minutes and then finally rinse. This saves so much time! I have a two year old and no matter what time I get up, it seems that she always wakes up as soon as I set foot in the shower. So I have to be very quick or she will start yelling. So there's no time for multiple hair products and treatments. This save me time without sacrificing results!
I did receive a discount on my purchase of this shampoo in exchange of my honest feedback.

review_text:
The upper bristles are limp.
The lower (suction cups) are limp as well.

While the concept seems cool when viewing the ads, the reality is otherwise. In chrono order:

(1) First I had read the many poor reviews of easyfeet.
(2) Then I phoned Easyfeet, whereupon the guy insisted that the suction is excellent and the reviews were not true.
(3) So I found a place to buy this cheap, since I wanted them for a senior citizen
(4) Upon receipt I confirmed that the poor reviews proved correct. The suction cups are the kind which are LIMP & SHALLOW instead of "firm/resilient rubber".

Having bought & tried many bath mats over the years, I have experience with both good & bad suction cups. You'd be surprised how many bath mats have flat/limp suction cups. I had bought once a PVC bath mat from a reputable company which had similar limp cups. Upon complaining to them, they immediately replaced it with an identical mat, BUT this time, the model number was different. Because they knew full well that the latter model had deeper/firmer/resilient suction-cups which actually work, instead of shifting around!

(5) Finally, as stated previously, the bristles of easyfeet are a bad joke. (the upper ones) More like the bristles of a baby brush than the type to give a massage, the way the lower ones are. But actually, all of them are sorta scratchy. Instead, they should have used SWEEPA type of bristles. (see online images)

Very deceptive world we live in...

review_text:
Update: I ordered a couple of months ago and love the set of 6 I got. Then I ordered again thinking I'd get at least slightly different ones. Nope! I got the exact same shades again. And I mean EXACTLY the same shades as last time. So no, I wouldn't call it "random" by any stretch of the imagination and no, I'd not order this set of polish again. I like it but not enough to get a third set of the exact same polish again.

The set I received had 3 bottles that were various shades of pink (#419, #279,#339), a light green (Prince Char-mint #754), Scarlet red (#429), and Head Bang (#199). Out of the 6, I can honestly say that I love the scarlet red, the light green and the wonderful chocolate color of Head Bang. I didn't get the top coat I requested and was hoping for but I'm okay with that because if I only really liked 2 of the colors I'd have already gotten my moneys worth.

When you order this you have to keep in mind, you may not like the colors you get because you are letting someone else pick what you end up with. I am a darker skinned person but I love wearing all colors, no matter the shade, and you kind of have to have that mindset before ordering this. At the same time, keep in mind the cost of one bottle of this polish. It's totally worth it to me if all I have to buy separately is the topcoat. Honestly, if I knew I could get a whole different set of colors, I'd order another random set even if I only get 2 or 3 that I totally love. It's worth it.

review_text:
I love the way the Argon Oil Therapeutic Shampoo for damaged hair makes my hair feel. I have long, thick hair, which is dry and damaged due to coloring, using my flat iron and blow drying. I am always looking for new products to increase livelihood and moisture to my hair. This shampoo is made from natural oils such as argon, almond, jojoba, and Camilla seed. There is also vanilla and honey. I love how the product’s natural ingredients avoid the use of harsh chemicals and leave my hair feeling better than before use. I have noticed an increase in the shine of my hair. After only a few uses, my hair is softer and less damaged. Same results as seen with expensive products from beauty supply stores or salons. This Argon Oil shampoo is only $15, but I was able to try it for free. Being said, I do believe it is worth the label price for the quality of the product. The fragrance is light and I enjoy the smell because I am not picky as far as scents. For those that are into the smell of their shampoo, this is a more masculine scent but it is not overbearing. After use of the Argon oil therapeutic shampoo, I felt like I was in a spa. My entire bathroom had a lush aroma and I felt more relaxed.
I believe that one of the most important highlights of this product is that it is not tested on animals. I am an advocate for humane treatment of animals and it is important to me that I use products that hold the same values.

review_title: Without a doubt, this was money well spent!
review_text:
An incredible Bang💥 For The Buck‼
The included free manicure set in a hard case was the best set I've ever had and I would have paid $10 to $15 for it alone!
As for the electric drill, its simply phenomenal for the money. I don't know how it compares to the others that are very similar, but I chose this one because of the included manicure set.
I have an autoimmune condition called scleroderma. It manifests itself in me with hyper-keratinosis on the connective tissue under my fingernails and toenails along with
thickening skin around fingernails and toenails. This condition has been driving me mad for over a year now and this drill has brought sanity back into my life. It gently files away the hard keratin deposits that seep out from under my nails. Up until now, the only way I was able to chip away at it was with traditional nail clippers and critical cutters which always left me with bleeding and painful fingertips. It was also impossible to access the as deep as needed around the critical and underneath the part of the nail that was growing out. Also, all the different filing attachments made it a snap👌 to file the dry thick skin around my nails and on my fingertips.
With this drill and all the filling attachments being so amazing for such a severe condition, if all you need it for is to make your nails look great, this drill is a WINNER 🏆 for sure. My fingers and nails were a mess and in one treatment my fingers have never looked better!

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Works ok, but a wet/dry trimmer is the way to go!
review_text:
Had this trimmer for 2 years and it died last week after sliding into the bathroom sink under running water....

While it was working it was a good trimmer overall, though I really didn't like have to switch out the trimmer heads for the standard and then the detail sized cutters--on more than one occasion I was in a hurry and fumbling around looking for the other cutter assembly than what was on the trimmer. Another issue was that it was relatively easy to move the height adjustment by accident when taking off and replacing the plastic trimmer guard, which you need to do in order to switch cutting heads. It wasn't a really big deal, but a lot of times I wouldn't remember which number I had the hair length set on, and then I would have to guess what setting I had it one the last time I used it.....The vacuum feature was nice I guess in that it doesn't get too many little beard trimmings all over the sink, but then again it's really easy to just turn on the sink and rinse it, or, use the trimmer over a rug where you'll never see the small trimmings.....

But the big lesson here is to be sure buy a wet/dry beard trimmer that won't die if it gets a little wet. I just bought the Panasonic ER224S All-in-One Cordless Hair and Beard Trimmer [[ASIN:B000F4USF8 Panasonic ER224S All-in-One Cordless Hair and Beard Trimmer (Silver)]] which was almost half the price of the Phillips Norelco unit and it's a wet/dry trimmer that you can use in the shower. It also has a built-in detail trimmer so you don't have to switch cutter heads and worry about loosing attachments. When I went to replace the T980 that died, I avoided the latest Phillips/Norelco version because I think a wet/dry is beard trimmer is really the only way to go. So far I really like the Panasonic, and I wish I had bought one of these to start with.......

After about a month of use I am very satisfied with it.

PROS:

Oscillates as good or better than my old one.
Still on the original batteries.
I brush during my shower and the inside of the battery compartment is bone dry.
Cheaper than the rechargeable units.
Comfortable size.

CONS:

Marketed for teens? Pbbbllt. It can and should be used by everyone.
Doesn't come with a travel case.
Doesn't have the Quad Pacer® feature.

If the oscillating action seems weak, make sure the brush head is inserted correctly (bristles in line with the button) and the collar is on tight.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
I have owned two other Sonicare Power Toothbrushes over the past many years and have loved them both except for one thing. The rechargeable batteries are not replaceable. When they eventually failed, I have had to throw away the otherwise perfectly good toothbrushes. I hate waste, and this obvious scheme to shorten the life of their products to force me to buy a new toothbrush infuriated me.

Now I discovered the Xtreme e3000 model which comes with replaceable alkaline AA batteries. It is intended for pre-teens and teens. I am 69, but it works great for me. Like all Sonicare Power Toothbrushes, it does a great job of removing the plaque from under the gum line and preventing gum disease. I use NiMetalHydride rechargeables instead of alkaline AA batteries. A charge lasts many times longer than the charge on the non-replaceable batteries in my previous two Sonicare brushes. I recommend it to anyone of any age.

review_title: Save your money and find a better constructed piece.
review_text:
The pictures of this necklace are beautiful, the reviews seemed positive and these are my favorite colors - so I definitely wanted to try this necklace for myself.

Unfortunately, it's only okay (at best) - definitely not great. Since I received this necklace far sooner than the estimated shipping date the beaded portion seems alright, I have decided to be nice and give this three stars instead of one or two.

The ornate "half moon" which is on half the pendant is slightly off, it does not curve around the round pendant as the picture on the listing shows and instead is almost too large. The slightly skewed appearance of it makes this necklace look poorly constructed and cheap.

Also, the chain and clasp are very, very cheap - I am unsure that this would survive several wearings and "opening and closings" - the metal feels rough and scratchy against my skin, like it is already rusted (but it isn't). Just generally feels unpleasant.

I'm very disappointed, as I truly wanted to love this necklace - it would have complemented so many of my outfits. Unfortunately, I will just be tossing it in the trash; it isn't worth it to return due to the price. I had just hoped that the product I received actually resembled the pictures truly, and not some "one-off" version.

product_title: Collapsible Hair Diffuser by The Curly Co. with The Curly Co. Satisfaction Guarantee
review_text:
I really wanted this to work for me as I love to travel and this diffuser would take up much less space than my regular one. Alas, it isn't going anywhere with me.

This unit suffers from the same issue as others of its kind: it collapses too easily against your head when you're trying to use it. The merest touch against your hair causes it to buckle, so you have very little control over the diffuser. Additionally, the "fingers" that protrude from the bottom don't protrude nearly far enough, nor are there enough of them, to adequately hold/lift the curls or to help separate them into a soft, piece-y style. The diffuser DID diffuse the air stream from the dryer, but it didn't facilitate styling like my regular one does. Lastly, the opening that fits over the dryer barrel is very small, so it wouldn't fit over 3 of 4 dryers I tried. (I'm also in the market to replace my dryer.)

I hope someone does come up with a workable travel diffuser. Unfortunately, for me anyway, this one doesn't cut it.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: Just don't leave it in standing water, Einstein
review_text: First point: the sonicaire toothbrushes, as a group, are worlds better than any other electric toothbrush out there. Second point: the actual brushing mechanism of all the sonicaires is the same, so think hard before you waste the money on the more high-priced brushes in the line. The various bells & whistles cannot possibly be worth the astounding mark-up. Third point: when the built-in battery of a more expensive model goes bad (and for me it went bad inside of two years), you're screwed. There's no option but to throw it away and buy a new one (though I've seen videos of people cracking open the case & replacing the battery, but really who's actually going to do that?). The xtreme is the best bargain out there, not only relative to other electric toothbrushes or other sonicaires, but on an absolute basis, considering how much money you'll save on dental bills over the years if you use it faithfully. And to those who grouse about the fact that this model is susceptible to water infiltration, I say DUH. It's an electronic device, and its battery compartment is near the base! Keep it away from water, just as you would any other gizmo.

product_title: Easy Feet Foot Cleaner
review_title: The good and bad about Easy Feet
review_text:
My Easy Feet $14.95 purchased on their site (EZ Feet site) (buy one and receive one free plus "handling" and postage) cost a total of $30.97 (with their handling fees) shipped to the house, with their standard slow delivery which I approved. The good: EZ Feet seems very well constructed for what it has, and so far the bristles are holding up for me (owned for 2 weeks now). EZ Feet cleans MOST of the bottom of your foot and in between the toes, satisfactorily. With my size 12 foot, the REAR bottom of the foot is rather hard to clean with the EZ feet.

The bad: (as I see it) is that the EZ Feet doesn't clean any of the sides of your foot, being there's no bristles on the side, only on the bottom and the front part of the foot. I can't push my foot in far enough to get the rear BOTTOM of my size 12 foot. I have to wash most the top of my foot and all the sides of the foot after using the EZ Feet. It is easier cleaning my foot with the EZ Feet unit, ultimately.

EZ feet should positively add side bristles so the sides of the foot can be washed, and a larger footprint (or raise the top bristle armband slightly) so as to allow larger feet to clean the REAR bottom of the foot.

review_text:
This was my first time using poly gel, but I am not new to doing my own nails. I am very happy with the product and found it easy to use. You will need a UV light in order to use this product.

I was not happy with the dual forms. There was not a size that fit my thumbs and the some of the other sizes were a bit too small, but usable. I would suggest purchasing a separate set of dual forms if you intend to use those. The dual forms that I could use were easy to handle, but I wish that they had guidelines on them in order to make sure the nails are even and to keep from wasting gel. I prefer thinner nails and these came out very thick. I don't know if that was because I used too much gel or if it was due to the shape of the dual forms.

I have only used one color so far, but love it. My guess would be that you could get a max of 4 sets out of each tube depending on nail size and length that you choose.

The base coat and top coat bottles are really tiny and I don't know if they're sold separately in order to get more. I don't see them lasting as long as you would need in order to use all of the tubes of gel.

I did not have any issue with the brush tool and found it to be the proper size even when shaping both thumb nails without the dual forms.

Overall, I would recommend this product for ease of use, colors, and price. I give it 4 stars because of the issues with the dual forms.

review_text:
I have tried many shower caps before and it was very hard for me to find something good for my head. I have long hair coming down to my mid back and keeping it dry is really important to me to prevent frizz and oiliness. Most shower caps made in China were probably also to be sold on the Asian market, because anything made for Asians is too small for the rest of the world. None of them would cover my whole head and the water would always wet my hair.
Finding this cap was literally a lifesaver. Even though it's also made in China (obviously), it was most likely intended for sale on the Western market. It is REALLY stretchy and most importantly it covers my hair fully. I can tie up my hair in a bun and there still will be room. My hair NEVER gets wet in this cap.
This is my second time purchasing it. The first one I ordered on eBay and it was about $4 there! I will now buy from Amazon and will always stick with this amazing cap. Too bad it's only in one pattern though, I would love to see more designs.
TIP: Hang it up to dry so it will last you a long time. The first cap I made a mistake with and neglected letting it dry after showering and it got covered in mold after a while.

The customer in this case loses out and it leaves a sour taste and bad feelings all around.

My old Sonicare died after and few years and I had tried using several different brush types, manual and powered, attempting to find a cheap replacement. After a less than stellar annual check-up, I decided to just buy another Sonicare.

I saw this model and could not believe how little it cost. My old one was over a hundred dollars. It worked great too. I saw no difference other than the lack of the quadpacer timer thing. Unfortunately, it died in less than two weeks. And no, it was not the batteries, the thing is just dead.

I suggest you buy a rechargable 4100 for forty or fifty dollars. I have been using one for a few months now with no issues. It has the great cleaning action of a Sonicare at a reasonable price. Same as with the cheap battery powered model, the brush turns off after two minutes but does not have the quadpacer or any other fancy features.

product_title: Easy Feet Foot Cleaner
review_text:
I purchased this at a local drugstore. I did not have the suction problems others described - quite the opposite. I put it on my tub floor and when I went to throw it out, it was quite a fight to un-suction it. Why did I throw it out? Two reasons. First - I don't know why it didn't occur to me, but I'm super ticklish on the under side of my foot between the ball and heel. Washcloths and those mesh-type bath sponges are fine, but bristles - forget about it. This made this akin to a torture device. Second - I *might* have been able to tolerate the torture if it had actually cleaned my foot. It did nothing even close to clean it.

So, in short, doesn't clean your feet and it's torture if you are ticklish. Garbage.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
Until recently, I had been using a Remington beard trimmer I had received as a Christmas gift from about 5 years ago. The Remington was good but it eventually just couldn't go any longer so I had to search for a new trimmer. I found the Phillips Norelco T980 fairly quickly and was impressed by the good reviews. And it didn't disappoint!

The shipment came quick and I got to test it out (waited an hour for it to fully charge) to see how it would perform and perform it did! The shaver comes with 9 different preset trimming sizes so there is plenty of room for dynamic trimming. The flexible trim guard was something I immediately noticed and enjoyed, since my previous trimmer did not have this feature. In addition the flexibility really does allow you to get a precision trim really easily as it contours to the face great.

The T980 comes with a 2 bristle (one soft, one hard) brush for cleaning out the clippers but what really is unique about this trimmer is the vacuum that is attached to it. The vacuum is made so that there is less of a clean up once your done trimming your beard, although it doesn't catch all the trimmings it did catch most of them and clean up was much faster than what I am used too. It also comes with a smaller clipper attachment for precision sculpting or just your run of the mill mustache trimming which is slid on and off with ease.

The shaver also comes with a Turbo Mode but the only thing this really does that I have noticed is give the vacuum more power, it may also speed up the clippers but I am not sure about that it seems to clip nicely whether the Turbo Mode is on or off. I think because of the vacuum this trimmer seems a bit louder during operation than my last trimmer but by no means is it a chainsaw (haha).

Finally, the trimmer comes with a travel bag for easy storage on trips which I thought was thoughtful. The only qualm I had was the packaging...it comes in a really sturdy clam shell package and with no helpful opening tabs so it could take you at least a few minutes to get everything out without cutting yourself on sharp plastic edges but since that has nothing to do with the performance of the trimmer I wont go on about that.

So all in all, this trimmer is a fine replacement; dare I say upgrade to my last trimmer, it is said, "You get what you pay for" well, with the Norelco T980 I think you may be getting that and then some! Precision trimming, ease of use, and convenient clean up and features makes this shaver a must buy for any man especially those on the job hunt!

review_title: Drill is okay but I had to buy separate bits.
review_text:
I used this drill about twice a week on hard gel and polygel nails. I only ever do my own nails but I do them fairly often so I got a moderate amount of personal use out of it for about 8 months before it completely died.

This drill itself worked well for me and I liked that I was able to change the direction of rotation. The drill was slim, light, and easy to hold in either hand the whole time I used it.

The bits were fairly useless. The softer bits just kicked up fuzz and most of the metal bits didn’t have enough grit to do anything. I had to buy new bits to get any real use out the the thing but for the price I didn’t mind too much. The bit I get the most use out of is the one that holds disposable arbor bands.

The drill gave out and stopped moving counterclockwise about 6 months into using it which was unfortunate because some bits not work while spinning in one direction and it can help to switch directions when you switch hands. Just over a month later it gave out completely in both directions and I can no longer use it at all.

Bottom line: Yes, it is a good drill while you can use it but be prepared to buy your own bits if you want to get any real filing done and don’t be surprised if it doesn’t last forever. I am disappointed that it gave out, but I feel like the price made it not worth getting angry about. For personal use it was alright but I would absolutely not recommend for professional use. I’d consider it if I were a nail student trying to save where I could.

review_title: NO DESIGN FLAW - USER ERROR - Well Designed, Its design is INTENTIONAL
review_text: I would give 6 stars if possible. For only $25.00 this is an extremely well engineered item. I also have an ORIGINAL Sonicare Advanced and it is nearly 13 years old now.  I learned a long time ago how damaging water can be.  My brother in law and my sister got Sonicare brushes for themselves and me for Christmas over a decade ago. Theirs went out quick, due to water and calcium buildup. All my Sonicare products I take extreme care of.  When using, I try and never let water drip down the brush head.  After use, I remove the brush head, and store it and the handle upside down.  This keeps water from going down into the device or the threads and causing problems.  If not stored upside down, not only can water get into the item, but, calcium and contaminants can leak down and get in the brush head threads.  All can be resolved by simple care and upside down storage. Of note, my original Series A over a decade old, looks like NEW from pampered care, excluding the discoloration of age. A little care goes a LONG way. A little lack of care/abuse and anything will deteriorate. With the top of the line Sonicare Diamond Clean being over $200.00 versus the HX3351 at only $25, you can't expect bullet proof.  For $300 to $400 they could make this out of aircraft aluminum like LED Flashlights and make it 100% waterproof but you wouldn't buy it, the cost would be prohibitive.  A little care goes a LONG way, 13 years for me and counting.
