review_title: Great smelling and makes pores look smaller.
review_text:
I've recently been on the warpath for something to fight my middle-aged (okay, just aged) acne that has popped up to join my wrinkles, age spots, and gray hair.

I have to say first that I am not an experienced user of either cosmetics or products claiming to clear your skin. That said, I have found that rose oil water is effective at shortening the life of some of my acne. I think THIS product is actually either eliminating some blackheads, or at least making my pores smaller. And it smells and feels really good when you use it. Very pleasant texture somewhere between a mud mask and extremely fine exfoliant. It doesn't dry out my skin and I live in an extremely dry high desert climate, but it isn't oily, either.

You have to put it on after you wash your face, and then wait a few minutes, which does add time to my morning routine of washing my face and then just heading out the door. But I believe it is worth it

Be realistic in your expectation of any face products, none of them can give you skin like Nicole Kidman. I'm still breaking out with my annoying 'spots' but this product does seem to make my pores less conspicuous, which for me is quite an achievement.

I was give a sample of this to use and provide a review.

review_text: If you are considering getting this trimmer, all you need to know is this: The 9 lockable length settings don't actually lock!! I tried putting it on length "3", but when I started to trim, it went down to length "2".  Then I started on length 2 and it went down to length 1.  Besides this, the cutting block is too far away from the thing that touches your face (not sure what it's called), so it's very hard to cut any hair at all unless you choose the length setting 3 or lower.  I know all this may come as a surprise to those of you who have had success with previous Norelco trimmers, but the fact is that this thing is a serious piece of Sh_t.  In my estimation, their aspirations to achieve the fancy "vacuum effect" has clouded what should be their primary goal with this device: to trim facial hair EVENLY and EFFECTIVELY!  I would have given this 0 stars if it would have been an option.

review_title: Very Miniscule Results…  Not As Nourishing As Described…
review_text:
I had very high hopes for this shampoo that has a “#1 Best Seller” stamp and mainly amazing reviews. I got this shampoo to restore my hair to its natural state (silky and soft) because another “Argan Oil” shampoo caused damage by making it dry and brittle. I have been using this shampoo for several weeks now and I’ve noticed very miniscule improvements. My ends aren’t as brittle and doesn’t break as badly as before. That is the only positive think I can say about this shampoo. I feel it strips my hair and leaves it flat and lifeless. My scalp is not rejuvenate. Instead it feels dry and itchy at times.

It smells on the chemical side and I certainly don’t smell any notes of “natural vanilla and sumptuous honey.” I was expecting an at least pleasant scent. The bottles says “No Harsh Chemicals” but there are ingredients I can barely pronounce – Acyl Sarcosine, Cocamidopropyl Betaine, Sodium Lauroyl Sarcosine and what the heck is GRECAT BTMS-350???

It comes in a generous size pump style bottle that will last you a while. However, my search goes on for a decent shampoo with or without argan oil…

review_title: Expensive and not quite the same.
review_text:
I needed replacement blades and these did the trick. They allowed me to get a better shave than my old blades and that is a good thing. With that said, they certainly have some downsides.

(1) They're quite expensive. I might have to consider getting a new razor before purchasing these again.

(2) They don't trigger the "intensive cleaning needed" message on my 8995 like my old blades. Previously, I'd get the cleaning message after about 10-15 minutes of shaving ... now I could shave for hours and it'll never pop up. Is that a deal-breaker? No, I can figure out when I should clean the razor on my own, but wasn't that LCD/notification one of the supposed perks of the 8995 over lower models?

(3) They retain much more hair than my old blades ever did. The hair really collects on the inside ends of the blades, so you have to get at it with the brush after each shave. If you don't, you will have to replace your cleaning solution a lot sooner.

1

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
1. I don't understand these reviews that complain about getting water into the battery compartment and corroding the batteries. I've never had this problem. It would seem that one would have to be really careless for this to happen. Don't submerge it or pour water over it, and you should be fine.
2. Don't worry about battery life. Get some Eneloop rechargeables, and swap them out anywhere from a couple weeks to a couple months and you'll be fine.
3. This does such a good job, my dentist assumes I'm flossing like I'm supposed to be. I'm not. I do use a waterpic, but only a couple times a week these days. My dentist gave me an A+ on my last visit (part of this is because of the fluoride rinse that's been helping strengthen my teeth, but that's another review).

So now to the reason I only gave it three stars.

I had one of these that we bought years ago. I don't remember how long, but it's been probably 5 years. I'm not exactly sure, but it's been awhile. It's always worked great and still does. We finally got tired of sharing, and when we saw they were only $20 on Amazon we got another one.

This second one has had to be replaced under warranty twice in about a year and a half. It just stopped working, both times. No corrosion in the battery compartment or anything. The unit looks pristine, it just stopped working.

The first one lasted about 8 months. The second one only about 6 months.

So while this is a great product (functionally) and I would still likely buy it again if my current one died out of warranty (can't beat $20) I'm getting concerned about the quality. Here's hoping third time's a charm.

review_text:

It's a little bulky, so getting the hairs under the nose takes just a little more effort.

Recently I dropped the trimmer, and trying to catch it accidentally slammed it onto the tile countertop. Pieces went flying everywhere, and I thought I had to buy another one. product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Excellent concept and product, but with ultimately fatal design flaws.
review_text:
I've had this trimmer for a little over a year, and prior to this I'd been using a similar product by Norelco, so I came to love the vacuum concept. This product does what you'd expect it to, and it does it well: Trim your beard (or hair, if you're patient) and vacuum up the trimmings. It doesn't catch 100%, but it gets pretty close. In general, it's a worthwhile product.

However, it is fair to mention one fatal flaw with this design: the vacuum door hinge. It is constructed of brittle plastic, and the hinge crumbled on me after 15 months of use. I have since decided to try a non-vacuum product by Wahl. If Norelco could change the design of the trimming area to eliminate the hinged door design -- say a small cup that you snap out and empty instead -- then this product would be flawless and guaranteed to last for years. As it stands, I'm going to wait for this product to evolve a little further before purchasing from Norelco again -- unless a competitor comes up with an improved design first!

3. It comes from China, so it takes forever to get to you. I don't remember seeing that in the description, although I may have missed it.

product_title: Easy Feet Foot Cleaner
review_text: If standing on one foot on a wet, soapy shower floor isn't an issue for you, you don't need this.  For those who have balance and mobility trouble, it's a safer way to scrub and exfoliate your feet and clean between your toes.  It's well made and with daily use hasn't shown any signs of falling apart.  The bristles are fairly soft but diabetics and anyone else who must guard against cuts on the feet should be cautious during use.  The attached pumice stone is positioned to work on the heels, but just place the ball of your foot on the stone without putting your whole foot inside if you need to exfoliate that area as well.  UPDATE: After more use I agree with warnings that the suction cups DO NOT hold it in place.  If standing on one foot is a problem, use this only while seated.  If standing, keep your free foot planted firmly and never put your weight on the foot inside the scrubber. It will be very uncomfortable and will probably slip out from under you.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: BUY UNLESS YOU ARE FROM THE HARD OF THINKING CLUB
review_text: I was looking to find a groomer that was fast and could provide an even cut on my beard which consists of both straight and curly hair. This one sounded like the right choice plus it had the bonus vacuum feature, but some of the negative reviews about sudden cutting length changes almost made me pass it by. I am happy to say that I purchased the groomer and have had no problems at all with unwanted adjustment changes. With the amount of people complaining about this, I have no doubt that it can happen, but my guess is that in most cases if not all, it has more to do with the way the groomer is being held. I can imagine situations where with a death grip on the adjustment ring and extreme down pressure on the cutting head, one might be able to duplicate the problem during a direction change. I really like the vacuum feature and would put it the 90% range for effectiveness when taking your time and not trying to trim your beard when you're already twenty minutes late! I have normal hearing and do not find the trimmer overly loud even in the turbo mode which for me is the only mode that I use as both the cutting and vacuum features work best at high speed and battery life remains very good.

review_title: You get what you pay for!

While I didn't like the flat foundation brush or the flat angle brush at all, I thoroughly enjoyed the round dome brush, the tapered concealer brush, and the angled blush brush!

However, you shouldn't let this dissuade you from buying the brushes. Keep in mind that this review is entirely subjective, therefore the brushes that I listed as horrible may not be so bad for the prospective buyer (and vice-versa)

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Excellent Shaver, a Few Minor Criticisms
review_text:
There are a ton of reviews here, so no need to go into great detail about what everyone else mentions, but I'll summarize anyway. It works very well, the battery life between charges is very good, it looks nice, and as many others write, it does a great job at vacuuming up trimmed hairs, even if a few escape.

My criticisms are:

1. I wish the case that came with it were more compact, even form fitting. The one I received was basically a small pouch with a flap that seems almost like an afterthought design-wise.

2. The power on button went off many times when traveling, due to the fairly sensitive button being flush with the shaver. This could be prevented if the button was recessed and/or there was a lock switch to lock the trimmer off completely when traveling. A few times, it accidentally turned on and started buzzing in my suitcase and caused a few stares, and even a few chuckles, if you know what I mean. A form-fitting case that has a space around the button would also help.

3. I agree with other reviewers: I wish this was designed so that the mini-trimmer attachment was on the other side of the head, so that there are no attachments at all. Perhaps this could be re-designed so that a simple switch (like on a reversible screwdriver) could switch back and forth between the beard trimmer and the mini attachment.

All in all, I am very happy with this trimmer, but would purchase another one if they addressed the previously mentioned issues.

review_title: A pump? For this thick stuff?  Really?
review_text:
I love this shampoo. The product itself is excellent. Makes my long, blonde hair, silky and soft. (See Picture) And it has a very light pleasant scent I can barely smell. What's not to like? The reason I only give it 3 stars is because of the pump bottle. First, the pump is too small for this thick shampoo. I have long hair so it would take 20-30 pumps to have enough to cover my whole head. So... just take the pump off and pour it, right? Wrong. The opening is so large that you get too much in one pour. It makes a huge mess and wastes product. So just put it in a squeeze bottle, right? That's what I did. And it wasn't easy, because you can't pump it and the opening is too large to pour from one container to another without a funnel. So I used a funnel, and slowly, very, very slowly managed to get product into my squeeze bottle and voila! It works great. Now I can squeeze out just the right amount! (See picture)

I would definitely recommend this product and have done so.

Please offer this wonderful, amazing shampoo in a squeeze bottle. Please?

product_title: Collapsible Hair Diffuser by The Curly Co. with The Curly Co. Satisfaction Guarantee
review_text:
I was SO excited when I came across this diffuser on Amazon. I’ve used other diffusers in the past, but did not like how much space it required to store it. So this Silicone base product was a new concept to me- a collapsible diffuser, what a great idea! However, the reality was very different. Read below for my experience.

Pros: I found this diffuser to be very light weight, because it is collapsible it saves lots of storage space when traveling, the silicone product also stretched a tiny bit to fit around the nozzle, the nozzle measurements were accurate; it fit very snug around my blow dryer (which is a Jilbere by Conair Titanium Tools Dryer, 2000 watts- I LOVE LOVE THIS BLOW DRYER !!).

Cons: From my experience the diffuser would often collapse when using it, my curly hair would often get wrapped around the prongs that stick out and would get stuck and pull my hair out even with the slightest touch.

Overall, I found this diffuser to be no different than other diffusers; it did not make my hair any better (in terms of volume or frizz) than other diffusers. After a while of attempting to use the diffuser, I was VERY disappointed and annoyed so I returned the product to the seller. I found the product to be poorly constructed (or at least the one that was sent to me was not made well). I would like to give it a 2.5 stars because it delivers on half of what it claims but I don't see an options for this.

*** THANK YOU for reading an I hope this review was helpful to you ****

review_text:
DISCLAIMER: I DO NOT RECOMMEND YOU USE THIS PRODUCT FOR YOUR OWN DOGS UNLESS YOU ANYWAY KNOW HOW TO SCALE THEIR TEETH AND THEY ARE USED TO IT!!!

I have been scaling my dogs' teeth since I have had them, for one dog that is over 13 years and the other, over 4. I scale them by hand about every 2-3 months. I have previously used regular metal hand tools exclusively. My vet is very impressed with their teeth and has said that they are the cleanest teeth he's seen on dogs their age. I am a bit anal retentive about it I suppose. I tried to ask for a perfectional cleaning once when my older dog had to go under for a different procedure but my vet said there was nothing to clean off.....

Anyway. All that to say I am experienced with doing this to my dogs and they are used to me doing it. I would not recommend anyone start off a dog that's unfamiliar with them being in their mouths to try to use this on them, the vibrations could be scary and you could get bitten by your own dog.

I bought this on prime day a few days ago and just used it the first time today. It works GREAT. No more force needed to scrape their teeth! Just a little back and forth and the plaque just liquifies. Saves their gums from the occasional slip and poke that sometimes happens when I have to go near the gum line! I will be using this from now on!

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
My hygienist and dentist kept encouraging me to switch my family over to sonic care toothbrushes, but the big investment and expensive replacement heads held me back. I purchased one of these toothbrushes each for myself, my oldest child and husband. Since then, we have all gotten better reports from the hygienist. I had actual gingivitis for awhile that occurred during my last pregnancy, and I haven't had it this pregnancy. The big difference in my routine is this toothbrush. If you want to reduce your ecological footprint, put rechargeable batteries in it.
The downside is that it doesn't have some of the fancier features of the more expensive sonics - I still get coffee stains on my front teeth. Sonicare has a whitening brush that would stop that. My hygienist told me I could just hold my current brush on my front teeth for an extra few seconds, though. Also, the top part where the brush head fits into got gunked up in my brush before. I cleaned it out and there was no damage, but I guess it could happen to others - so that is something to keep an eye on.
If you are looking for value in a sonic brush, this could be the answer.

review_title: Smooths hair without weighing it down
review_text:
I have fairly fine hair, but LOTS of it, and it tends to get a frizzy, especially in the humidity. I don't really spend a lot of time fixing my hair (2 year olds don't give you a ton of free time to do your hair!) I like to just wash & go and don't tend to use much product either.
My roots get oily after 1 day of not washing, so I was skeptical as to what would happen using something with OIL in the name! I was impressed though, the amount of oil on my roots did not increase. I tried this, just the shampoo itself, and found that my hair felt softer and looked shinier once it was dry. Even without me doing anything after washing--no drying, products, straighteners, etc. It also helped to seal the shaft and decrease the overall puffiness that can happen with wavy hair and the humidity of April! The scent is nice too, not overbearing at all.
Overall, I think it's a good product to help smooth damaged hair without weighing it down.

review_text:
For reference, I have oily clog prone skin. I've never really suffered from major acne, just occasional breakouts and issues with blackheads and a lot of whiteheads which has caused large pores and minor skin pitting/scars. I have been on a quest to find something to help with my large pores for a while. I feel like I have tried just about everything under the sun. I purchased this product based on the good reviews here and I am glad I did. This product has definitely made a difference. I didn't find it to be over drying or harsh to use. Additionally, it has kept away any breakouts. The changes aren't dramatic or seen overnight but significant enough for me to want to repurchase and recommend to others. I haven't found anything that has worked better for me and I have tried a lot of high end and OTC skincare products.

Update: I finally finished up the bottle, it lasted me quite a while. I've decided not to repurchase at this time, maybe if I don't find something else intriguing, I may return to this product. The reason for not repurchasing is that the end results were good but not great, subsequently I cannot justify the price. I did notice reduction in clogged pores and blackheads but it did not completely go away. I did find that this product worked great for keeping my skin clear of acne.

USDA organic certification should only add at most %20 increase in average market price over other organic castor oils. I have purchased excellent rich, thick organic castor oil at $14 for 16 oz (Heritage brand).  What really gets me is that all the product description is anecdotal customer reviews. Why exactly should we pay a 100% markup?

product_title: Easy Feet Foot Cleaner
review_text:
RETURNED!
First of all, I am barefoot all day long, so I need to clean the bottoms of my feet, but I also do a lot of dying, and constantly have dye spraying or dripping on the tops of my feet as well. So when I get in the shower, I usually end up scrubbing my feet with a brush anyway - I thought this would be great, because it scrubs the bottoms *and* tops at the same time! Yay! What a great idea!.... NOT.
Problems;
1. First problem, the suction cups suck (and not in the way they should!) The thing slides around, and is nearly impossible to keep still long enough to get on a good scrub. I spent more time chasing it around the shower with my foot, than it would ever have taken me to just scrub my feet by hand. Even when I was able to keep it still long enough to start scrubbing, every time I pushed my foot into it with enough pressure to actually scrub, it started to move again, and here I am chasing it around the shower again! So #1, bad suction.
2. And this is the worst part! When I was able to push it up against the side of the shower so it wouldn't slide around so much, I don't know if it's because I have high arches or what, but when I put my foot all the way in, that hard blue plastic across the top just scraped the tops of my feet raw! Very painful, and even feeling kind of bruised as well!!
So even if it didn't slide around, and make it impossible to scrub for more than 5 seconds, it is so painful to put my foot all the way in, so I wasn't able to scrub the whole foot, I had to just do the bottom of my toes, and then going only up to about half of my foot, stopping once it got to the hard blue plastic on top. So after my first use, my feet remained dirty, and now have painful scratches on the tops of my feet.
Not a pleasant experience to say the least!! I saw another one on here that only does the bottoms, so I am going to cross my fingers, and try that one, and hope that the suction cups work better! It won't get the tops at the same time, so it won't hurt them either!

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: great alternative to pricey rechargeable models w/ sealed battery compartments
review_text:
I had a $120 Sonicare system that came complete with power brush handle, charging base, sonicare brush heads & it was great up until the sealed unit/non user replaceable batteries/designed to be thrown away power brush handles died/wouldn't hold a charge. The sonicare brush system itself is great & I noticed an improvement in my teeth & gum health along with the use of a WaterPik, but the non user replaceble power brush handles made me not want to buy another Sonicare system again. Phillips Sonicare just tells you to throw them out when they don't hold a charge. Same with their Phillips/Norelco Shavers, but those at least I can use plugged in/corded after the internal rechargeable battery dies & it's no longer "cordless"

The Phillips Sonicare battery operated toothbrush is the best of both worlds. You get your Sonicare powered toothbrush system, it uses standard AA batteries, & Sonicare E-series brush heads which I usually get a 6 pack at Costco when they have the $9-10 off coupon promotions making it about $40/6 E-series brush heads (locally at drug stores, its $12-18). Now the best part, since it uses Standard AA batteries, I just buy high numbered mAh rechargeable batteries designed for high drain/power usage so I basically have a rechargeable Sonicare brush head system that won't go obsolete when the batteries die (user replaceable & not sealed like the Sonicare systems with sealed power brush handles & charger bases)...

I read reviews of it getting wet inside the battery compartment before purchasing & haven't experienced that. I make sure to face the handle down so gravity & running water would make the water go towards the top/brush head & not the bottom base/battery cover compartment. Haven't had any issues with corrosion, water getting inside the battery compartment, or inside the unit.

I use my UV sanitizer for the brush heads which came with my previous system.

All in all awesome, like my previous $120 system, but w/o the non replaceable batteries. I've used it daily for about a year or so without any issues & it performed about the same as my $120 sonicare system, minus the quad pacer timer, low battery/charge warning, and of course charger base.. but what I have right now is basically the same thing.. a rechargeable sonicare toothbrush system... it's not as convenient to recharge as just docking it on the charger base, but if you buy high mAh batteries, you really don't have to charge that often.. I get at least 2 weeks between charges with 3200 mAh Panasonic batteries designed to work with digital cameras & other high drain/power consumption electronics & toys.

Amazon had it for almost half than what Target & local retailers sold it for at the time. Great purchase & I don't miss much from the rechargeable all in 1 packaged systems.

Not sure how this thing got so many good reviews. The device is completely useless at trimming my beard, and only works on the lowest setting (which is a really close trim). Literally on any setting past the shortest setting, it won't actually trim any hair.

Not sure who designed the springy gaurd but its clear just from looking at it that none of the hair actually gets close enough to the blades to get cut.

I have an old razor that plugs in and has 3 or 4 different adapters, and that works a lot better.

When it does cut, on the really short setting, the vacuum does actually work, but theres a plastic thing that gets in the way and makes it tough to shave with any accuracy.

Anyway, hope to prevent people from having the same frustrations I have after spending $40 for something that could barely shave your head much less something a bit more technical, like your face!

review_title: Good for travel but not especially sturdy
review_text:
This diffuser is lightweight and only 1.75" tall when collapsed. And the part that slips over the dryer nozzle stretches ever-so-slightly to accommodate my Conair Vagabond, which has a non-tapering barrel and 2" mouth. I don't mind that half the vents in little circular piece (in the center of the "bell") are blocked by plastic; it's a minor flaw. But it gets annoying when the diffuser keeps collapsing, partially or fully, with little pressure when I'm drying my hair.

Despite the collapse issue, I bought a second diffuser about a year ago to use at home. It was better than the bulky plastic "universal" one that kept falling off my full-size dryer. Since then, 5 of the 6 larger nubs have broken - the bullet-shaped caps came loose and fell off. I just bought a replacement - but not by The Curly Co.

product_title: Electric Portable Bidet
review_title: Great for one use. Then broken.
review_text:
Worked once. Then died/broken the second time i plugged it in.

Order:
I received this product quickly and the condition was great. It comes in a small box with all the parts, and even a “free kit” with tweezers, clippers, cuticle cutters, etc.

Use:
I only got to use this product once for less than five minutes to shape the top of my nails while doing a nail dip manicure. The speed options were great, from very slow and light to very quick. I found the drill worked best for my purposes low-medium. The drill heads were very easy to remove and replace.

Broken:
Unfortunately when I went to use this drill again for a second time, I found that it wouldn’t turn on. The power cord light was on, the unit got warm (I’m assuming this isn’t normal), but the drill would not “turn on.”

Overall:
Given the fact that this unit didn’t last more than one short use, I probably would not buy again.

Customer Service;
I was contacted personally by company regarding my poor experience with this product. I like the integrity of the company, and willingness to make sure things were e of.

product_title: Moroccan Argan Oil Shampoo, 8 Fl Oz - Smooths and Repairs - Sulfate Free - Natural - Imported from Morocco by Pure Body Naturals
review_text:
I absolutely LOVE this shampoo!! Argan oil is "in" right now and I can see why. I've purchased serums and conditioners in the past but this shampoo is some of the best. The directions say to use a dime size but i have thick hair so I used a full pump. The directions also state to repeat as needed, I think I repeated 3 times just to get the full effect. I used a tiny bit of conditioner but only because I have hard water and my hair does not do well with it. I let my hair air dry overnight as usual but the next morning my hair wasn't frizzy and crazy, it was actually manageable (after a good brushing). I didn't put any product in my hair before I used my iron to straighten it. I wanted to see how the shampoo actually worked. My hair went from thick and crazy to flat and sleek. NO greasy feel! NO weight added to my hair!
The bottle is a plastic bottle so it's excellent to have in the shower. The pump is fantastic and works well! Totally worth the price, it's an absolutely large bottle and I hope I don't go through it too fast. It does not dry out my hair or strip away the natural oils. I haven't straightened my hair in a few days and although it's not sleek and flat like right after ironing, but it is not frizzy and it still looks and feels great. And because the shampoo didn't strip away the natural oils in my hair, my body didn't have to create more oil, leaving my scalp itchy and my hair looking greasy.
Love this shampoo!! I have thick black hair and it works wonders!

product_title: Organic Castor Oil - Boost Hair Growth for Hair, Eyelashes & Eyebrows. USDA Certified Organic, 100% Pure, Cold Pressed, Hexane Free. Eyelash Growth Serum & Brow Treatment with Appl
review_title: Love this USDA certified Castor oil!
review_text:
If your use to the super tall 16oz plastic bottles of castor oil for a dirt cheap price, probably cheaper than this 4oz bottle, then your probably not understanding what is so great about castor oil. You more or less probably just use the castor oil as a cheap carrier oil to dilute essential oils, which I myself also do with those big cheap 16oz bottles. If your looking at this bottle and then the price and thinking no way, then I can guarantee you've never tried Pure, "real" ,no filler, Castor oil, because if you did, you would understand why this 4oz bottle costs what it does. Also you would have reaped the benefits in probably more ways than one from using True Castor oil , and would think this is actually a really great price for USDA organic certified castor oil. I use this oil as part of my night time facial regime, and it's also amazing at getting rid of scars and stretch marks.
This oil can also be used to help grow fuller darker lashes, eyebrows and you can even add it to your shampoo and or conditioner to improve the overall health and growth of your hair. The only Castor oil that I will put in my hair and on my face is USDA certified, otherwise you have no reassurance that what your using, especially on your face, is in fact pure and without fillers. Because of this not being a food item, the regulations on it are extremely light, and therefore companies can mix castor oil with water or other things and slap a pure castor oil label on it, and not have to disclose that it's been diluted in one way or any other. The ONLY way to know for sure is to purchase a bottle that's been stamped with the USDA stamp, which she means it has gone thru rigorous testing and is in fact pure with nothing added to it in anyway.
Pure castor oil is going to be semi thick, exactly like this oil from RejuveNaturals. This is great oil and I'm very satisfied with the purchase and recommend if you haven't tried pure USDA certified castor oil that you purchase a bottle of this castor oil from RejuveNaturals, it will change the way you look at castor oil forever. I did recieve a discount on this bottle during a promotional period. In return I agreed to give my honest unbiased opinion of the oil after having been able to test it. My opinion is purely my own and in no way was purchased or compensated for in anyway.

I use mine at 200 degrees Celcius, but it is capable of much higher temperatures. With practice, you can get the roots of your hair--it all depends on how you part and angle the brush from the roots. Package arrived with brush in well-cushioned air bubble packaging, and since the tips of the brush have silicone, I had to pick away some excess silicone hanging off the bristles from the molding--nothing major. I saw none of the issues shown in other reviews on here, and was very pleased. The directions also state not to use this product on wet hair, your hair needs to be dry. My mother used it on wet hair(despite the instructions saying not to), and if you are looking for a product like that to dry and straighten--this isn't like that, and I doubt you will find a good quality product that does both. No enamel issues with the bristles, I highly reccomend!

review_text: I love everything about this Argan oil shampoo. After using for a few weeks my hair seems healthier, with more luster and shine. I am big on researching ingredients and I am extremely satisfied with the simple list of ingredients, I did have to research GRECAT btms-350 (also known as Behetrimorium methosulfate)because it was something I was unsure of, however I am pleased with what I have found: "Behetrimorium methosulfate is basically considered to be the most promising hair detangling ingredient ever; it is also considered to not only be effective but also safe and mild to use. Behetrimorium methosulfate is also known as BTMS". product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: A Review just for the Sake of Reviewing
review_text:
There are plenty of reviews on this trimmer so I won't go into detail - but I did want to make sure I rated the item. I think overall the trimmer is a good product - it does what it is supposed to do. After a few months of use (1-2 times a week), I developed my own pro's con's for the trimmer. It replaced a very cheap Remington trimmer that I had for years (the rechargable battery no longer held a charge) and although I know "change" can be tough after using something for several years, there are a few things I just can't get past.

1. having to remove the general trimmer and replace it with the mini trimmer is more of a PITA than I thought it would be. My old Remington had a built in mini-trimmer that flipped up on the back side - nothing to remove - just flip up and use. On the Philips, pulling the gate off and swapping the basic trimmer for the mini trimmer is pretty annoying. Granted it's not that big of a deal in the grand scheme of life or my morning routine, but it is still pretty annoying. When you remove the gate and start swapping parts, some of the hair that did make its way into the vacuum chamber now gets scattered about again.

2. many have complained about the height adjustment changing on them... I have not encountered this. I can add that for me, none of the settings match my old Remington. This is not so much a reflection on the product, but more of a: "keep in mind, you'll have to adjust to this new product's height - it doesn't adjust to you". I keep my hair short and for me 3 is too long and 2 is too short. I needed a 2.5. I find that if I press really hard in the 3 setting, I can get close, but it seems to take a lot of work. Again, not so much a complaint on the product, just personal preference.

3. For whatever reason, I can not seem to get the hairs on my lip that are close to the underside of my nose. The trimmer gate seems to be so bulky that it hits my nose before the cutter can clip the hair. I have to remove the gate and carefully trim the hairs using the height of the surrounding hairs that the trimmer did get as a guide.

Other than those three annoyances, I can live with the vacuum not catching ALL of the hair (the Remington flung ALL of the hair everywhere). Battery life seems solid, but I guess only time will tell. Someone else mentioned they wished it came with a stand and I concur - it would be nice. Overall it's a solid product and for those with a lot of facial hair, I bet this would be a great purchase.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I bought this trimmer after my old Norelco stopped charging. For the record, I maintain a full beard with this. Overall, I am satisfied with the product, but there are some caveats.

Vacuum: Like me, you may be interested in the included vacuum, rather than getting hair all over the place. It works pretty well for this! I'd say about 90% of the hair is trapped in the canister, about 3% on the sink, and about 7% left in my beard. For this reason, I recommend using the trimmer before you shower. Otherwise, you will get little hairs all over your shirt during the day. If you only have a goatee or similar, it may not be quite as bad. It's not much hair, but the little vacuum can't solve everything.

Noise: The noise level is loud, but not really any noisier than an electric toothbrush. To me, it's really no big deal. With the bathroom door closed, you can only hear it when close to the door anyway. I even run it in turbo mode most of the time, and still don't have an issue with this. Of course it would be great if it were completely silent, but really it's not that bad.

Trimming: Like all Norelcos, it does a great job trimming. The included adapter(s) handle just about everything I could imagine needing. I am a hairy guy, and have not felt any pulling or ripping of the hairs, just a clean trim.

Power: I typically get several weeks worth of trimming (every 2-3 days) on a single charge. To maintain the battery, always ensure you fully drain it before recharging. Using turbo mode drains it slightly more quickly. I can go a whole vacation without needing to recharge, which is nice, but the included travel bag is handy just in case.

So, overall I'd give it 4.5 stars, only because of the leftover hairs. It would be nice to have a slightly more powerful vacuum, but I realize it's difficult to get the hairs that are trapped in a beard. I love the trimmer, and have not seen anything else out there that would beat it.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text: The Norelco T-980 price was not much more than the cost of replacing the battery in my 10-year old Norelco Maverick T-3000 and I was excited about the addition of a vacuum feature. Be careful what you wish for! The vacuum does its job and sink cleanup is definitely faster. But the vacuum feature tends to obscure your view of the blade edge making it much trickier to aim the thing at your beard's edge while looking in the mirror. The vacuum must be emptied by using thumb pleasure to disengage one side of a rather flimsy, curved compartment cover that swings open on a hinge that looks so weak that I'm afraid it's just a matter of time before I accidentally break either the hinge or snap the cover in half. Equally delicate-feeling are the two sliding, plastic prongs used to hold the primary blade in place. Yet it must be removed each time one wants to use the smaller, more accurate trimming blade. And of course the trimming blade uses similar prongs to hold it in place. My older T-3000 had a self-contained trimming blade that slid forward with a simple thumb push whenever needed and then retracted just as easily. The T-980 is larger around and heavier than the older unit... enough so that I really miss the sense of control and precision I was used to. In short, the T-980 feels clumsier, less maneuverable, and less accurate. It takes longer to complete the job due to the hassle of changing the regular blade and the trimming blade. And it really tries my patience having to be so careful not to beak one of those delicate, sliding, plastic prongs or the vacuum-compartment cover. I'm really tempted to pay the $30 it will cost to restore my old T-3000.

product_title: Braun 8000 360 Complete Foil/Cutter Block for Models 8995, 8985, 8975
review_text:
SEE BOTTOM FOR MY UPDATE: Is the 51s foil and cutter really terrible? Is the 30B foil and cutter really better for your Braun Series 8000 shaver? Is there an Original Equipment foil and cutter still available for the Braun 8985 shaver? Answers: no, no, and no. I have the Braun 8985 shaver and bought BOTH of the foils and cutters mentioned in these reviews: the 51s, which Braun sells as its only replacement now for the 8000 series, and the 30b, which is supposed to be for the Braun 7000/4000 series shavers, but some buyers are saying it works better for the 8000 series shavers than the so-called "terrible" 51s replacement. Both foils and cutters fit my 8985 shavers, and I've shaved serveral times with both. The 51s does NOT pull, cut or irritate my face and gives a very close shave, particularly if I have a 2-day beard. The 30b also gives a good shave, but perhaps not quite as close. Some reviewers say the 51s wears out quickly, is prone to dents and starts irritating your face. If that happens, I will update this review, but so far, so good.

I ordered the 51s by mistake because the seller's web listing did not mention that its "Braun 8000 360 Complete Foil and Cutter Block for Models 8995, 8985 and 8975" is really the controversial 51s replacement. When it arrived with the dreaded 51s name on the package, I immediately ordered the 30b foil and cutter and planned to return the 51s, but I waited until the 30b arrived so I could be sure it worked. It does, but it buzzes differently and didn't shave much closer than my 3-year-old original foil and cutter. The 30b DOES give a more comfortable shave -- it glides over your face like nothing is happening. The shave is fine, what you'd expect from any electric. But Braun is better than "any electric." The 51s is giving me that exceptionally close shave I expect from Braun. You DO feel the 51s a bit more than the 30b, but it's not irritating. I am keeping the 30b in case my 51s goes haywire on me, but for now, the 51s seems better.

UPDATE May 6, 2012: I'm glad I kept the 30b because the 51s did indeed start inflicting red marks on my face, and it stopped shaving as closely. Very disappointing. So now I'm using the 30b, the red marks on my face are gone, and the shave is close. So if I had it to do all over again, I would recommend getting tthe 30b foil and cutter instead of the 51s.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I really wanted to love this trimmer. Especially given the hefty price tag. It trims as you would expect and the vacuum works well and is a must-have feature in my opinion.

Another must have feature is either Ni-Mh battery or the more expensive Lithium ion battery. This has Neither it is the bad/cheapo/old Ni-Cad (Nickel Cadmium) with all the memory effects and shortened life span that implies. For a device like this where you can't swap the battery yourself and you can't leave the job half done you will have to partially charge and then finish your trim. Then you will recharge it fully, boom instant battery memory and shortened life. Or maybe you re-charge it after every use? That may be even worse... I've been through this before, you are doomed to a useful life measured in months before the battery (and therefore the whole trimmer) craps out.

I researched on line and couldn't discover what type of battery it was so I went in person to my local WM and looked at the packaging, still no hint. So I bought it thinking they couldn't possibly sell it at such a high price point with such an unsuitable battery.

I got it home and found in the instructions that the battery is Ni-Cad and soldered into place and must be disposed of properly. I'll be returning it and looking for a different vacuum trimmer with a battery that will be useful for longer than a few months.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
I bought this about a year ago and it was my first electric toothbrush. I wasn't sure if I'd like using an electric but the combination of a low price and great ratings persuaded me to buy it. I have to say it works very well! At my dental checkups the dentist always comments that I don't have much plaque on my teeth and since I've started using it, I have had few cavities. I'm not sure if the toothbrush is responsible for that or not.
One of the best features is that it has a two minute timer, so that I always brush for the amount of time that dentists recommend. It's gotten me into the habit of brushing that long even when I'm using a different toothbrush. My only complaint is that it uses regular AA batteries. I find that the batteries generally last somewhere between two and four weeks, but after a few days the speed of the brush head slows down quite a bit. I tried using rechargeable AAs, but they don't deliver enough current to make the brush run.
Because of the low price and the ease of use, this has been a great electric toothbrush to start out with. I think I'll be getting a rechargeable one in the near future though.

I like to use a little dry shampoo on my roots after I brush through.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
Unfortunately I have to agree with some of the more critical reviews of this product. I say unfortunately, because the vacuum actually works pretty good when the unit is new. But ask those people who rave on and on about this unit how well their trimmer is working after a few months use and i bet you will get a totally different answer. The suction power substantially decreases after a few months of use it and it drops clumps of hair every where. And this is despite cleaning the unit thoroughly after each use.

There are just too many other problems with this trimmer to recommend it. Most namely, it keeps breaking. I'm on my fifth unit in 3 years. Luckily it does have a 2 year warranty and Philips/Norelco has been terrific at replacing them. But, still, this continually breaking is a problem. I think this is mostly due to the cheap plastic build.

I also agree with another review in regards to the ON/OFF and Turbo buttons being in a bad location. Because these buttons are where the fingers naturally sit to hold the trimmer I'm constantly, unintentionally, turning the trimmer off. This is very annoying. And I too have had the unit change to a shorter setting during use. Also very annoying.

product_title: Moroccan Argan Oil Shampoo, 8 Fl Oz - Smooths and Repairs - Sulfate Free - Natural - Imported from Morocco by Pure Body Naturals
review_text: This shampoo is super emollient, lathers nicely, smells fabulous (it says honey and vanilla but it's a little more of a perfume smell, very pleasant).  I used on my children as the baby all in one wash/shampoo wasn't really doing it shampoo wise for my kiddos anymore.  I needed a little more performance (my sons hair is very fuzzy and my daughters is getting longer and tangly) but, still wanted to keep it as natural/chemical free as possible.  Both of my children's hair was great after using and their heads smelt awesome!  My daughters was shiny, smooth and tangle free, my sons was also shiny and extremely soft. I didn't have to use a conditioner for either (a huge bonus since rinsing their hair out is a nightmare).  My issue, and thus a 4 star instead of 5 is 2 fold.  1) at the very end of the ingredients there is an item listed as a series of letters and numbers, when you look it up you find it is a chemical.  I feel the company purposely didn't just list the ingredient name instead as a means to hide this ingredient ( its behentrimonium methosulfate and it's not a surfactant sulfate and is rated a 0 on the list of dangers.  Zero being the best rating) I am fine with this ingredient, I do appreciate full transparency however.  2) this particular form is made in China and the bottle states "product of morocco" and "bottled in China".  I try to avoid things made in China and I feel this labeling hides the fact that this shampoo includes an ingredient made in China.  Again, transparency becomes an issue here.  Neither of these are a deal breaker but, I do feel the bottle is labeled to be purposely misleading.  I was given this product as a sample in order to try it and share my thoughts on it.

review_title: Not tested in animals; Hypoalergenic and sulfate free!
review_text:
I'm a person that loves fragrances, specially natural oils.
I have a diffuser, I add natural essential oils to all my homemade lotions, shampoos, conditioners, body scrubs. My favorite scents are peppermint, sandalwood and argan.

I have tried a few other brands of argan shampoo, and as someone who loves skin and hair products, i'm always on the lookout for brands I haven't tried yet. The ones that work best for my skin and hair, I become a recurring customer.

I have other products from Pure Body Naturals; I like the fact that their products strive to use natural ingredients, mostly are hypoallergenic, and this shampoo is sulfate free.
This shampoo is very thick and dense, you don't need to use much to wash your hair; it doesn't lather - because it's sulfate free. I have no problem with it not lathering. If you think products need to lather to clean, you're mistaken. Sulfate strips your hair of it's natural oils, making it much weaker, brittle, and dry, that's why you need conditioner after a sulfate full shampoo.
I did not use conditioner after this shampoo, and i wash my hair twice, once to remove dirt, and second to rinse and coat my hair with the "goodies" in this shampoo; specially because i work in the elements and with animals, my hair and scalp need good cleaning.

My hair smells absolutely amazing, looks healthy, shiny, strong and clean. It brushed easily, no snagging, no knots. Very silky and soft.

I love the pump, a couple of squirts and no lid to close, and if it falls in the shower, it won't spill everywhere.

Very well made product, great natural ingredients, awesome smell! Highly satisfied!!! OH! Very important: NOT tested on animals!
Although i've received this product discounted, my review is an expression of the uses i put it through.

review_text: This thing is as good as original one that I paid $100+ and it died on me after number of years, at least if this dies, I only out $16 bucks, highly recommend it. I added silicon lube around the o-ring of the cap, going to stick to one set of rechargeable batteries in case the rusting gets worse.  I still think it's a lot cheaper to replace my rechargeable batteries IF they do go out, which I don't think it's going to happen anytime soon, than to replace the whole brush when internal battery goes out.  I got this on sale ($16) with free shipping, I plan to order more when I see it on sale again.

review_title: Good oil with a lot of uses
review_text:
I love this company's products. I love that they are organic and not tested on animals. This castor oil comes in a nice 4 oz bottle and a little goes a long way, so this should last you a long while. I do wish it had a pump dispenser or something other than just a screw top. It can be a bit difficult to use oil without making a mess. It would be much easier to control with a pump. There are so many uses for this great stuff, tons of DIY beauty recipes out there. I plan on doing something with this at several times a week, if not everyday. This oil great for moisturizing my super dry facial skin and long curly hair. My face and hair are always dry, but of course, cooler weather does a number on them. I plan to use this regularly in my hair as a mask since my hair is already thin and sheds terribly. I hope to gain the thickening benefits of this soon.

The oil is clear, thicker than most other oils and a bit sticky, so bear that in mind when using on your hands, etc. if you'll need to do anything immediately after applying it. It will take awhile to absorb. The smell is somewhat earthy, yet very light. It isn't overwhelming at all and dissipates quickly. Overall, I am very pleased with this oil.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I've owned this for like a week now and my first time using it I was FREAKEN amazed. I had a crappy old vacuum beard trimmer by Remmington that I replaced because It would never trim evenly, even if I really really tried, I'd always end up with a bald spot on my chinstrap haha. I actually finally dropped it one day and bent one of the plastic trimming guides so I said to hell with this damn thing!

I always trimmed in a downward fashion with my old one because if I went up it would reduce it to stubble even with the right length setting. So I busted this beast out set it to 4 turned it on and put it on turbo (sorry I'm a sucker for a things that say turbo hah)! The trimming head actually bends to the contours of your face and trims every single hair to the same height when shaving upward. Now my chinstrap no longer looks patchy it's just full and even, don't waste your time with scissors or a "bunk" trimmer, get this one! I didn't have a giant beard for my first shave but I'm sure this thing can get through the narliest of beards...not that you would ever wanna shave a good beard off. So for the beard lover and facial hair perfectionist, this thing does an A+++ job!

Just for review integrity I personally did not purchase this, my mother purchased it for me as a gift! :)
She, and the girlfriend loved the difference.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I'm a person who has used several types of clippers in the past, both corded and cordless and I've gotta say this is one of the best! Originally discovered it on Amazon when I was in the market to replace my former cordless clipper and was impressed by the high rating. Now I'm singing its praises too.

I've been using it for over a year now and would definitely buy another if I had to... but I don't! It's still going strong with a powerful battery and the suction of loose hair even allows me to shave in the car when I'm pressed for time. I would say as long as you shave in the proper direction (where the blade cuts first and the suction thingy follows) the shaver will suck in at least 85% of the loose hair it cuts. Usually I have very little hair left on the sink after I shave. The fact that it's cordless is a plus and the device gives just enough options with the adjustable guard and the precision blade. A full charge last me long enough for me to forget when was the last time I charged it and I love the fact that it's a good size and weight for travel. A great buy at a good price!

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Doesn't do what I need - returned it the next day
review_text:
I bought this to replace a 4 year old Norelco G390 which served me reasonably well for the past 4 years till its NiCd battery died (bought at a "warehouse" store for just under $20).
There are over 600 reviews with an average of 4 stars and I thought "how can 600+ people be wrong?" so I bought it.

Dumb idea.

I won't go through all the pros and not even all the cons so you'll need to read other reviews, I'll just focus on why I simply can't use it and had to return it:

1. The distance from the comb interface to the blade - the part that goes up and down and stays at the same distance from the blade - is 1/8 inch longer than on the G390. This is due to the vacuum duct. As a result I was simply not able to get all the way up my mustache to trim it - it simply hit the nose. Other angles of approach or even the lowest trim setting didn't work. I was left with a funny looking longer part of the mustache and looking like a dictator from the previous century which i will not name. I ended up taking the comb attachment off the blade and, using a real comb like hairdressers used to do, trimmer the rest of the way manually. Suffice to say I did not pay $[...] so I could do that.
I'll post the image comparing the G390 to this one on Amazon and you can see for yourself how it limit the reach of the blade.

2. The vacuum is useless. Sure, it capture a lot of the hair but enough of it drop out too. There is no way I would use it anywhere else but over a sink and even then I'll have to clean both the sink and the little transparent bin - so why pay extra.

I've returned it to Amazon the next day.

I'm going to look for the G390 or another similar model from Norelco - the G390 was about half price, didn't have vacuum or direct AC but did have multiple attachments, upright stand and lasted 4 years despite the antiquated battery technology.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Good blend of power and convenience
review_text:
I bought this mainly to use on my beard, which grows quickly. Overall, I like it. It's not the best (most powerful) trimmer I've ever had, but its other features make up for what it lacks in power.

The adjustable comb is easy to use and I don't have to dig through the drawer in the bathroom to find a snap-on #3 comb I like to use and therefore always lose. The vacuum feature is nice and makes cleaning up small jobs easier, especially since I don't have to sweep hair off a wet sink afterwards. Cleaning is straightforward as all the pieces come apart and go back together pretty easily. The turbo feature is also helpful. My beard is very coarse, and tends to jam up most trimmers. This one gets hung up sometimes, but if I go slowly and don't try to cut too much at once, it works fine.

One note: The hair "reservoir" under the vacuum fills up quickly, so it's better to use this more often on smaller jobs than waiting to do a bigger trim.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
Functionally, this trimmer worked fine. Not even sure they make it any more. However, I have a problem when the design philosophy is based on designed obsolescence. When the rechargeable battery on this unit (and I owned two of them over the years) finally failed to recharge the product's life is over. I does have a cord but won't run off a wall outlet if the battery won't recharge. I've been left with two perfectly mechanically functional beard trimmers that will no longer run because of the design. I find such design decisions reprehensible from an environmental perspective, and shady from a business perspective.

Has Norelco fixed this in their more recent models? Don't know. I won't buy the brand any more.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: Love this brush! Pay less for this model, use rechargeables, you'll never go back
review_text:
Everybody knows that Sonicare cleans better and stimulates gum tissues better than a regular toothbrush, right? But why pay $100+ for the super duper model when you can get this one for much less and just use rechargeable AA batteries in it? Some say water gets into the battery compartment, but I haven't had that trouble. It sits on my sink with the clear cap on it until I'm ready to brush, and I'd say it probably gets splashed with water at least once a day when my toddler is washing his hands, but no water seeps into the compartment. A fully charged pair of AA batteries last me about two weeks. When the batteries are low, it completely stops. You don't have to wonder if it's brushing well, because it will either brush "full blast" or not at all. No in-between. I liked this brush so well that I convinced my husband to get one, too. I know it will pay off with a great dental checkup!

2 year update: STILL love it! And I've had some really great dental checkups since I started using it! Okay, those could be due to the combination of using a better toothbrush that really stimulates the gums to keep them healthy AND flossing more regularly (about 3 times per week as opposed to MAYBE once). But I'll admit something: I'm only brushing about once per day instead of twice. *shame* I have to chase two little ones and frankly I put off brushing most mornings. So factor that in, and it's AMAZING that I get good checkups, right? Just wanted to weigh in on the long-term use. Love this brush! (PS: I use the "compact" size brush head and really love it. It helps me brush better in the back, and I think that makes a big difference.)

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
This is my second trimmer. My first, a Remington was at least 15 years old and worked like a champ. It had it's problems like many of these in holding the desired length. But you learn to hold it tight so it won't change while trimming. I babied the batteries for years and quite honestly if you don't, with Ni-Cads you'll be replacing them or the trimmer a lot sooner.

I like this one and was concerned by some of the negative reviews. I don't use a lot of pressure when trimming so I haven't seen it change (shorten) while trimming. The vacuum feature is nice and works well. Others complained about getting up under the nose. This is no different from any others I've tried that use a blade guard.

I'd give it 5 stars if I had it longer. So far so good and has lived up to or beyond my expectations. I'm still on the first charge so time will tell. If it lasts half as long as my Remington I'll be happy.

product_title: Collapsible Hair Diffuser by The Curly Co. with The Curly Co. Satisfaction Guarantee
review_text:
I was SO excited for this diffuser. I bought because I was going on a 2 week trip throughout Europe and because I was hopping countries, I needed to pack light.. but my curly hair needed to also be tamed, haha.

I was so mad when it came in.. it did not fit my travel sized hair dryer!!!! UGH. So, I tried to squeeze it on my regular hair dryer...... didn't fit. Kept thinking I must not be putting this on correctly, because they advertise it fits on most hair dryers! Grabbed my roommate.. she tried. She couldn't fit them either. The end of the diffuser is a little stretchy, but not stretchy to fit either of my hair dryers.. Determined, we tried my roommates hair dryer as well.. IT DIDNT FIT. This is terrible. Well, I finally got it to fit on my travel size because I ended up putting one of the attachments on the hair dryer; the one where it's like a flathead. Once I did that, the diffuser awkwardly fit over it, but at times will slip off because it's not a circle shape it's stuck on to. Once I added the attachment, the diffuser did end up working pretty decently. So, I took it all to Europe.

Another con to this, one of the six nodules on the face of the diffuser fell off! UGH! Maybe because the air flowing through was too hot and it warped because it's plastic? I'm not sure. I have no idea where it went though, so that sucks. and then when I took the diffuser off the hairdryer, there's a little plastic cap on the inside center of the diffuser that popped off as well! ...This seems to either be a faulty diffuser that I was sent, or these are actually just insanely cheaply made.

I do like how the silicone diffuses my curls... but because of all the MAJOR setbacks that I've dealt with, this is not worth it. ...Unless like I mentioned, I was just sent a faulty diffuser. :/

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: Great value, better than the rechargeables!
review_text:
I bought this toothbrush in July 2012 and have been using it daily for ~18 months and I couldn't be happier!

I used to own the same Sonicare but with a rechargeable battery and a charging stand. I was very happy with it until the battery refused to hold a charge for more than 10 seconds (admittedly it took quite a while to die). In that model, there is no way to replace it so it went in the trash.

I bought this one and it has been great so far! Definitely a better value than the rechargeable ones. It brushes just as well as my old one but won't wear out. It eats up batteries quite slowly, much more slowly than I had anticipated. It is durable as well (I'm super clumsy and have dropped a few times).

Overall no complaints, even after all this time. Btw, all the reviewers complaining that water gets into the battery compartment aren't that clever. I have avoided all such problems by laying the toothbrush on its side. No water can get at the batteries if you don't stand it upright. Definitely a great purchase!

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I must say that I disagree with most reviewers on this product. I have several problems with the design which I would like to share.

First, a disclaimer. The product title says that it is a hair "trimmer" and not a "clipper". Perhaps I did not see the distinction at first, but I see that others purchase this unit as a clipper as well. So, as a trimmer (used very frequently and with very short hair trimmings) this unit may work for you. But even as a trimmer, if the hair is cut at any length (and there are 9 settings to the guide), this thing is useless.

First, the "on" and "turbo" buttons are too easy to push while handling, and I'm constantly startling myself with the turbo setting (it is a little loud). Also, I find that the guide/vacuum design is poor. This may work OK if you are trimming short guide settings, but if you get a clump of hair in the guide, which happens constantly with me, it will block the tiny opening for the hair cup. The vacuum is not strong enough to pull the hair in, and it clogs the whole works. If you do not notice this, the blockage will prevent the trimmer from trimming, and you may think that a lower guide setting is needed. You can see how this sets you up for a scalp job when the low guide setting is finally low enough to make a cut. I just find the whole set up "gimmicky" and I will take the old standard guides and no vacuum any day.

It does have a strong battery and if you are just lightly trimming a mustache or a beard, it may be the right choice for you. I think people like me would not be disappointed (and would not have purchased the product) if it had been called the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Beard and Mustache Vacuum Trimmer. Long title, but descriptive enough to avoid purchasing the wrong product.

I will say that this is much better to use than the Remington 3000 that I have seen selling for nearly $100 on Amazon (which I originally bought for $50).

I generally like the shave.

I would recommend that this be the first one you try - you may not want to go to any others.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Amazing Trimmer... that doesn't hold the trimming level.
review_text:
I was incredibly excited to get this trimmer. I previously had a Norelco Trimmer that I absolutely loved and thought worked wonderful. After a few years of use the battery didn't hold much charge and I finally lost the charger after traveling!

I looked at the trimmers available and the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer sounded great. I was a little worried about purchasing it however because I read some users were having problems with the trimming guard moving position. I thought I'd give it a try and if it didn't work, I'd send it back... and ultimately I was hoping the people having troubles were just incompetent.

I charged the trimmer for a day. Played around with the trimming guard by pushing on it and moving it up and down and it seemed to be extremely solid and sturdy. It seemed like it locked in position just fine.

After starting to trim on a safe level 6 (my goatie had gotten long, waiting for a new trimmer) I was having success. While gliding the trimmer up the side of my goatie, WHOOPS, it slipped to Level 4. Oh well, I said, I guess I'm going to have a level 4 goatie. Well to sum it up, about halfway into it I was surprised with a slip to level 2.

The vacuum is wonderful, it works perfectly. But honestly, do you really give a crap if you have to shave at a level 2 every stinking time? Why didn't I send it back? The package was impossible to open, I had to cut and rip it in shreds. It's hard to go without a trimmer but PLEASE read this review and know that you WILL have problems with it slipping trim guards, I guarantee it.

The design of the trim guard dial is part of the problem. I'm not going to sit here and tell Philips how to design a trimmer though, they've done it correctly in the past.

BOTTOM LINE: Great idea, new innovations work great, but as a trimmer this is a piece of junk because you can't shave at any level higher than a number 2 without risk of ending up 2 levels lower or MORE.

review_text: Bought this to replace an older model Norelco trimmer without a vacuum function. My only complaint, and it's not really a complaint, is I did like the simplicity of my older model in just removing the hair comb to use the trimmer head for the detail work.  Because of the vacuum attachment you can't do that with this trimmer, you need to remove the comb, and then replace the trimmer head with a smaller trimmer attachment that sticks up past the vaccuum catch.  This attachement works well, but it is a little on the small side and I'm still getting used to it.  It works fine, but I wish you didn't need to go that extra step of switching out the trimmer blades.  If you don't really care about the vacuum function you might want to keep in mind that trade off.  Overall, I am very pleased with the purchase, and you can't beat it for under $30 shipped.

well, i had the older model of this trimmer for a couple of years now and decided it's time to get a new one.

so when the battery dies on you in the middle of a trim, you are not left with half your face unshaven.

bottom line - killer trimmer. i like it.
get it.

update:
no more pinching. the self sharpening was the issue. works smoothly now.
the vacuum feature is still not really what i expected it to be. still have to clean up after i'm done.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
This product is good while it lasts; it'll clean your teeth better than almost anything out there (unless you have tartar, then you'll need something with a bit more power) and stimulate your gums. However, having autopsied this model, I am convinced that it was engineered to fail under typical conditions after a time, perhaps to motivate the purchase of a more expensive model, which will itself become useless when the irreplaceable batteries go out.

The first one I bought lasted a year, and even that long only after I learned that you have to plug the two holes in the back of the battery compartment to prevent the corrosion from taking place. By the end, batteries were lasting one week tops, at 2x use per day. I also learned that you have to hit it against hard objects when it won't turn on and sometimes then it'll go. You also need to scrape off any rust from the battery contacts occasionally.

Knowing these quirks, I bought another one and immediately plugged up the holes in the back and put tape around the battery cap. However, it has now lasted only a month. There's no rust or corrosion to speak of, however, it just doesn't turn on anymore.

Today I autopsied the first sonicare to see why it had failed (the new one is still on warranty). In taking it apart, it's clear that most of your money goes into buying a tank-like shell around the $1 worth of electronics. This would be a good thing, if there were not two gaping holes in the battery cap that let water in anyway and the shoddy rubber seal. After taking it apart, it's clear why the corrosion so quickly leads the failure. They protect everything on the circuit-board from corrosion by putting glue over it, except the battery contacts, and the contacts and wires that lead to the solenoid coil (that makes the brush vibrate). The contacts that lead to the solenoid and the battery contacts are also strategically located next to each other on the circuit board, so they can corrode together quickly using any moisture from the adjacent battery-terminal holes, while the non-essentials like the timer are located on the other side of the board and completely sealed off from the ambient air by glue. This also explains why hitting it sometimes allows it to start; you're shaking some of the corrosion loose.

The switch is also of questionable design, being nothing more than a paper-thin piece of plastic with some kind ring on it that's slightly more conductive than the plastic.

If the replacement that I get out of the warranty fails, I think I'll try a cybersonic or an oral-b; hopefully their teams of engineers weren't paid to make something less reliable than a politician.

Why can't they make a sonic toothbrush with no batteries, that plugs into the wall, and lasts a lifetime? Or just quit making these to fail so readily?

Now 7-months later. I had some qualms about this unit because of the reviewers who had them die by water damage. I would say it is probably not safe to leave this unit in standing water (like a cup that accumulates water in the bottom), but otherwise with normal usage and storing it dry, there was absolutely no problem. I use rechargeable batteries and they last well over a week using twice a day. I get the impression they go longer between charges than the rechargeable units.
I have had a lot of rechargeable units in the past, but at half the price and the same performance (without bells and whistles) I shall stick to this type. To me it is the best buy by far.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text: I purchased this to replace a 3.5 year old Norelco T990 when its batteries died. I *loved* the T990 and would buy it again, but it's no longer available. (The current T765 is a similar design to the T990.) T980 issues: The electronic power and turbo switches are touch sensitive and too easy to press while trimming. The settings window is tiny and it's hard to read the number. The mini trimmer is an inconvenient attachment. When using the trimmer without the comb/guide, like for neck cleanup, the vacuum tube blocks your view of the cutter. These were enough to make me return the trimmer to Norelco with their 60-day return policy. There was also an issue that may be a defect in the trimmer I received. It would not hold the selected setting. While using it, it would change to a shorter setting! Yikes! I ended-up replacing the batteries in my beloved T990 for about the same price as the T765. Unless you must have the vacuum and one-hour charge time, buy the less expensive T765. [[ASIN:B0001HYL0M Philips Norelco T765 AccuTrim Beard and Moustache Trimmer]]

review_text: I bought this for the very dry skin under my eyebrows. No medical condition; simply chronic dry skin in that area made worse by pretty strong acne face wash. review_text: I have owned various panasonic beard trimmers for past 20 years, untli the non-replaceable batteries go bad.  This is the first one I have had which sucks the trimmings into a built-in container, which is a great idea.  The problem is it clogs every 2-3 strokes, which makes it unusable.  Now, if you use this on a daily or every 2-3 day basis, and are cutting hairs taht are 1/8" long, for instance, I bet it would work well.  But when you do trimming every 1-2 weeks, and the hair is 1/4" or longer for head hair, it will clog, and this product is not for you.  So I would give it 0 stars if you are like me, or 4 stars if you plan on using it constantly, for an overall score of 2 stars.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text: I got mine around three weeks ago.  The good news is that it cuts my beard well, and the vacuum is not noisy.  The bad news is 1) the controls are positioned such that I find myself accidently hitting the on/off switch as I am shaving, no huge deal but annoying, 2) the vacuum action catches 95% of the hairs but 95% means you still have to clean up afterwards so it is of dubious value, and most importantly 3) it does not hold its distance setting.  I find that, as I shave, the shave length setting can very easily be pushed down so that I end up with a much shorter beard than I intended.  I can't imagine why after all these years Norelco has not come up with a better system for locking down the shave length so that it does not get changed by the mere act of shaving.  In my opinion this last issue makes it a dud product that fails at its intended function, and I would recommend against buying it.

review_title: Good, not great, with a flaw
review_text:
The trimmer works pretty well. It trims my beard and moustache adequately and to the length I want, but not on first pass. That is a problem with this trimmer too: it has a rechargeable but not replaceable battery. When the battery no longer takes a charge, as with my old trimmer, the trimmer will not run even when the cord is plugged in. I would prefer a trimmer that is corded, with no battery, or with a replaceable rechargeable battery. What Norelco has done is created a trimmer with built in obsolescence. When the battery is dead, the trimmer is done for. And batteries are not environmentally friendly.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: So good I bought two of them
review_text:
I travel a lot between two places and one of the things I bought for the 2nd place was this razor, so I wouldn't have to carry one back and forth. This razor impressed me so much I bought one for my 1st place to replace what I had been using.

The major pros of this product: Solid feel, the vacuum feature definitely reduces the amount of hair in the sink (and on the counter, on the floor, etc.), the Turbo mode, while loud, is awesome. The razor cuts well, fast, and can do very straight lines (and I don't have very steady hands).

There is at least one caveat, which other reviewers mentioned: For detailed, close trimming, you're cutting blind with this razor. I use a cheaper Norelco to even up corners and other tight spaces. Also, the power brick is a bit large, and there's no included charging base.

However, the product works well, feels solid in my hands, and it looks cool :-). I have about 6 electric razors and I highly recommend this one.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
Here's the deal: If you own the rechargeable version of a Sonicare, chances are you CANNOT use that base charger in a foreign country when voltage is outside the USA's 110-120 range. Therefore, having a battery-operated Sonicare is the best alternative not only because it uses 2 AA batteries (standard or rechargeable) but because there are no additional accessories to drag along AND it's very affordable.

For those with broken or defective brushes: SAY HELLO TO THE TWO YEAR WARRANTY. A quick toll-free phone call to Phillips nets you a replacement device FREE of shipping charges. Did I mention it's a TWO YEAR warranty? Not 90 days, not 1 year, but TWO YEARS.

I buy a few of these E3000 brushes at a time to give as gifts and every receipient has been happy with it -- some have even upgraded to the higher-end rechargeable models because they are so amazed with how well these brushes clean your teeth.

The only thing you're missing is the Sonicare AirFloss -- get one of those, too!
