review_text: Where do I start? This product is everything that you see, with the exception of one thing and I'll refer to that later. The packaging alone is amazing. You get this neat sturdy box to keep all your supplies organized. All tools are made of solid material. You're not getting some flimsy products that someone just threw together to create a bundle. I'm very happy with that. I did one test nail to determine the consistency of the gel itself and it's very easy to work with. It's just stiff enough to use the slip solution and it not water down the product. This is very important because once you place the dual form on top of your natural nail, it doesn't ooze out as much around the cuticle. I especially like the dual forms included because they have smaller sizes. My pinky is a size 3 with a nail bed of a 6 year old lol. I finally found something that I really like and works. Now, you see the black envelope in the pic? It's full of surprises and goodies. Such a sweet touch. They included free nail forms. Ironically the same brand that I ordered at the same time I placed this order. And if that isn't enough, the envelope also includes another generous gift of great value but I won't disclose it here. You're just gonna have to get your own to find out 😁 I don't want to spoil it for you. The only thing I found a little disappointing in this kit is the colors. They're a translucent jelly type instead of the solid colors I thought I was getting from other review photos. This is the reason I had to give 4 stars instead of 5 😔.  I contacted the seller who explained that this is the only colors they carry but will consider adding more. I decided to just keep it and add more colors to my kit because the overall value is worth it when you include the tools. I'm sure I'll find something creative to do with the colors that came. Support responded to my inquiry immediately. I ordered this product one day and received it the next. Over all, great product, great support, great value. I'm satisfied.

review_text: Purchased this product in Oct 2018. Primarily used for misting indoor plants. Very fine water mist and smooth trigger function. Helped the indoor plants immensely. Used it once or twice a day during weekdays. Worked beautifully for about 9 months then the trigger abruptly went from smooth to jammed. I kept on using it because the nozzle was still spraying the mist correctly. That is until today. Now there is just a jet stream that comes out. I will be more than happy to maintain or repair the nozzle myself. But the product designers, intentionally or unintentionally, have made any access to the nozzle parts impossible. Therefore, we the consumers, have no option but to toss the entire product in the garbage and buy a new mister. Agreed, it is inexpensive and agreed it works well initially. But the mister does not have a sustainable and a durable design. The designers should not hide behind the excuse that the parts are plastic. They can absolutely create a modular design where the plastic parts can be replaced instead of tossing the whole bottle away.  Creating products that do not last long and create massive garbage is a future we cannot subscribe to.  Happy with the product intent. But disappointed in the design thought and durability of the product. Hence the three stars.

product_title: Braun 8000 360 Complete Foil/Cutter Block for Models 8995, 8985, 8975
review_text:
I've had my Braun 8595 for 5 years. I LOVED MY BRAUN!!! It was worth every penny of the original purchase price, and the cost of previous replacement foils. I went to buy my third set of replacement foils to discover the Model 8000 Activator, the original shaver foil and cutter block, had been discontinued and replaced with the 360* Complete, so I bought that. Braun had been great, and never let me down before.

I have fairly tough skin, but this new head caused horrible, painful razor burn. It's the worst on the neck, but it causes it everywhere. Rather than simply cutting the hair as I moved the razor across my face like the original foils had, the new one grabs my skin and hair and drags them along before finally cutting. As a result of the painful dragging of the skin and hair before eventually cutting it, the shave is not as close since it isn't cutting the hair straight on as the razor with the original foils did. Now it hurts to get a lousy shave.

Braun must want us to buy the new Pulsonic, but I'm not falling for it. They'll just mess up the foil and cutter again once a newer razor comes out.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
I have been using this brush now since Approximately November 1, 2010. I use it every night but not in the mornings and am totally pleased with it. Two thoughts might be helpful for those reading about problems with the water seal on the bottom of the handle and battery usage.

1)I was flabbergasted once I started using the brush by the comments of those who had trouble with the water seal. I suspect there are two types of brush users. Those like myself who keep their lips closed while brushing and therefore have no water drip down the brush whatsoever. And then I suppose there must be people who brush their teeth with their moth open and the brush handle pointed down and let water and saliva and paste drool down the handle. I suppose it would be possible to get moisture to the bottom cap of the battery compartment is you did this regularly and perhaps some moisture could get in. Or perhaps if you rinsed the brush but also rinsed the whole handle you could get moisture in.

So if when you brush your entire handle does not regularly get wet, then this complaint about the water seal will have no effect on you.

2) My experience with battery usage has been that the two AA batteries supplied with the unit lasted from 11/2/2010 until 1/16/2011 being used once a night for two minutes. Two rechargeable NiMH batteries are still going strong as of today 3/6/2011 with the same usage rate.

The brush head is still in fine condition and not splayed out.

I hope this helps folks trying to decide on this unit. Seems ridiculous to pay for a more expensive model that is virtually the same but with unneeded "features"

ADDED COMMENTS AS OF 6/5/2012: My and my wife's brushes are still going strong with no signs of fatigue, breakdown, or water seal problems. We continue to use NiMH rechargeable batteries and get months of use out of a charge. I just came back from my dentist today and they have noticed an obvious improvement in my gum health. I will be ordering another one to use in another bathroom which will be more convenient for morning brushing before leaving for work. Great product and great price savings over the unnecessary added "features" of th higher priced models!

review_text:
I've had this trimmer for about 1 year now. It doesn't get a lot of use, I only trim about every 1.5-2 weeks (yes, I'm a bit lazy like that). So at most, I've used the trimmer about 35 times. It should work longer and better than that.

A few uses ago I went to pull out the little plastic trimmings compartment and the front of the compartment pulled off, leaving the rest inside the unit. It appears that these pieces are just glued together.

The second strike is that it doesn't catch about 20% of the trimmed hair, even in Turbo mode. I've tried it trimming very short amounts of hair, or longer. It doesn't seem to matter much.

The third strike is that 2-3 times during a trimming I have to remove the trimming guide, and then the blades to remove hair from underneath the blades. I don't see why hair should get trapped under there, but it does and reduces the trimming ability significantly. I don't think I should have to dismantle the trimmer to trim my beard. It's done this since day one.

Otherwise, it works pretty well. With some patience and a bit of mess it does a pretty good job at trimming. This is my third Norelco trimmer, none of them seem to have much staying power, my other two had similar clogging issues with the blade, and both had the rechargeable battery die.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
The vibrating is unpleasant at first, but you get used to it. And you grow to appreciate the intense feeling because you know that it is precisely that motion that makes your teeth so damn clean.

This is an excellent toothbrush. It's the cheapest of the adult brushes in the sonicare line and sonicare is way better than any other electric toothbrush. And any electric toothbrush is way better than a manual toothbrush. Electric toothbrushes are not about being lazy, they're about being time-and-energy efficient when cleaning your teeth. Example: 2 minutes with a sonicare brush makes your mouth around 75% cleaner than 2 minutes with a manual brush. Maybe 25% cleaner than 2 minutes with a different electric toothbrush that isn't sonicare.

And you honestly don't need to spend $100 or $200 on one of the more expensive brushes in the Sonicare line either, since this does the same work for less money. It uses 2 AA batteries, and I use rechargeable ones, which makes it more convenient than charging the brush every night. I just swap my one pair of rechargeable AA's for my other pair when I need to, and so it is easier to travel with the brush.

The sonicare technology was recommended by my dentist, and I found it here on Amazon for cheaper than what the dentist was selling it for, with the buy-from-dentist rebate INCLUDED. You could always win an eBay auction and possibly get one for cheaper than this, but I was too impatient to wait, and most auctions I saw ended around $30 anyway.

Did I mention that I love my Sonicare Xtreme?

Allow me to make an above point clear: If you want to spend $100-$200 on a toothbrush, then just buy 3 to 6 Sonicare Xtremes, and then give them to your family and friends. The Sonicare Xtreme uses the same brush heads as ALL THE OTHER SONICARE E-SERIES BRUSHES. These brushes are the top of the line, and the Xtreme has the exact same essential functions as the rest of the Sonicare family does, except for $100-$150 less. I recommend you don't waste your money on a more expensive brush just because it is more expensive.

Do some more research and see that Sonicare brushes are the best for consumer oral hygiene. Then do more research and see that the Sonicare Xtreme has all the necessary features that the other Sonicare brushes have. Then buy it, and keep your teeth for longer. You and all the people who have to look at your teeth or smell your breath in your life will be happy you did.

review_title: A dental visit at home. Amazing!
review_text: This set of dental tools for at home is honestly amazing. I was hesitant from reviews but it does work great. I have some not awful but still bad calculus build up on my teeth. The calculus remover with little effort got the majority off the front of my bottom teeth that most bugged me. I used the metal tools to scrape a bit of the harder stuff on the front. Then I’d go back over it with the tool. Even more impressive was what it did on the inside of my bottom row. I definitely had a few mm of calculus between teeth built up. It cleared out chunks around my teeth. I will note I used a combination of the remover and scraping with the tool included. The tool itself though did do some of the removal and was better around the gums especially as it’s not as sharp. The best way is to scrape with the point between teeth. Then use the side of the metal too to scrape off of the tooth surface. Then use the tool to go over and break up the calculus. So for the price this is such a great value! Not that you want to skip the dentist but of you don’t have a major issue this is a GREAT inexpensive way to keep up on regular tooth health between visits.

product_title: Collapsible Hair Diffuser by The Curly Co. with The Curly Co. Satisfaction Guarantee
review_text:
I have fine, curly hair, and use a Conair dryer with attached diffuser every day at home. I purchased this collapsible diffuser to use exclusively with my travel blow dryer (https://smile.amazon.com/dp/B00006IV22/ref=cm_cr_ryp_prd_ttl_sol_2?th=1) when traveling, and have used it a few times now. Overall, it works like it's supposed to and takes up a lot less space compared to my every-day diffuser. Some other reviewers commented about the tight fit when putting the diffuser on. I also had a hard time with this, but once it was on there wasn't a problem. Other commenters also mentioned the diffuser collapsing. I didn't have a problem with this, but I tend to hold the diffuser and not the dryer while I'm drying my hair. However, it isn't sturdy enough to lift my hair at the roots like my every-day, non-collapsible diffuser is. Pros: compact design (collapses to about an inch); light; easy to remove from dryer and collapse; diffuses the air like it's supposed to.

Cons: a little hard to fit over the dryer nozzle; not as sturdy compared to non-collapsible diffusers; not strong enough to lift the hair at the roots for drying.

product_title: Moroccan Argan Oil Shampoo, 8 Fl Oz - Smooths and Repairs - Sulfate Free - Natural - Imported from Morocco by Pure Body Naturals
review_text:
I live in interior Alaska and during the winter my hair gets really dehydrated. I am always on the look out for better hair products so I was eager to try this shampoo. I have tried so many different products over the past few years and nothing has really worked, my hair is always left with a thick residue or else not hydrated enough. I have been using Wen products for the past few months but I was still underwhelmed by the results. The first time that I used this shampoo I used it as my shampoo and used the Wen as my conditioner. I am ecstatic with the results! My hair feels absolutely amazing. It is super shiny, soft without being frizzy, and it feels stronger than before. I usually wear my hair in a bun or ponytail at work and I have not had as much breakage since starting this shampoo.

The shampoo comes with a lot of product and a little bit goes a long way. I have very long hair so I had to use a little bit more than the bottle recommended but it was still only a quarter size amount. The smell is very subtle and nice, it is almost a light floral smell. product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
Although I am definitely on the 'Sonicare' bandwagon in so far as this product's ability to clean my teeth--it does a great job--this model brush is made quite poorly.

The battery compartment (the e3000 uses 'AA' batteries) on mine, regardless of it having an o-ring on the door, seems to be continually wet inside, with the negative (-) terminal on one of the AA-cells rusting after only two weeks use. Philips acknowledges this is a problem but offers no solution.

Also, there are many small crevices in/around the nameplate on the side, and a large gap under the nut for the brush-head that accumulates 'gook' on a daily basis. Philips advises that this is probably 'mold' and the brush should be 'disassembled and air-dried' after every use. It takes longer to do this than to brush my teeth--

Again, while this is probably one of the best ways to clean your teeth at this point in time, and an economical way to try one of the products that normally start out at $64e (and up), there is no reason why the e3000 shouldn't be made as well as the better units, or hold up to water/daily use as well as some of the $9 Crest electrics we commonly see.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
I've owned this toothbrush for nearly a year now and have no problems. I do, however, recognize the limitations of the design. If you expect to be able to rinse off the handle or submerge this toothbrush, you will be one of the many disappointed reviewers. Now, I owned two previous sonicare toothbrushes and I was never really happy with the life of the internal batteries. This is the reason I decided to go with this unit and I have not regretted my decision. My 12 year old daughter has also had this toothbrush for almost a year now and NO problems. While I do believe there could be inconsistencies in quality control, I think one can work around these shortfalls.

Here's how I believe I've managed to keep my sonicare running.
1. I don't put the handle under water, only the part that goes in my mouth
2. I ALWAYS make sure to place a little vasoline on the O-Ring when I replace the batteries
3. I fling the water off the brush after I rinse the end off.
4. I don't leave the brush standing up. This prevents any residual water from running down the handle. I always leave the brush laying out flat/horizontal.

Now, I realize one shouldn't have to do all this stuff to keep the brush working properly but, for me, it's a small inconvenience considering I have the ability to change the batteries.

Bottom line. I really like my toothbrush but the design is not bullet proof.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I have owned the Norelco T980 for a few months now, and it is great. I had a previous Norelco model for about 4 years and finally it just stopped holding a charge so I bought the T980. With the old Norelco my wife used to complain about little hairs all over the sink. No more! It may not capture every single hair, but I would say it gets a good 90-95% of them. Regardless, it vacuums up enough of the hairs to keep my wife happy!

In my mind the only two small items that keep it from being a 5-star product are: 1) it does not have a pop-up trimmer like my old model did - you have to take the regular blade off and put on the trimmer blade, but that is the price you pay for having the vacuum feature, and 2) its harder to get up close and trim under my nose - it can be done, it just takes more effort than before; again I think its the price you pay for the vacuum feature. Overall I have had great luck with Norelco trimmers and this one is no exception.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I'm a repeat Norelco user. Having read some of the other reviewers' complaints of "excessive noise" and "soft" depth settings, and considering the somewhat vague description of the T980 Turbo, I was hesitant, but bought it anyway.

I'm happy to say the T980 is an improvement in every way over my old faithful trimmer (T970 maybe? I threw it away after a couple of days with this one). I'd used my old trimmer for over 3 years with no problems whatsoever. The old battery was weakening, and when I saw the Philips special promotion on Amazon, I decided it was time for an upgrade.

Here's the lowdown: Most important to folks wondering whether to upgrade- the T980 works EXACTLY like the old one; you can still pop the top off and do the edge trimming without adding any attachments; No. 3 and No. 2 depth on this one are the same as on the old one, etc.

As for noise, my old trimmer had no doubt gotten noisier over the years as the blades dulled or whatever, but with them side by side, the T980 was noticeably QUIETER right out of the box. On the "turbo screamer" setting, it was about even with the old one as far as pure decibels. Speaking of the turbo setting, it's a neat idea, but the vacuum on this one works so much better than the previous one on "normal," in practice I never even switch it to "turbo."

The depth adjustment on the T980 does have a slightly soft "click" right out of the box, but contrary to what I've read, it holds the setting at least as firmly as my old one. Plus, once I used it a few weeks, it loosened up and now "clicks" as definitively as the old one ever did.

If you're using an older Norelco trimmer similar to this one and have been pleased with it, I can recommend the upgrade to the T980 without hesitation.

I ordered the Foil & Cutter Block from Amazon and it arrived quickly. I'm not at all techy so I wondered if I'd have trouble fiddling with tiny screwdrivers etc. No need to worry; you simply pull off the old one, pop on the new one, snap on the new foil cover and start shaving.  I noticed the difference immediately. A much cleaner, quicker shave. If you own a Braun shaver and haven't replaced the cutter in 12+ months, I strongly suggest you do it now.  It's like getting a brand new shaver.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
It's certainly not all that. I've had it a year and a half and the whisker tray already broke. If you empty it every day, it falls apart. If you don't empty it each day, whiskers end up all over the place, including inside the floppy, soft case that has trouble keeping its contents inside. Despite the vacuum action, whiskers collect in every nook and cranny. If you like your grooming aids sanitary, you'll have fun cleaning this thing (and, except the adjustable guide and whisker tray, you can't wash it in water)! Speaking of the adjustable guide, check the setting often, or you'll end up with a surprise...a much closer cut than you expected. The spring-loaded dial adjuster with "digital" read-out doesn't hold its settings as you press harder to get an even cut...it gets worse the more you use it. This is my second Norelco trimmer and the previous one did the same.

Conclusion: I wanted Braun-quality to match their stellar shavers (I'm on my third Braun shaver in twenty years of use), but they discontinued their beard trimmer. While the Norelco is certainly not in the same universe as Braun in quality, neither are they in price. The best thing I can say about this trimmer is that at least it's cheap to buy...a plastic throw-away you have to re-buy every year or two.

UPDATE: I called Norelco before the 2-year warrantee elapsed. Since the whisker tray broke in two pieces and the spring-loaded beard guide is on it's last leg (thin plastic holds in the "springs" and is very fragile), Norelco decided to replace the unit en toto. They said they'd send a new one out and that I should just put the old one back in the same box, apply the PP label they'll include and drop the whole enchilada in the mail. It's nearly two weeks, and I still haven't seen hide nor hair of the new shaver. Only time will tell if Norelco stands behind their product (and their promises).

UPDATE (3/11/09): Well, the replacement unit finally came, after three weeks and four phone callls. Apparently, the thing was on backorder, but nobody at Phillips/Norelco Customer Service bothered to disclose that fact, nor did they provide a tracking number. After my fourth call yesterday, they finally provided me a UPS tracking number which was moot as the package arrived when I returned home from work. So far, so good..at least it works and isn't falling apart. Unfortunately, I have no faith that this one will perform and hold-up any better than the first. At least I won't have to buy another until this one breaks.

Update (7/22/09): Well, only four months after receiving the new replacement trimmer, the whisker tray (aka "hair collection chamber") has fallen apart, just like it did on my original defective trimmer. The difference this time is that Norelco is hanging me out to dry and is refusing to do anything to repair/replace this poorly designed and manufactured product. They claim that because the warantee period is up on the ORIGINAL defective unit, that they can do nothing about the replacement unit they supplied, i.e., they won't stand behind the product even though any other new one has a TWO-Year warrantee. FYI, the original unit was bought from Amazon on 4/7/07. As such, I am downgrading the original 3-star rating to ONE-STAR and changing my review title from "It's Just OK" to reflect my true feelings about this product. As such, I will NEVER buy another Phillips-Norelco product again!

The razor does everything I wanted it to do, and I would purchase it again.

review_title: Norelco blew it with the vac/trimmer/guard interface.  This thing is bad.
review_text:
I'm very disappointed with this trimmer. The thing that made me buy it is the thing that makes this unusable. I speak of the vacuum. It does a good job at keeping the hair out of the sink, but its placement sets the trimmer so far back from the guard that using this trimmer on setting 2 (which is what I always used on my old Norelco T7500 to keep it nice and tight) is the equivalent of setting 7 or so (which is fairly long) on my old trimmer so I am unable to get a nice tight, trim look. Using it on a mustache is useless especially right underneath your nose. It is simply impossible to angle the trimmer in such a way as to trim the hair. I have attempted to use this trimmer twice and both times have had to result to pulling my very old T7500 out of the drawer and using it to get a decent trim.

Even setting this thing on the closest setting (#1) the trimmer still sets back waaaaay too far from the guard to be useful. If you contort you wrists and elbows you can get a fairly close trim on setting 1, but it is a giant pain to have to keep twisting and turning this trimmer around to achieve an even halfway decent trim. This thing is done. I'm shopping around for another brand.

I've been a Norelco user for over 10 years, but they blew it with this one!

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text: At first, people think this is some kinda sex-toy from the future. It's not. It's a beard trimmer. And a pretty good one to boot. If you're like me, you use your beard trimmer when you don't have much time in the morning before you have to take off for work. If you trim with this thing quickly on the 'normal' trimming mode, it'll catch maybe 75% of your hair in the vaccuum. However, when you enter warp speed (turbo mode) this thing is insane. It's really loud and sounds like it might explode, but it works great. It catches roughly 90-95% of hair in the vacuum in turbo mode. It's quite easy to take apart to empty out the little hair-catch-all and clean trimmer attachments or swapping them out (comes with a fine-line trimmer). The height adjustment doesn't seem quite as pronounced as my older Norelco trimmer (meaning you can obviously tell when it clicks into place...this one not so much) but it works nonetheless. I'm happy with it and recommend it to all who read this. Just be sure to take a minute out of your abnormally busy day to read the instructions and precautions and maintenance tips to prolong the life of this thing. That's what they're there for, after all.

product_title: Braun 8000 360 Complete Foil/Cutter Block for Models 8995, 8985, 8975
review_text: There are a lot of posts about this item and the series 3 replacement foil and cutter.  They both work on a variety of Braun shavers, and I have the 8995 model.  I've had it for a decade or more I think and at one time the Series 3 replacement parts worked better than the Series 5, but the last few times I bought the series 3, it just didn't seem to be as good as I remembered.  So, I bought both this time, the series 3 and series 5.  I can tell no difference in the shave with either and they both are worse than what I used to get.  I believe the information about the cutters now having thicker blades is probably the issue.  They cutters for the 2 items appear to be identical and the blades do look thick.  It still does perform really well and if I take the extra time to go over my beard multiple times, it turns out OK.  However, I'm disappointed that I'll probably have to start shopping for a whole new razor soon to get the cut I desire, or just switch back to manual blades.  Hope this helps others.

review_title: Nice shampoo, leaves hair soft and shiny
review_text:
i received this product quickly and in excellent condition.

I bought this product mostly becuase my hair is thinning, and my granddaughter has had some hair loss in the front of her head due to "pulling"her hair back too tightly in barrettes or pony tails. I would say both her hair and my hair, qualified as damaged hair! I figured I would give this product a try. The bottle is completely gone now between both of using it on a daily basis. I always wash my hair twice to remove the styling products, so we go through shampoo rather quickly.

I have honestly noticed no change in my hair thickness or loss. My granddaughters hair has not changed either. We have also stopped pulling her hair back ( which is pretty stressful for me because her bangs are continually in her face, and it drives me crazy). The shampoo does a good job as far as a shampoo goes. I think it leaves our hair soft. Possibly because of the argan oil, but i find this shampoo crazy hard to get completely out. It takes more rinsing than normal. We also haven't not been using a conditioner on my granddaughters hair after using this shampoo because this shampoo leaves her hair very soft and a seperate conditioner is not needed.

As far as a shampoo, this product does the trick. It leaves our hair soft and clean. I can't not tell any change in the thickness or less amount of damagetof our hair since starting this product. Maybe it takes longer than one bottle to see a change, i am not sure. Dont' expect drastic results quickly

review_title: Great battery "training" equals a great experience
review_text:
I've always been a believer in correct battery "training." If your unit (phone, laptop or in this case, shaver) spends every night on the cradle or sucking juice from your home or apartment, odds are that battery will suffer. This suffering will take down its operating ability and cause the charge to last less each time you use it.

I've trained my battery correctly from the start (turn it on and leave it to expend itself when I opened the box and then give it the first good, solid nights charge).

I enjoy the trimmer, love that I can walk around my room and clean my beard without spilling shards of dead cells everywhere.

review_title: it felt better than it would have with any other shampoo
review_text:
I received my purchase of Pure Body Naturals Argan Oil Shampoo over a week ago. I have since used this shampoo 4 times, to truly test the restorative nature of this product.

1. The shampoo comes in a 16oz bottle with a pump dispenser. The shampoo is viscous, and whitish in color. The smell can be a little much for some people. It has a light musky floral scent to it (not sure how to explain the smell), but I did not get the honey scent that other reviewers were talking about.
2. My hair is very thick and curly, so I used about 2 pumps of shampoo each wash. The shampoo lathers very well. There's no heavy residue feeling, and my hair did not feel oily afterwards. Immediately after washing my hair, it felt better than it would have with any other shampoo. I didn't have that hard straw feeling, however it wasn't soft enough for me to not use a conditioner. After conditioning, my hair did have more sheen than usual, and it felt softer. My hair was easy to comb through, and manage.
3. After the 4th wash, my hair has had less breakage, and feels stronger. Overall, I'm happy with the product, apart from the musky floral scent, which is okay.

I did receive this product at a free/discounted rate for my unbiased opinion.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
Pro
Cleans teeth really well through high-frequency oscillations
No rotating parts
Brushhead slightly smaller than manual brushes

Con
May not be sealed as well as it should be
Brushing power decreases as alkaline batteries run down

Discussion
Before I bought this brush, I read the 1- and 2-star reviews complaining about corrosion, and the one reviewer who cautioned against reviewing too soon after purchase. Well, I've been sitting on this review for more than two years. No water intrusion, no corrosion, no need to wait any longer before posting.

After the first use, I was convinced. After the first 2-minute session, my teeth were as clean as from an office cleaning.

The e3000 is intended for teens and preteens, thus it has a slightly smaller brushhead. This makes it less prone to bump against teeth (which IS disconcerting!) and the small size encourages keeping the brush moving. There's no need for 30-second reminder beeps, because you will have touched all surfaces "equally" if you keep it moving the whole time.

The toothbrush uses a strong permanent magnet at the bottom end of the brushhead assembly. This magnet is deflected in a resonant mode by an electromagnet inside the handle, and torsion waves are sent to the head. It's efficient and there are no rotating parts. Regular alkaline batteries last at least a month; my next set will be NiMH rechargeables. The handle is larger and heavier than might be expected, probably to counteract the oscillations of the head. The buzzing is not at all unpleasant, as I also had feared.

Before switching to the Sonicare I had used the Crest SpinBrush for 10 years, and the last straw was when I rinsed off the SpinBrush and black flakes fell out into the sink, and kept coming out as I rinsed and shook. I'd been cleaning out the crud that I could see, but what I hadn't counted on was the stuff that I couldn't see! The openings in the SpinBrush accumulate crud, and since you can't see it, you don't think about it. My breath is not as nasty since I started using the Sonicare and ditched the SpinBrush.

I've applied a small amount of clear silicone seal to the flexible boot which tries (not entirely successfully) to seal the top of the brush. A couple of dabs seals the inside of the top chamber, and the tiny amount of water that gets inside that chamber does no harm. There's only one place for crud to hide, and that's between the torsion shaft and the rubber boot where it emerges from the cap. The brush head gets rinsed off with every use, and there are _no_ crevices in it. After two years, it just might be time for a new brushhead... or maybe not.

Reading through the reviews here on Amazon before purchase was very helpful, and it seems that all those who experienced early failures had water intrusion. The addition of clear silicone to the marginally sealed areas (and if you must, silicone grease to the O-ring) fixes this one design weakness. Make this modification yourself and enjoy it for a long time!

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
I really enjoyed my previous Philips Sonicare rechargeable toothbrush, but after the wand stopped maintaining charge, I decided to replace it w/ this toothbrush. It was a big mistake! My rechargeable toothbrush lasted me several years. This battery-only toothbrush STOPPED WORKING no matter how many different NEW alkaline batteries I put in it.

The Philips batteries lasted me almost a month, and they must be potent, "miracle batteries". When I switched to Rayovac batteries they lasted 1/2 as long. Last week, the toothbrush stopped no matter how many batteries in the pack I put in. I put those batteries into other devices to see if I somehow bought a package of dead batteries. NO.

I now have the world's heaviest, impractical manual toothbrush. I wanted to try being untethered to a recharger, but the rechargeable Sonicares do go at least a week 2x/day before needing a charge. And to repeat, my old rechargeable one lasted me YEARS!!!

DO NOT BUY THIS, DO NOT BUY THIS, DO NOT BUY THIS! There are cheaper comparable battery powered toothbrushes. I wasted $30 in this experiment! I will be buying another rechargeable Sonicare. Because Sonicare DOES really truly clean teeth better than any other toothbrush.

review_text: The bristles on this brush are a bit more rigid than other boar bristle brushes I've owned, but they feel great on my scalp. I imagine after a few washes the smell will fade- but even if it doesn't, it's not transferring to my hair...and since I don't particularly enjoy sniffing my hair brush I'm not too worried about this. I think the thing to remember is that although this cost a little more than a standard drugstore hairbrush- this is a boar bristle brush. You could easily drop $250 on a hand crafted boar bristle brush that is perfect in every way. Or... You can spend $13 on a boar bristle brush that has a faint odor. I've had several brushes in this price range and I assure you, none have been perfect and this one is just as good if not better than the others I've used.

review_title: I have shampooed three times and have to say I am in love with this product
review_text:
I have been using the pure body naturals shampoo for two days, I have shampooed three times and have to say I am in love with this product.
First off, the pump makes dispensing the shampoo easier & it's an effective way to measure out how much liquid you need for one shampoo. I have medium length thicker hair and I use about a pump and a half.
My hair has been damaged over the years with use of many products and dyes. I blow dry and straighten my hair every day & there are times where I use a curling Iron as well. Needless to say my hair can feel quite dead at the ends and very frizzy. There is an element to this shampoo called botanical keratin which helps tame the frizzyness.
The vitamin D and jojoba in the shampoo also have given my hair incredible shine WITHOUT making it appear greasy!
If you have a dry scalp this shampoo will also help you, make sure when you are applying the product you start at your scalp, always give your scalp a good massage, it will stimulate your hair follicles to promote growth and if you have a dry scalp the Argan will help with that!
I would love & can't wait to try the conditioning oils. However I didn't even need to use a conditioner with this product. There are vitamins A, B(1&2), E & D, which I believe are the reason why my hair felt so brand new and de-tangled.
The scent on this product is heavenly. It's like your shower has been overtaken by a spa & you're not only getting an amazing shampoo you are getting the effects mentally of aromatherapy. The vanilla and honey is such a perfect combination. It's so light and airy yet with the steam of a shower it's just enough to make you feel a great start to the day.

I recommend this product 100 percent.
*i received this product discounted for an unbiased reveiw

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Observations from a previous Norelco owner:
review_text: This unit does an entirely adequate job of beard trimming.  The settings match up well with those from earlier units and, once set, there is no slippage from one setting to another.  In my estimation, the "turbo" feature adds no functionality, only noise and increased battery drain.  The new vacuum feature allows for the capture of only about 60-70% of the hair trimmed.  A potential positive is not having to oil the blades, but only if this does not shorten product life.  And as with the last trimmer I owned, the NiCad battery is not replaceable, but it should be.  The battery is the size of a standard AA but it is soldered in place.  Directions are given as to how to remove the battery prior to disposal, but Norelco could have gone the final step and made the battery replaceable.  My old trimmer worked fine; only the battery needed replacing.  But then again, I would guess that product longevity does not rise high on the list of marketing features.

review_title: This unit handled a deployment in May 2008 and is still operational in September 2011
review_text:
I purchased this sonicare unit in May 2008 when I deployed to Afghanistan. I decided to take this item over my regular sonicare foreseeing the problems with electrical current and I didn't want to destroy a $60-75 unit. I paid about $28 for this item. I placed this item in a regular ziplock bag in my ruck sack and used it every night with no issues. It probably got banged it quite a bit. I changed batteries no more than 3x. It served me well. I always wiped it dry and stored it in a the ziplock bag. The bottom did chip and it made it difficult to remove the bottom to replace the batteries but that was the only issue. I have noticed that the inside case is starting to rust but it is still operational and still going with no issues. I will definitely buy again...3 years + and still running.

Update - March 2012 - Unit is still going strong. Use it everyday, change the batteries about every 60 days. Best Sonicare, I've ever owned.

Update - July 2013 and still using it everyday!

Update - July 2017, the handle finally died.

review_text:
This product would be great were it not for several design flaws. This will only stick to a completely flat smooth shower floor or surface. So if you have any kind of raised texture or tile shower floor, forget it. Next, when you do have a smooth place, it will not stay put, it slides when you try to move your foot in and out, even though the suction cups are holding to the floor. Also, the bristles need to be more rigid. Put the most painful thing is that the part that goes over the top of the foot is not padded in any way and will irritate the top of your foot after several uses. And the pumice stone in mine broke almost as soon as I started using it.

The makers of this product have a good idea but need to go back to the drawing board for the reasons above. If they improve it I may try it again later, but I doubt they will re-do it.

review_text: Amazing product! It dose require a uv led light any poly gel will they are not for air drying so I got one from amazon which I included a picture above of the lamp it was only 10 dollars with a few cents with tax. I used color 014 and it looks amazing. I used a thinner layer then recommended to achieve a more natural nail look so my own nail dose peek through but this color is more on the see through side then on the solid color side. It took me a few hours to make the nail just because I chose a time consuming shape but when you use the lamp the actual product dries very well I put the nails under my light on the 120 seconds timer twice to make sure it dries and it did. The base coat is hard to dry but it is not supposed to super dry fast because it acts like a tacky glue unlike the top coat that dries perfect under my lamp in 120s only once. My lamp is 36 w and i would not get anything lower them 36 it will not dry your nails fast at all so only 36 and up. The product is relatively easy to handle and the instructions are easy to understand, I did have to start over twice but once i got the hang of the product everything was easy peasy. Now I can paint over them if I'd like to or leave them as be, I highly recommend for someone who will have patience and time to commit on doing their nails and do the whole process to shape them and paint them if they wanted to.

review_title: It will make your eyelashes grow
review_text: Ok, so I bought this stuff on Amazon but, I have never felt the need to write a review.  I bought this castor oil because I had seen on a youtube where someone swears by putting a drop of castor oil in each eye nightly will ward off cataracts.  So, I thought, what the heck, can't hurt.  I by the way, had been to the eye doctor and he said I showed early signs of cataracts but, nothing to worry about.  I bought one of these bottles and have just now gotten to the bottom of it probably after about 1 year.  I went back to the eye doctor and they said that I had no real signs of any cataracts so, of course I pleased to hear that.  But, that is not why I wanted to write this review.  This stuff makes your eyelashes grow and it also makes the dark circles under your eyes really look a lot better.  I had not noticed my eyelashes growing, it was when I went to the eye doctor that one of the nurses mentioned "you sure do have long eyelashes".  I thought that's strange.  I'm getting older and the last time I checked my eyelashes were starting to get pretty sparse.  So, I went home and looked and sure enough My eye lashes had gotten significantly thicker and longer.  How wild.  I would just put a couple of drops in each eye before bed and the excess I would wipe onto my eyelashes and around my eyes.  Anyway, just want you to know I am 62 and I am a man....  I like my lashes lol...

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I purchased the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer a year and a half ago, so I now have some experience using it. Previously, I've owned two Panasonic trimmers/clippers. Both worked well for a number of years, but eventually suffered from the same problem; the battery lost the ability to hold a charge. When this happened to the first trimmer, I had the battery replaced locally; the replacement battery did not hold a charge as well. When the second failed similarly, I purchased the Norelco.

It was a tough decision to purchase the Norelco instead of another Panasonic. However, the Panasonic models readily available differed from those I had used previously and the Norelco had good reviews and a nice price. I was also a fan of the understated styling and Japanese build of the Panasonic units, so this Norelco was a bit of a departure. I don't recall the exact model number for the Panasonic, but something similar to the ER389K or ER205.

Overall it's served me well for the past year and a half. So, time to share my thoughts. The Norelco is built in China; I haven't noticed any quality problems as of yet.

Positives:
---------

Vacuum is a great improvement. It's much less messy to use this trimmer than those I used in the past.
Power is sufficient, even without the boost.
Battery (still pretty new) holds a charge for a long period of time and recharges relatively quickly.
Comb stays in position (one of the older Panasonic could switch to a lower position under pressure).

Negatives:
---------

It's loud. Bothersome enough for me that I put insert earplugs before using.
The circumference is large; it's a pretty large clipper. I'd prefer something more narrow.
Difficult to replace to guard if you remove it.
Brush falls out of small compartment in case (will be easy to loose it someday).
Possible for pressure to turn on clipper when in soft case; it's happened to me.
Gaudy looks. Why does it need shinny highlights?

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Overall a great trimmer with 1 exception
review_text:
I've been using a Norelco beard trimmer for years. I bought the first T100 which used 2 AA batteries. I've seen the improvements over the years and they have definitely added to how well the products functioned. Right off the bat I'll tell you my exception. This beard trimmer was made in China. That might not matter at all to some and you are entitled to your opinion. But it matters to me and I was slightly disappointed to see that they are not being made in Austria anymore.

Other than that, I am impressed with this trimmer. The turbo vacuum system works great. I have not had to clean my bathroom sink even once. The self-sharpening blades no longer need to be lubricated with oil. Ever though this unit is slightly bigger than my last one (T990)it is not more awkward in my hands. Even the Accu Control System's flexing guide comb is easier to clean than the last one.

I do have to recharge the battery after 2 or 3 uses but it does have a quick charge feature that takes about 1 hour. So I can't really complain about that.

I have not noticed any problems with actually trimming my beard. The 9 lockable length settings have not slipped for me as others have reported (I am currently using a number 4). I have not had any problems with trimming under my nose but I have been used to using a Norelco.

Some trimmers are still made in the USA like Wahl but some of the features in this Norelco I have not found in other trimmers like the vacuum trimmer feature. If this Norelco was still made in Austria I would have given it a 5 star rating. But other than that it is a good beard trimmer and I am enjoying using it.

I will be purchasing this face wash from here on out. The price concerned me but now it just makes sense cause it actually works.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
This beard/head trimmer works as you might hope it would. I had purchased, about 3 years ago, a version of the same trimmer and the battery eventually stopped holding a charge for very long. The old version was an AccuVac T870.

I got another trimmer to replace the old one and it did not have the "Vacuum" part and my wife was not happy about the "little hairs all over" (even after I tried to clean up) -- so I returned that one and looked for a similar one to my old one. That is when I found this one on Amazon and got it.

Great upgrade from the "older one" I had. Every feature I liked from the old one is still there but it has been improved in many ways as well.

The old one took 12 hrs. to charge and this one takes 70 min. The adjustment "clicker" (how close to trim) is firmer, so there is less chance of it moving on you while you trim (making for a shorter than expected cut at times - a risk with the older one).

What totally amazed me is after the first initial charge (following instructions) I let it drain the battery until it indicated it was time for a charge (neat new flashy light thingy does that), but it let me use the trimmer for full trim (I do my head and my beard) about 6 - 7 times before it needed to be re charged.

This one also says it can be used while plugged in. The previous version never said it could be and I used it that way at times which may have compromised the battery for the old one. Now I feel fine using it plugged or unplugged since the instructions say it's OK.

I like it, no more "little hairs all over" -- of course a few leak out here and there, but I usually do a good enough job to keep my wife happy with a little wipe down around the sink, etc. after trimming. I don't even use the "Turbo" switch but perhaps if I did there would be no hairs around at all.

Good Product, get one. I really like mine.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
This is my fourth electric toothbrush (my first Sonicare), and it is the best I have ever owned. For several years I had heard that Sonicare makes a good product; but the price for a toothbrush whose rechargeable batteries couldn't be replaced, made me reluctant to try one. Well, the introduction of this product made my purchase a "no-brainer," and I couldn't be happier with it. My son owns a more expensive version, and the brushing action/speed are identical.

The first week of use was a "ticklish" situation. The ultra-high speed vibration does startle one at first, but after a few days the tickle disappears. I know this is subjective, but the Sonicare makes my mouth does feel cleaner than it has with other toothbrushes.

Some reviewers have complained about the battery compartment not sealing well, but this has not been a problem for me. I don't drool when I brush, so water rarely gets to the battery hatch opposite the business end. I am also amazed that two AA alkaline batteries last almost three months.

Now that I am on my third set of batteries, I know this much for sure. I don't want the expensive version of the Sonicare because it offers no real advantages (just bells and whistles), and I will continue to use this toothbrush until I have to replace it with another Sonicare just like it.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: Small investment that seems worth it
review_text:
I have only been using this toothbrush for a week or so, but already I can tell a marked difference over the conventional brushes I had been using. The plaque removal is much more effortless with this brush and it has a stimulating effect on your gums.

I definitely noticed that the plaque levels have been dramatically reduced, and it does a much more thorough job of getting in tough-to-reach areas, which is a big help for a snaggle-tooth like me.

This brush appears to be the entry-level model, so I think it is worth a try for anyone who is curious. I am doubtful that the more expensive models have that much more to offer. The lack of rechargeable batteries may seem to be a problem with this model, but it also allows for more flexibility and easier replacement, as you can use standard or rechargeable AA batteries.

This one also lacks a detailed timer, but you're buying a toothbrush not a stop watch. This one has what's important: the cleaning power. It runs for 2 minutes, so you know when you've brushed at least that long.

The biggest drawback for the entire Sonicare line seems to be the expense of the replacement heads, but for the price of this brush it's hard to complain too much. Some have also commented on the fragility of this model, but even if I had to buy an entirely new brush every 12-18 months, it would be worth the 30 bucks.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_title: Use a little common sense, folks!
review_text:
I'm sorry but I just don't see how all these people are getting so much water into the battery compartment. Are you submerging the whole thing just to rinse the bristles? Are you spitting up all over it? Are you holding it vertically while you brush/rinse? Are your kids dropping it in the toilet? I've had mine two months and don't have a bit of trouble holding it so the bottom end never gets wet...or the brush end of the head either, for that matter. Just rinse off only the brush itself holding the brush end DOWN. Use a little common sense and take care of your things, for heaven's sake people. It doesn't take a genius.

edit - I've now been using mine once or twice a day for over two years and have had NO problems with water leakage, corrosion, burnouts or breakdowns. Rechargeable AA batteries last up to 6 months and I change the brush/head once a year although I'm not sure it needs it even then, the new bristles feel just the same as the old ones, despite Sonicare's recommended 3-4 month lifespan. At $12-15 a pop I'm sure Sonicare would like you to replace them far more often than really necessary. No special o-rings have been needed. I still can't understand how so many people are reporting water leaks & corrosion unless they just need special supervision to operate any mechanical device.

review_text: I really like this trimmer. I have a full beard, and have been using this trimmer several times a week for the last couple of years or so. Even with that amount of use it holds a charge for a really long time. It has a "turbo" boost setting, but I rarely ever use it; it does a fine job on regular speed. And the vacuum feature works really well. I've been through several other kinds of trimmers over the years, but this one is by far the best. product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text: This brush is awesome. I've had mine for well over a year now and it is still going strong. The other reviewers that speak of the water getting into the battery compartment; they are correct, it is a poorly designed watertight compartment and the rubber o-ring does tend to stop sealing correctly after you change the batteries out one or more times. However, I have come up with a very simple solution: when you first get the toothbrush, remove the end cap and lubricate the o-ring with plumbers grease. Granted, I'm sure alot of you do not have plumbers grease handy and if that is the case, petroleum jelly will work just as well. Make sure you apply liberally to the o-ring all the way around and once you place the cap back on, you can wipe any excess from the outside. Voila, now you have a watertight seal that actually seals.

review_text: Just replaced the foil and cutter block that came with my Braun 8975 electric shaver, after almost 14 months of daily use. The foil in the original had some breaks in it.  As soon as I used the replacement, I noticed how smooth the shaver felt on my face.  The User Guide indicates that the foil/cutter block should be changed after 18 months of use, but I had to do so sooner, perhaps because I press too hard when shaving.  If I want a really close shave, I wind up using my Gillette Fusion Power razor.  No matter how I twist and turn the Braun, I can't seem to get as smooth a result on my neck, as I do on my face.  I do not have to use the razor every day. review_title: I love the Sally Hansen gel nail polish and when I ...
review_text:
I love the Sally Hansen gel nail polish and when I saw this offer from Beauty Brags, I was thrilled with the price even knowing I might get a color or two I wouldn't use often. The product arrived in a very timely way and was wrapped securely. The problem I encountered was that I could see through the wrap that there were only 2 colors I could use. I suspect the bargain is the result of retired and off color paints. I decided to return the package for refund. Unfortunately even though this is a PRIME qualified purchase a return wasn't possible stating 'special handling' was required. This was not indicated in any of the product details. I opened the package and found that two of the bottles were used as evidenced by the wearing off of the type on the bottle cap and less than full containers. In addition there was also a leaking bottle which suggested a third was used as well. See attached photos.

Even though the cost per bottle seems to be a really good deal the shipping of a used product is very disturbing. I have been in communication with Beauty Brags and will revisit my one star score if the customer service is responsive.

product_title: Braun 8000 360 Complete Foil/Cutter Block for Models 8995, 8985, 8975
review_title: Review of 51S foil and cutter for Braun shaver
review_text: Just my .2 cents. I have a Braun model #8985 Series 5. After a year of satisfactory use, I thought I should replace the foil and cutters. I got the one recommended for my shaver, the 51S. I started to use it, and after just a few shaves, I noticed the shaves were not as smooth, and more irritation to my face, than I was getting with my original shaver I had for the past year. Now just after a few shaves, I noticed my cutter was starting to dull. I stuck with it a few more months, and then I started looking for a better cutting block for it. I came on Amazon and read some reviews, and there were many satisfied users of the 30B kit. . I even called Braun, and told them my situation, and asked if I could change over to the 30B, instead of staying with the 51S. NO WAY said the rep, use only the cartridge recommended by Braun, the 51S. Well, I decided otherwise, and went to "Target", and got the 30B replacement foil and cutter. Boy, what a difference. It fits right in, no problem with the foil or the cutter fitting, I even like the foil better than the 51S, seems to roll over my fact smoother. The shaves seem so much better. Now to be honest, I have not used the razor much yet, but I'll get back to you with my thoughts when I do. On my #8985 there is a light that comes on, and it says "change foil", which came on right then when I changed the foil over to the 30B, it lite up. There is a reset button right there, and if you push it with a pen or pencil point, the light goes out after blinking a few times. Maybe the 30B is the way to go, and the 30B is about $15 cheaper than the 51S. I don't know what Braun is doing, but it is not making me buy a new Braun. If I get upset with their shaver, I'm not going to buy a new Braun, I will switch brands. Hate to say this folks, but every manufacturer out there is trying to rip us off today! Regards, TC

review_text:

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I've been using beard trimmers for almost 30 years. This is the best so far. Light, powerful and very smooth. I had the prior version which was good, but not as good. I was surprised how much better this version is. The vacuum is much better, the alternate head for detailed trimming is easy to change back and forth, and the ability to use it plugged in is a big plus. The prior version could only be used in battery mode, and when the batteries wouldn't recharge after a couple years there was nothing to do but tear it open, recycle the batteries and throw the rest away (the batteries were soldered, so I couldn't just replace them). Norelco does recommend running the battery until the charge light comes on, and then recharging it (probably NiCad batteries), but this is no problem if you can use while charging. It also charges quickly and indicates when the charging is finished.
I shopped around, and Amazon's price (when I bought it) was the best around, online or in stores.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Very good product; could be better
review_text:
Lots of plusses: It works and is attractive. The charge is lasting longer than I expected it to, but I have only charged it once.

I did not experience the problems most frequently reported by others. This vacuum works very well; the "turbo" vacuum setting is somewhat louder but does not bother me at all. I have not experienced any of the "down shifting" on the trim height dial due to pressure, as reported by others. I even tried to get it to do this, and mine would not. It has an attractive design, which doesn't matter much to me but is an added plus that makes it more enjoyable to use. It works quite well without the comb housing to clean up the back of my neck between haircuts.

The negatives are minor, but are as follows:

My biggest peeve is that there is a little blue rectangular spring-loaded vaccum mouthpiece right in front of the blade, which sucks the hair into the vaccum. I suppose something like this is necessary from an engineering point of view to get the vaccum to work effectively. However, it seems that this also limits the ability of the hair to get to the blade from that direction, which limits the blade's effectiveness. This is somewhat frustrating, as one has to go over the same areas more than I used to with my old similar model. Also, it makes it hard to use the trimmer with the comb housing off to trim the hair around my ear, which I like to do between haircuts. I can do this if I use my index fingernail to carefully hold down the blue piece. This puts my finger quite close to the blade and makes me a little nervous that I'm going to slice through my finger.

The comb attachment has a spring-loaded base feature. It just seems like something that will break at some point and adds no real functionality.

I agree the case is a bit lame; it could be more rigid or padded, but if you travel with it, just roll it up inside an item of clothing and it will very likely survive just fine. The case should have separate compartments inside for the charger and the trimmer, so the plug doesn't scratch up the trimmer surface.

So I got this thing home to see if it would trim to my preferred length, and no it won't.  I'm liking the stubble look, and about 3-4 days growth looks best on me.  This trimmer only goes down to what represents 7-8 days growth for me.  I have another Panasonic trimmer that works fine, but it has the same issue.  I can take the comb off and cut the stubble down to about one day's length and then let it grow back a few days, but I'm getting really tired of doing that.  I think these manufacturers should specify their trimming lengths so you can do a reasonable buying comparison.

review_title: Two thumbs up... and one hand in the pants.
review_text:
I just bought a Phillips-Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer, and if any of you men or women are looking to give your beard that perpetual 'George Michael-esque' look, search no further. This thing is frikin' sweet.

Works as advertised. Trims fast. Does not pull the hair. Does not need to be used on turbo mode, works great on regular mode. Set the dial to (1), and you'll be in that 1.5mm length mark. Adjustable Guard: Glides smooth. Adjusts quickly. Durable, not flimsy. Removes instantly for a closer trim. Open the compartment door, and brush out the trimmed hairs.

review_title: Great product, does what it says. Smaller pores, smoother skin, less blackheads, and no more full on breakouts
review_text:
Great product, I can visibly see the blackheads have A) become very small, B) have completely disappeared, and it also C) really closed up my large pores and shrunk all of them. My skin has infinitely smoothed out, the acne(white heads, blackheads) have cleared up, and i only get the occasional blemish instead of a full on breakout. At first the deep tingly feeling was a LOT to handle(almost burned a little), so i started with small dime sized amounts and worked my way up to about a quarter size. After only a few days the tingle didn't bother me, i actually LOOK for that deep cleansing tingle to wake me up in the morning, It has become a staple of my daily morning routine.I would advise people with very sensitive skin to perhaps stay away from this, or use very small amounts until you become used to that deep clean feeling.

I also enjoy how the deep cleanse feels, with some products it felt like my skin was peeling off, you know the processed chemical burn you get with most OTC face washes. The dryness was very light, i only noticed my nose was extremely dry, to the point of peeling, when i was using this face wash in conjuction with another product i was using. i have since discontinued with the other product becuase this product does it all. No more rotuines of muliple face washes, toners, and moisturizers.

This is an all-in-one product. I'm buying more when my bottle runs out.

*Side note* I use this in the shower. First thing i do is wet my face, massage the product in and let it stay on as im washing my body, which takes a few minutes, by the time i'm done scrubbing myself i wash everything all at once. It acutally reduces my shower time. Also, on your first several times using this, perhaps cut the time you're suppose to leave it on in half until you get used to it. This only took me 3 or 4 days.

THANKS VI-TAE!

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
Only tried it once so far -- for beard trimming -- but it's very promising.

The "mowing" operation -- getting my beard to an even length -- went extremely well. It was easy, the results were good, and the vacuum did a surprisingly good job of capturing most of the trimmed hair.

The "edging" operation was a little less successful, but I think that new personal care products like this always take a little while to get used to. I'm optimistic that I'll go from liking it to loving it with a little practice.

And the battery ran the trimmer strongly throughout that first session. It's a Ni-Cad battery, so you KNOW it will disappoint you in the end, but:
- The instructions are very clear about how to maximize a Ni-Cad battery's life.
- You can always fall back to corded operation. (That's a smart design.)

review_text: The item pictured is a light or baby blue. The item I got is a very green-blue teal. I've seen pictures others posted with their reviews, and some show the light blue pictured in the listing, and others show the deep teal as I got, so it is not a monitor issue -- we actually are getting two different colors, and apparently you are rolling the dice on which color you will get. Also, a few people wrote in their reviews that the necklace was larger than they expected. I found that strange since it was smaller than I expected. The large "stone" in the pendant is actually plastic, and looks plastic. It looks much cheaper in person than it does in the picture, and being the wrong color, I'm disappointed. But it only cost $5 and it's not worth the hassle to send back for that, so I'm keeping it, although if I could do it all over again, I wouldn't buy it, even for $5. Mine DID come with the earrings and several reviews said they did not get the earrings. It took just under 3 weeks to arrive using standard delivery, which is pretty typical coming from China.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_title: Best beard trimmer that I've ever owned
review_text: I have had this trimmer for about a month now.  It is easily the best beard trimmer of the many that I have owned.  Exceptionally well thought out, simple design is very user friendly.  The vacuum feature, which I was actually pretty skeptical about, works extremely well: there are only a few clippings that fall to the sink or countertop requiring cleanup after trimming.  Cleaning of the trimmer itself is a snap as well.  The depth gauge, blade head and vacuum collection chamber all simply pull off and on smoothly without any difficulty lining them up or anything like that.  I also really like the feature of running off either corded or cordless.  I can use the battery to complete depletion and then finish the trim using the cord.  This will allow me to fully discharge the battery and, hopefully, give it a longer life.  I haven't actually had the battery run down yet -- even I use it 2-3 times per week -- so I'm liking battery life as well.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
I bought this to replace a 5-6 year old similar version that finally gave out on me. The suction action on the old went out after 3 years of use but that may have had to do with a broken guard (my fault not Norelco's). Then the battery finally gave up a few months back.

I researched several alternatives but came back to the PN due to price and my experience with the previous version. The T980 does all I ask it to: I clip my goatee 2x per week and with this usage the battery lasts about a month. I haven't felt the need to use the turbo button so that might be contributing to the good battery life.

The clipper is a little loud but nothing out of the ordinary for a clipper in general. The consistency of the cut length is superb. If this clipper lasts as long as the previous one I'll probably go back to PN and buy whatever the current version is then too.

review_title: Not Good, Nor Is It Decent. Its Bad
review_text:
Good things:
1. Very convenient to use with simple instructions
2. Good battery life

Bad things:
1. Barely removes and does a bad job removing even the blackhead
2.. Can't remove 100% of the spores so I had to use my fingers to remove the deeper ones
3. I had to literally put it on max to effectively use it and even then it doesn't do a good job sucking out the spores and blackheads

Some tips and advice I recommend from what I've learnt:
- Use the big round head on lvl 2 to clear most of the blackheads on the 1st day. You'll clear out most of the blackheads
- Use the small round head on lvl 3 - 5 to get rid of the really stubborn ones on the 2nd day
- Avoid using the big round head on lvl 2 in the area between your eyes and eyebrows. If you do, you will very likely get some red bruising
- Avoid using the big round head on lvl 2 in the area under your nose

Conclusion:
It does a pretty bad job for what its designed for. It certainly is not value for money and you might as well spend your money on some candy instead.

review_title: Lasted only 2 months before it went dull
review_text: Like some other reviewers have mentioned, the original foil and cutter block that came with my 8995 lasted for years. Subsequent replacements lasted a decent time as well, but in the last couple of years it seems like the durability had diminished greatly. This last one only lasted about 2 months before it became so dull that it was virtually unusable, and I don't even have a thick beard or aggressive facial hair growth. product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
i've had this toothbrush for about 4 months now and it still looks brand new. i just checked inside the battery compartment and it's perfect; i've never seen a drop of water inside it any time i've checked. inside where the brush screws on, it looks brand new also. there was a drop or two of water up in the brush shaft, but i think it had been prevented from dripping into the base by a seal*. the base shows no signs of water at all. i had the first version of sonicare toothbrushes that stood vertically on the recharging base and those always had water dripping down into the inside. what's the difference? i read so many reviews of water leaking into the base and the battery compartment i decided to store it vertically, but upside down. that's right: UPSIDE DOWN.

honestly, some of the negative reviews i read had me so scared, i've been pretty obsessive with it. after i brush my teeth, i rinse it well but only to about an inch above the logo. i certainly don't submerge the whole thing. then i vigorously shake off the excess water. then i wipe the outside of the toothbrush with a towel. then i stick it upside down in a toothbrush slot until next use. did i mention i was obsessive? well, anyway, it works like a charm and it's still in perfect condition.

also, i have not used any of the newest models of sonicare, but i'd rate this one as slightly better than the original model, which had a guard around the brush that got in the way. sonicare is the best performing toothbrush i've ever owned by a landslide.

*or more likely because it was upside down.

review_title: My first electric toothbrush - very pleased
review_text:
I've been using this toothbrush for just under a month now, and its benefit to my dental health has already paid for itself tenfold. In fact at the end of this first month, stains on the back of my incisors are completely gone. Can't wait for the second month's results!

I noticed a few reviews remarking upon a faulty seal that led to the destruction of the unit. I haven't had this problem. But then, I've been treating the toothbrush like any other electric appliance by keeping it out of puddles of water.

PROS:
- speed (teeth feel perfectly clean in the allotted two minutes)
- mobility (I'm writing this review from on the road, with my Sonicare packed away in my toiletries bag... and I know if it runs out of juice, I can easily find a couple AAs at a gas station)
- effect (as stated earlier: one month of use has already removed stains on the back of my incisors)
- economical ($25?!? How have you not bought one yet?)

CONS:
- I'm afraid of dropping it; it feels like it would smash into a thousand tiny fragments. If it came with a small travel case, I would've given five stars.

review_title: I'd recommend googling some info about them before buying
review_text:
If you've never used a boar bristle brush before (or any natural type of natural bristle, I suspect), I'd recommend googling some info about them before buying. You don't use them quite the same way you'd use a brush with hard plastic bristles. You definitely want to comb the tangles out of your hair first, for example, and wait until your hair is dry to brush it. (Maybe you're supposed to do those things anyway, for all I know -- I have shorter hair so it's easier for me to use brushes incorrectly without too much damage, but I find plastic brushes more forgiving.)

Because of those things, I'm not sure a boar bristle brush would be great for styling my hair -- but I didn't buy it for that anyway. I bought it more as a type of hair treatment, to get the benefits of boar bristle brushing: distributing oils evenly, improving the condition of the hair, stimulating the scalp, extending time between washes, etc. I have oily hair, but all that oil just build up on my scalp. With this brush, my hair feels and looks much more balanced. I do get some static while brushing, but it settles down quickly.

The brush itself is durable, seems high quality, and has a ton of nice stiff bristles. It feels great on my scalp, and I love being able to help my hair's health without having to slather on a ton of extra treatment products!

review_title: Works great and saves the sink clean up
review_text: I purchased the T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer as a replacement for a Norelco trimmer I had cherished for ten years.  You become attached to the weight and feel of a trimmer and losing an old friend is hard.  Finding a replacement is a risky challenge.  The T980, however, fit the bill.  The weight and feel are comparable, not bulky or heavy.  The fine tuning length control works well, although I recommend you always start a little long and work down.  The shortest setting will leave you with a "very" short stubble.  The best innovation in that ten year time span is the vacuum system for the T980.  No longer do I need to devote an additional 3 minutes to cleaning out the sink and counter after Trimming my beard.  What a blessing.  The one thing I should warn people of is the Trimmer's availability.  I looked all over for the instrument in retail stores as I needed a trimmer post haste for a trip I was taking.  Couldn't find it anywhere.  Lots of lower price point Norelcos, but not the T980.  Amazon was my salvation.  You can save time by forgoing the retail search and buying direct from Amazon.

review_text:
I really wanted to be excited about this product since it was said to be all natural and safe for color treated hair, but I have to say, after my first and only shampoo with this product I was disappointed and frustrated with the condition of my hair.
The disappointment came from the lack luster color I was left with after I shampooed. The shine was completely syeipped from my hair.
The frustration came from trying to comb out my hair after the shampoo. Even with using my professional conditioner for color treated hair, my hair was VERY hard to comb out. It felt as though I hadn't used conditioner at all. I was surprised at how dry my hair felt. Thankfully, I was able to shampoo and condition with my regular products the next day and my hair was back to it's normal healthy state with one shampoo. However, the damage was already done with the shine and color so I will have to touch up my color sooner then I usually do.
To give the shampoo one more chance before reviewing, I had my 11 yr old daughter, who has oily, non-colored hair try it and the results were great. It worked like a clarifying shampoo and left her hair shiny and with great body. She's used the shampoo along with her regular conditioner everyday for the past 5 days and it's really done well with her hair.
So I'm giving the product 2 stars because in my experience, the product does not work well for colored hair, as it states on the bottle, AT ALL.
It would be better advertised as a clarifying shampoo for oily hair.
