review_text:
A little background on my hair: I have curly, mid back length, thin hair. In the last 6 months I have bleached it twice and dyed it about 4 times.

This product would be GREAT for non-damaged hair. It's VERY cleansing, which is great, unless you have damaged hair. I never thought that'd I'd ever be typing that my hair was "too clean" but that's just what it was.

I tried the product for about a week before I decided to leave a review because I thought maybe it was just the one time that it would leave my hair very dry. I went on to try it for about 2 weeks and my hair was EXTREMELY dry. Maybe paired with the matching conditioner (which I didn't buy and I'm not even quite sure if there is one) it would work better. I also think it'd be great for oily hair because of how extremely clean it gets your hair. Unfortunately, my hair is quite damaged, plus, it's curly and it left my hair INCREDIBLY tangled.

Speaking on the smell of the product, it was GREAT! I LOVED the smell! It's a calming scent and it lingers after the shower for quite a while.

The saying "a little goes a long way" wasn't true using this shampoo. I had to pump it about 7-10 times to cover all of my hair, which is about half way down my back and very thin.

Overall: I'd recommend the shampoo for oily hair. But if you have damaged hair, like myself, I wouldn't recommend it. I didn't see my hair as restored as described. I wouldn't purchase it and I'm probably not going to use it again. Again, I didn't use a conditioner with this product to test the quality of the shampoo. So maybe a good conditioner paired with the shampoo would have better results.

product_title: Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer
review_text:
If you're like me, you start out reading the 1 star reviews to find out what's wrong with a product. You will see a lot of alarmist reviews claiming the trimmer shifts length settings without the person knowing. This does happen, but if and only if you have not set the razor attachment on correctly. The razor comes with a beard trimmer and a mustache trimmer, which involves switching attachments. Not setting the attachment on correctly will cause problems. However, if you set it up correctly (not difficult), then no problem occurs.

I like this razor because it has a long lasting battery, which makes the whole process much easier. It cleans easily, and captures a good amount of hair to prevent a giant sink mess. It cuts well, and accurately, although it does take me a while because you have to keep going over the beard to make sure all the hairs are cut to the same length. The mustache trimmer is a great addition as well, because it allows for some precision.

So assuming you can figure out how to work this product correctly, it should do exactly what you need it to!

review_text:
I had a thin black line of tartar (a.k.a. dental calculus) on my back upper molars along my gum line and wanted it to be removed. I brush 2x's within 24 hours, floss, and use a water piker. I initially assumed the tip on the electronic teeth scaler would be extremely sharp and I may accidentally puncture myself, but with care neither was the case for me. Always start on the lowest vibration setting, increasing the vibration after some experience. Additionally, I relied on the YouTube channel "Teeth Talk Girl", a dental hygenist, to provide me videos of how hygienists properly use teeth scalers to remove tartar and plaque and applied them to myself.

In regards to the other tool provided, the manual teeth scaler, please be careful because it is extremely sharp and one can easy hurt/injure your gums. I personally will avoid using this tool.

review_text:
I have been using the Philips Norelco T980 Turbo Vacuum Trimmer for a couple of months. It is the best trimmer I have used. It trims fast and evenly. There has been zero pulling or pinching. The vacuum is helpful, retaining up to 90% of the trimmed hair. It works better than I anticipated. I have not tried the Turbo mode since the regular setting works perfectly so far.

I have not experienced any issues with the beard length setting changing while in use that others have remarked on. Time will tell if parts fatigue plus pressing hard against the face will cause this in the coming months.

I do agree with others about the initial awkwardness of trimming with the comb-like top guide part off. There is a retractable shield in front of the blade that is designed to facillitate trimmed hair going down into the curved waste basket of the vacuum instead of falling in the sink. It would be nice if you could manually lock this shield down when doing fine edge trim. You will get used to it quickly, but the design makes fine trimming more of a blind operation, i.e. you do it by feel more than sight since the shield blocks my view. I use a little more care when fine trimming than with my older model, but the extra seconds aren't too much hassle and the results are fantastic.

The trimmer is of good size but handles easily and with better precision than I initially thought. I'm still on my first charge with about 10 trims and still running strong - no recharge indicator light yet. There is a little brush for cleaning the trimmer that works OK. Philips Norelco recommends cleaning after every trim. Cleaning is a drag but should keep the unit working better longer.

Only thing missing is a recharger/storage stand. You get a travel bag instead.

Bottom line, excellent trimmer. Would recommend to all.

review_title: I am on my 2nd pair (one for both myself and GF).  Same problem with the first pair, water damage as others are describing.
review_text: On the second pair I got smart and analyzed the problem and came up with a simple fix.  Take some vaseline and put a good coat on the rubber seal of the battery bay.  Problem solved!  Stays very dry.  Somehow the water was getting in though the battery door even though its on the bottom and had a rubber seal.  I also lay my brush long ways now vs. vertical.  This way any water doesn't run down.  I have been though at least 10 or more battery changes (I use rechargeable batteries) and at least 3 sets of heads.  I make it at least 3 weeks between charges for two brushings a day and 3 sometimes on weekends.  I owned an original Sonicare and hands down I prefer this model.  I will not even consider the newer fancy ones.  I am going to buy 2 more for future spares. review_text:
Had I read these reviews before buying this, I probably wouldn't have purchased it. I didn't ask if there was a certain MODEL that he recommended, so I assumed I'd have to pay from $40-$150 for a Sonicare. When I saw this one for $30 at Target, I figured I didn't have much to lose.

It turns off automatically after 2 minutes, so I know that I'm brushing my teeth longer. One thing that takes getting used to is NOT removing it while it's going...you'll splatter toothpaste all over yourself! :D Another plus is not having your tummy jiggle like it does with a manual toothbrush!!

The only negative is that it goes thru 2 AA batteries about once a month, but the directions said that it lasts about 60 brushes per battery change and that's about right. I've started using rechargable batteries and have had no problems.

product_title: Philips Sonicare HX3351/02 Xtreme Battery Operated Toothbrush
review_text:
Short version: I have crooked teeth. This brush got out coffee stains that normally required a visit to the dentist.
Longer: Dentists have been recommending Sonicare brushes to me for the last 20 years. The first one I bought, rechargeable, died after a year. So I decided it was too expensive a technology. Then about three years ago, with my dentist harassing me again to use a Sonicare, I found this brush. At the price, it was reasonable even if it only lasted a year, and I didn't have to worry about the charging unit dying.
I've seen the reviews complaining about water leaking in. I think that will depend on usage. I've been using the brush daily for three and a half years, and it only just died. Yes, there was some leakage, but I took care to keep water away from the base. I also used rechargeable batteries, as I find battery failure the biggest problem with rechargeable devices.
I've gone back to a rotary powered brush until I get my new Sonicare, and I miss the Sonicare.

product_title: Easy Feet Foot Cleaner
review_text:
I'm not sure if this just wasn't product tested with the shower actually on or if my product is defective. "suction cup bottom grips to any floor." The suction cups are a great idea for a shower product, but do they work on this one? ABSOLUTELY NOT. I don't know whose idea it was, but I would like to see someone actually cup this thing in the shower, put some soap in there, turn the water on and use it without having to superglue it to the floor.

It absolutely does not stay in one place no matter how light you try to get your foot in there. And I don't know why the pumice stone is there at the heel because you're lucky if you even get your arch in before it starts sliding away. I literally almost fell and broke my ankle the first time I tried to use this because I went into it thinking the suction cups would work. So just be warned, you need something sturdy to hold on to while using this product.

Another problem is the over-the-foot plastic. Why plastic?? If i'm not water skating through the shower on this thing and actually get my foot in all the way, that plastic hits the top of your foot and it's painful. I get the whole car wash appeal it looks like they're going for but that plastic needs to be made out of a softer material.

Since i'm assuming the paying customers are the only product testers in this case, I found it easiest to use one foot to hold the product down by stepping on the pumice stone and one foot doing a combined up/down left/right motion inside the "foot wash" while holding onto the shower rod with both hands. This did crack my pumice stone after 2 uses but at least it wasn't my back.

So as far as likelihood I would recommend this to a friend to use for its intended purpose, I would have to take a hard pass.

review_text: I have had my T980 for a couple weeks now.  It works great.  What used to take me 15 minutes annoying minutes with scissors and the little trimmer attachment on my electric shaver, now takes 2 minutes.  It saves me a lot of time.  It hasn't snagged a hair yet, it cuts clean and true.  It's not only a beard trimmer, but it will edge for you too, so you can get a nice clean neck line or shape up your sideburns. The "turbo" button turns up the speed of the trimmer, but I can't think of a reason why I would ever need to do that.  I like this trimmer.  All of the reviews and articles that I read online pointed me to this particular grooming tool.  I know there are other big names in beard trimmers, but I am glad I chose the T980. review_text: I have tried countless beard trimmers over the last ten years.  I have tried trimmers made specifically for beards, trimmers made for cutting hair and everything in-between.  The major complaints I had with all of these products were that a) they pulled my beard hair and hurt and b) were very messy and not at all precise.  This T980 takes care of all of that.  First of all, it's a well-made product.  All the parts fit cleanly, the charger works well, the directions are great, the packaging is terrific.  Secondly, it is easy to use with a cursory understanding of the instructions.  It took me less than 20 minutes to read the instructions and trim my entire beard.  The two things I like the most about this trimmer would be the vacuum feature (actually gets about 90% or more of the hair) and the smooth feeling it gives you when you use it.  It does not pull, yank or grate your face at all.  It makes beard trimming a very enjoyable experience.

review_title: Doesn't work if left in cold and humid bathroom - Updated! Now it's broken!
review_text:
Updated December 10, 2011. After having the trouble mentioned below for a brief period, now the brush doesn't work at all. Brush did not last long (~3 months). Disappointing reliability. Buyer beware.

____

I've used the toothbrush for a couple of months now. I'm basically happy with the toothbrush and the replaceable batteries are definitely a step in the right direction. My toothbrush stopped working (just one short buzz each time I press the button) and I eventually figured out that if I keep the toothbrush outside of my cold and humid bathroom then the toothbrush works normally again (so far). I guess that condensation inside the toothbrush prevents normal functioning of the toothbrush; once the condensation evaporates then the toothbrush works again (for now). The problem I have is definitely not just low batteries (the toothbrush has the same problem with new batteries).

product_title: GranNaturals Boar Bristle Smoothing Hair Brush for Women and Men - Medium/Soft Bristles - Natural Wooden Large Flat Square Paddle Hairbrush for Fine, Thin, Straight, Long, or Short
review_title: Using a boar bristle brush requires a little research and practice to get it right.
review_text: I've never used a boar bristle brush before. At first I was slightly dismayed at how short the bristles are. I didn't think they would get through my thickish wavy hair...and I was right. But I did a little research and found that they aren't supposed to. This type of brush is not intended for detangling. For that I use a very wide-toothed comb. What this brush is for is to distribute oils from the scalp down the length of the hair. This it does extremely well. The best way do accomplish this with my hair is to separate it into sections, and just brush one section at a time. I can't get over how fantastic my hair feels after brushing in the evening and all the next day. I am attempting to get away from shampooing my hair daily which has left my hair in worse and worse shape the longer it gets. So the brush gets five stars. And so does the service. The brush arrived well packaged and in good shape in a much shorter time than I expected.
